# Session history

Historical record of shipped features and session notes. Not needed at conversation start — only useful for tracing why something was built a certain way.

**2026-09-20 (Mac) — iOS: fixed the "notifications enabling doesn't work" onboarding bug, and reworked the Apple-sign-in "Connect Apple Music" step to also offer Spotify and explain both connections.**

- **User reported no iPhone popup appeared when tapping Continue on the notifications onboarding step.** Root-caused via the existing codebase's own documented pattern for the same permission elsewhere (`MainTabView.openNotificationSettings()`'s comment: "Denied can't be re-prompted in-app — only iOS Settings can change it now"): `StepNotifications.swift` always called `requestAuthorization()` unconditionally with no prior status check, so once notification permission was already `.denied` on a device (from an earlier TestFlight/dev build, or a prior account on the same test device), the call silently re-returned `.denied` with no popup at all — tapping Continue looked broken but was actually a no-op by iOS design.
- **Fix**: `StepNotifications` now checks `PushTokenService.authorizationStatus()` on appear (and again on returning from background, via `scenePhase`). If `.denied`, the screen swaps its copy and button to "Open Settings" (deep-links to `UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`) plus a secondary "Continue without notifications" — the same denied-state treatment already shipped in `MainTabView` and `ConnectedAccountsView`'s Apple Music row, just applied to this screen too. The non-denied path (`.notDetermined`/`.authorized`) is unchanged — same `requestAuthorization()` → `onNext()` flow as before.
- **Second, unrelated ask in the same message: "allow users to skip" the Apple Music screen, add a Spotify connect option to it if not already linked, and add a one-liner explaining what the connections are used for.** The skip part needed a decision, not a guess — the file's own comments document two real App Store rejections (builds 9 and 11, Guideline 5.1.1(iv)) specifically for a "Skip for now" button on this exact screen that let users leave without the system MusicKit dialog ever firing. Asked the user directly via `AskUserQuestion` rather than reintroducing that risk silently; **user chose "reword only"** — keep Continue's existing behavior (fires the real dialog, then advances regardless of Allow/Don't Allow) unchanged, just make the existing bypass (declining the system prompt) more legible via copy.
- **Built** (`StepAppleMusic.swift`, provider == "apple" signups only): retitled "Connect your music." with a one-liner ("We only use your listening history to suggest albums worth rating — never posted or shared anywhere"), added a two-row layout (`connectionRow` helper) — Apple Music (unchanged system-permission flow, `MusicKitService.requestAuthorization()`) and, only when not already linked, Spotify (`supabase.auth.linkIdentity(provider: .spotify, ...)`, the same generic OAuth-link pattern `ConnectedAccountsViewModel` already uses, refreshed on `scenePhase == .active` since linking completes via an external Safari redirect). Each row has its own short "Uses your X to suggest albums" line. Bottom Continue button's behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged from before (still the sole trigger guaranteeing the MusicKit dialog fires); added only a caption below it — "You can always connect these later in Settings." Fixed one icon-styling bug caught before building: initially reused `icon-music`'s `.renderingMode(.template)` tinting for the Spotify icon too, which would have rendered Spotify's full-color mark as a flat monochrome silhouette — every other screen in this app (`AuthView`, `ConnectedAccountsView`) renders `icon-spotify` in its real color with no template mode, so `connectionRow` was changed to take a `@ViewBuilder` icon closure instead of a name+shared-styling string, letting each icon keep its own established treatment.
- **Verified via a clean simulator build** (iPhone 17 Pro, `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**, no new warnings from either changed file. Not verified live: a real device's actual denied-notification-permission state, the Settings deep-link, and a real Spotify OAuth link-from-onboarding round trip all need an actual device/account, not just a clean build.
- **User tested the fix on a real device and reported the popup still didn't appear.** Asked for the actual device state rather than guessing further (`AskUserQuestion`) — confirmed: rebuilt with the fix, and Settings → sillajuku → Notifications already showed **Allow Notifications ON**. This is not a bug: permission was already granted from earlier testing (notification authorization is per-device-app, not per-account — it survives switching to a freshly created account on the same device/simulator), so `requestAuthorization()` correctly no-ops with no popup, same as the `.denied` case fixed above but for the opposite reason. `StepNotifications` only had UI for the `.denied` branch; the already-`.authorized`/`.provisional`/`.ephemeral` case still fell through to the plain "Continue" button that silently did nothing, looking identical to the original bug report. Added a third branch (`isAlreadyGranted`): shows "Notifications are already on for sillajuku on this device" and a plain Continue that calls `onNext()` directly, no pointless re-request. Verified via another clean simulator build — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- **User then asked, for the `.denied` case, whether a custom popup could let the user just tap "Allow" instead of going to Settings.** Explained this isn't possible for any app: once iOS's real permission dialog has been answered, `requestAuthorization()` is permanently blocked from showing it again — a deliberate OS-wide restriction, and a lookalike custom popup wouldn't actually change the real permission (and would itself violate App Review's system-UI-impersonation rules). Made the real path faster instead: `openSettings()` now uses `UIApplication.openNotificationSettingsURLString` (iOS 15.4+, this project targets iOS 26) instead of the generic `openSettingsURLString` — jumps straight to Settings → sillajuku → Notifications (one tap from Allow) rather than the app's general settings page. Verified via clean simulator build — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.

**2026-09-20 (Mac) — Fixed the email-confirmation Universal Link not actually opening the app (Universal Links can't survive Supabase's server-side redirect chain), and simplified the confirmed-page copy.**

- **User confirmed the `/auth/confirmed` page was now live with the right content, but reported the app never opened** — the Universal Link (built in the previous round) simply didn't fire. Diagnosed live rather than guessing: curled the deployed AASA file and found `sillajuku.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` 307-redirects to `www.sillajuku.com` (both are already declared in the app's `associated-domains` entitlement, and the `www` fetch does return the correct up-to-date JSON including `/auth/confirmed` — so the file itself isn't stale or broken).
- **Root-caused to something more fundamental than the AASA redirect, though**: Supabase's email confirmation link doesn't point directly at `sillajuku.com/auth/confirmed` — it points at `<project>.supabase.co/auth/v1/verify`, which verifies the token server-side and then issues its own HTTP redirect to the Site URL. **Universal Links only ever intercept a direct user tap on a matching `https://` link — never a page merely *reached* via a server-side redirect chain**, regardless of how correctly the AASA file and entitlements are configured. This is a known, structural limitation of Universal Links with any magic-link-style auth flow (Supabase, Firebase, etc. all hit this), not something fixable by adjusting the AASA setup.
- **Fixed using the mechanism that doesn't have this restriction**: the app already has a working custom URL scheme, `sillajuku://` (used for `sillajuku://auth/callback` OAuth redirects, `Config.oauthRedirectURL`) — custom schemes aren't subject to the "must be a direct tap" rule, so any page can trigger one regardless of how it was reached. `app/(auth)/auth/confirmed/page.tsx` now auto-triggers `sillajuku://auth/confirmed` on mount (mobile user-agents only) plus a manual tap-fallback link, for browsers that only honor a custom-scheme navigation from a genuine user gesture. `sillajukuApp.swift`'s `.onOpenURL` handler now recognizes this path (`url.host == "auth", url.path == "/confirmed"`) and posts the same `.sjEmailConfirmed` notification the Universal Link path already used — `AuthView`'s banner logic needed no changes. The Universal Link path is left in place too (harmless, and would still work if Supabase's flow ever changes to redirect-free).
- **Second, unrelated ask in the same message: simplify the page's copy.** Was two conditionally-branched sentences (mobile vs. desktop wording, "이메일이 확인됐어요" + a "may have opened automatically" hedge). Replaced with the exact copy requested: "이메일이 확인되었습니다." / "앱으로 돌아가서 가입을 완료해주세요." — dropped the desktop/mobile branching entirely (only the small fallback tap-link is now conditional on nothing extra, it's simply always shown as a low-emphasis safety net).
- **Verified via `tsc --noEmit`** (web, clean) **and a clean iOS simulator build** (`BUILD SUCCEEDED`). Not verified live — needs a real confirmation email tap on a device to confirm the custom scheme actually fires app-side.
- **Committed and pushed** (`62be289`), along with the notifications Settings-shortcut change from the prior round.
- **Follow-up polish request**: the `.denied` state's secondary button read "Continue without notifications," left-aligned under "Open Settings." Renamed to "Skip" and centered (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` on the label). Verified via clean simulator build.

**2026-09-21 (Mac) — Found the real root cause of the "fresh Spotify signup shows only 3 generic rows" bug: the retry loop from the earlier fix was silently defeated for its own gating check.**

- **User signed up fresh with Spotify again (on a build confirmed to include the earlier retry fix) and hit the exact same symptom**: only Popular/New Releases/Trending, no "Your Top Artists," no "Recently Listened" — confirmed via `AskUserQuestion` that Top Artists wasn't showing either (ruling out the separate `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()` catalog-matching path as the cause; this was the same original bug, not a new one).
- **Root-caused precisely this time, not just re-applied the same pattern**: `loadSpotify()`'s `linkedSpotify` gate read `supabase.auth.currentUser?.appMetadata["providers"]` — a purely local, cached snapshot of the SDK's in-memory user object. The bounded retry loop (5 attempts, 600ms apart) re-checked this exact same cached value on every attempt without ever refreshing it, so if that snapshot was stale or incomplete at the moment `loadSpotify()` first ran (plausible right after this account's two-step signup — Spotify's OAuth callback doesn't assert a verified email, so Supabase's own confirmation-email step sits in between the first OAuth attempt and the one that actually establishes a working session), **the retry loop could never self-correct**: it was faithfully retrying everything else in the function (DB fetch, live Spotify token check) while retrying nothing for this one gate, since re-reading a frozen local value 5 times returns the same answer 5 times.
- **Fixed by replacing the local snapshot check with `supabase.auth.userIdentities()`** — a live network call (same one `ConnectedAccountsViewModel` already uses to answer this exact "is provider X linked" question), so every retry attempt now does a genuine, fresh check instead of re-reading stale local state. A real timing race can now actually resolve across the retry window instead of being permanently masked.
- **Verified via a clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**. Not verified live against a real fresh-signup repro (same limitation as the original fix — can't drive a real interactive OAuth flow from this environment).
- **Committed and pushed** (`606c0da`).

**2026-09-21 (Mac) — Same bug recurred on the userIdentities() fix; checked the database directly instead of guessing again, which disproved the leading theory and found the real gap: zero error visibility into why the live Spotify API calls fail.**

- **User re-tested (confirmed on the build containing the `userIdentities()` fix) and got the exact same 3-generic-rows symptom.** Asked to check the database directly rather than propose another theory blind. Wrote a one-off diagnostic script (service-role key, read-only, run from `apps/web/scripts` then deleted) looking up the `junnwest` profile plus the matching `auth.users`/`auth.identities` record.
- **DB evidence disproved the leading theory**: `app_metadata.providers` = `["spotify"]` and `identities` includes a genuine spotify entry — the account really is linked server-side, so neither the original `appMetadata` check nor the `userIdentities()` replacement was ever the actual blocker; both would correctly read this as linked. The real signal: `profiles.spotify_artists`, `spotify_recently_played`, and `spotify_data_updated_at` are all `null` — the live Spotify fetch (Layer 3 of `loadSpotify()`) never once succeeded and wrote back.
- **Root-caused the *next* layer down, and found a real observability bug, not just a logic bug**: `SpotifyService.topArtists()`/`recentlyPlayed()`/`tokenIsLive()` all discarded the actual HTTP response on any failure (`try? URLSession...data(for:)` + `try? decoder.decode(...)`, response status thrown away) — meaning an expired token (401), an insufficient-scope grant (403), a genuine empty result, and a network failure were all completely indistinguishable, both from code reading and from any log/Sentry event. There was no way to know which one was actually happening without adding visibility first.
- **Fixed the visibility gap**: all three functions now check the actual `HTTPURLResponse` status code and call a new `captureSpotifyAPIFailure()` helper (`SpotifyService.swift`) on any non-200 or decode failure, sending the status code + a truncated response body to Sentry (`SentrySDK.capture(message:)`). `validToken()` also now distinguishes and reports "no token saved in UserDefaults at all" as its own event, separate from "token saved but expired/invalid" — previously both were the exact same silent `nil`.
- **Timeline evidence gathered along the way, worth keeping for the next round**: identity created 16:19:39 (first, client-failed-but-server-created attempt), email confirmed 16:19:56, `last_sign_in_at` 16:20:08 (the second, successful Spotify sign-in via the confirmation banner), profile row created 16:20:27 (onboarding `finish()`). All well within a normal timeframe — nothing here points at a timing/race issue, which is part of why the observability gap needed fixing rather than another retry-tuning guess.
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**. This round doesn't claim to have fixed the underlying failure yet — it makes the NEXT test attempt diagnosable instead of another blind guess.
- **Committed and pushed** (`d5f4dee`).
- **User asked how to give me Sentry access; got a read-only auth token set up in `apps/web/.env.local`, and found the iOS app's Sentry project directly via the API** (`sillajuku` org, `apple-ios` project — separate from web's `javascript-nextjs`, confirmed by matching the DSN's numeric project id against `GET /organizations/sillajuku/projects/`).
- **Queried the project's recent issues and found the exact captured event from the Sentry logging just added**: `SpotifyService.recently-played failed: status=200 body={"items":[{"track":{"album":{"album_type":"single",...` — **a genuine 200 response with real Spotify track data, and it STILL failed to decode.** This immediately ruled out every auth/token/scope theory from the prior round: the request succeeded and Spotify returned real data.
- **Root-caused precisely**: this is the classic Swift `Codable` array-decode gotcha — `JSONDecoder` fails an entire `[SpotifyPlayItem]` array the instant ANY single element throws, discarding every other valid item in the same response. Spotify's recently-played history can include edge-case entries (most likely a locally-uploaded file, which doesn't carry a normal catalog album/track shape) that this schema didn't account for — one bad item anywhere in the 50-item response was silently killing the whole batch, explaining "Recently Listened" being empty despite a real, successful, data-filled API response.
- **Fixed with a lenient per-item decoding wrapper** (`SpotifyRecentlyPlayedResponse.LenientPlayItem`, `SpotifyService.swift`): each item is decoded individually inside its own `try?`, so one malformed entry is dropped instead of taking down the other 49. Doesn't require knowing exactly which field/shape was the actual culprit, and stays correct if Spotify includes some other edge case later. `recentlyPlayed()`'s consuming loop updated to unwrap `.value` before the existing nil/podcast/dedup logic (all unchanged).
- **Separately, no equivalent failure was ever captured for `top/artists`** — the likely (not yet confirmed) explanation is Spotify's own `time_range=short_term` constraint: it only returns artists once there's been enough *recent* (~4-week) listening activity, which is a real, legitimate empty result for some accounts, not a bug. Flagged to the user as a possible follow-up (e.g. switching to `medium_term`) rather than changed unilaterally, since it's a product tradeoff (recency vs. data availability), not a confirmed defect.
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**. This is the first fix in this whole thread backed by direct evidence (a real captured failure event) rather than a plausible-sounding theory.
- **Committed and pushed** (`1dd5e01`).
- **User re-tested and got the same 3 rows again.** Re-checked Sentry (24h window) and the DB (fresh account, id `7dfc2a57`, created 17:17:33) — **zero new Spotify-related Sentry events of any kind**, not even the "no token saved"/"token rejected" messages added two rounds ago, and DB columns still null.
- **This absence is itself the finding**: no event from the Layer-3 API calls means the retry loop never reached them at all this time. The one remaining silent gate in `loadSpotify()` (`SearchView.swift`) is `let identities = (try? await supabase.auth.userIdentities()) ?? []` — an error here is completely indistinguishable from a genuine "not linked" empty result, and nothing was ever logged either way. Given the DB proved the account really is linked, this specific call — not the live Spotify API — is now the most likely remaining place still failing.
- **Fixed**: `userIdentities()` is now a real `do/catch`, capturing the actual error to Sentry on the last attempt instead of silently collapsing to `[]`. Also added a `defer`-based summary capture (`"loadSpotify exhausted retries: lastLinkedSpotify=... reachedLayer3=..."`) that fires only if the whole function exits without ever populating `hasSpotifyData` — one event with the complete picture of which gate the retry loop kept failing at, instead of reconstructing it from whichever individual capture did or didn't fire (which the last two rounds of this exact bug both required).
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**. Still doesn't claim the bug is fixed — narrows the search space further and guarantees the next attempt produces a definitive answer either way.
- **Committed and pushed** (`32bcd18`).
- **User re-tested once more; checked Sentry directly this time (per the user's earlier ask to stop needing manual reports) instead of asking them to describe the screen.** Found exactly one new, distinct event: `loadSpotify exhausted retries: lastLinkedSpotify=true reachedLayer3=true`, fired twice a minute apart (two separate `loadSpotify()` invocations — consistent with `refreshSpotifyIfNeeded()` re-triggering on scenePhase-active while `hasSpotifyData` stays false). Critically: **no** capture fired from `validToken()`'s two failure paths, and **no** capture fired from `topArtists()`/`recentlyPlayed()`'s non-200/decode-failure paths either.
- **Reasoned out what this combination actually implies, rather than adding another blind capture**: since `validToken()` never reported failure, it must be returning a genuinely live token; since neither live API call reported an HTTP/decode failure, both calls must be completing with a real 200 and successfully parsing. The only way `hasSpotifyData` still ends up false after that is if both calls are returning **structurally valid, but genuinely empty, results** — for `top/artists` specifically plausible given `time_range=short_term` only returns artists with enough ~4-week-recent listening activity (a real Spotify API constraint, not a bug); for `recently-played`, less obviously explainable without more data.
- **Added the one piece of visibility this reasoning chain was still missing**: both functions now also capture a message when they finish successfully but with zero results — `top/artists` reports "200 OK, 0 items"; `recently-played` reports raw item count AND individually-decoded count (distinguishing "genuinely empty response" from "every item present but failing decode" from "every item decoding but being a podcast/local-file with no usable track+album"), rather than continuing to infer this from the absence of a different kind of event.
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- **Committed and pushed** (`7af8665`).
- **User re-tested (after confirming no delete/recreate needed — just a fresh app launch re-triggers `loadSpotify()`) and got the definitive answer.** Checked Sentry directly: `SpotifyService.top/artists: 200 OK, 0 items (time_range=short_term)` — confirms the short_term theory exactly, matches the user's own "haven't been streaming recently" account. But also: `SpotifyService.recently-played: 200 OK, 0 albums after filtering (raw items=1, individually-decoded=0)` — **there genuinely is one real recently-played item, and it's still failing to decode even under the per-item-lenient wrapper from two rounds ago.** This matters because the user separately confirmed both rows worked correctly before they started deleting/recreating the account, meaning real underlying Spotify data exists — this isn't a legitimate empty state.
- **Root-caused one level deeper than the previous fix reached**: the per-item `LenientPlayItem` wrapper (added `1dd5e01`) only protects the ARRAY from one bad element — it doesn't help when the single item present has a field *inside* its own nested structure (`SpotifyTrack`/`SpotifyAlbum`) that fails to decode, since that failure still propagates and kills that one item's decode entirely. Most likely cause: a locally-uploaded file, which Spotify can represent with fields a normal catalog album always has left null or omitted — `SpotifyAlbum.id` (previously non-optional `String`) being the leading suspect.
- **Fixed by making the whole nested chain lenient, not just guessing the one field**: `SpotifyPlayItem`, `SpotifyTrack`, `SpotifyTrack.SpotifyTrackArtist`, and `SpotifyTrack.SpotifyAlbum` all got custom `init(from:)` implementations that decode every field with `try?` and a safe fallback (empty string/array, or `nil` for `SpotifyAlbum.id` specifically) instead of relying on synthesized `Codable` conformance, which fails the whole nested value the instant any one required field is missing or the wrong type. `recentlyPlayed()`'s consuming loop updated to handle `album.id` now being optional (falls back to a synthetic `"local:\(name)"` id — safe, since this id is only ever used for local dedup/`Identifiable`, never sent back to Spotify or matched against it) and to skip any item whose album name came back empty (nothing worth showing).
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- **Committed and pushed** (`fe5bd7c`). Separately, the `top/artists` empty result confirmed as genuine Spotify behavior (not a bug), flagged to the user rather than changed unilaterally.
- **User re-tested once more; still 3 rows.** Checked Sentry (no new `recently-played` failure event, only another genuine `top/artists: 0 items`) AND the DB directly — **`profiles.spotify_recently_played` now genuinely contains real data**: `[{"name":"MOHO","artistName":"dress",...}]`. The decode fix worked. So the remaining gap had to be somewhere after that, not in `SpotifyService` at all.
- **Found it by checking whether "MOHO" by "dress" actually exists in the catalog** (it does — `search_release_groups('MOHO')` returns "MOHO - EP" by "dress & Raf Sandou", whose `primary_artist_id` matches the "dress" artist row exactly, and `fetchRelease`'s accept-gate substring check (`"dress & raf sandou".contains("dress")`) would pass) — ruling out a catalog-coverage gap and pointing at the resolution step itself never running.

So once real data finally arrived via a background retry — exactly what happens after all the fixes this session made `loadSpotify()` more resilient — nothing ever re-triggered the catalog match to actually use it, short of a full app relaunch or a manual pull-to-refresh the user had no reason to try.
- **Fixed**: both `refreshSpotifyIfNeeded()` and `refreshAppleMusicIfNeeded()` now reset `hasResolvedRecentlyPlayed = false` and call `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()` after their respective `load*()` call, matching the exact pattern `refresh()` already used. Fixed both functions identically (not just the Spotify one under test) since they share the exact same structural gap.

- **Committed and pushed** (`94bc487`). This is the first fix in the whole "3 rows" saga that explains 100% of the observed evidence (real data confirmed in the DB, real catalog match confirmed to exist, and a concrete code path that explains why it never reached the screen) rather than a plausible mechanism.
- **User re-tested and interrupted mid-diagnostic with the actual result: "Recently Listened" DID appear this time — but took 10+ seconds, well after every other section.** "everything should appear uniformly and immediately" — a real, valid UX complaint, not a missing-data bug anymore (the underlying bug from this whole thread is fixed).
- **Root-caused immediately from `load()`'s own existing code comments, no new instrumentation needed this time**: `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()` was sequenced to run strictly AFTER an unrelated one-shot Discovery retry (`if !hasDiscoveryData { await reloadDiscoverySections() }`), which the code's own comment already documented as a real extra network round trip (~6s). `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()` has no actual dependency on Discovery at all — it only needs `recentlyPlayed`/`appleMusicRecentlyPlayed`, both already populated by the FIRST task group earlier in `load()`. The two were sequenced for no real reason beyond code organization, meaning "Recently Listened" was needlessly waiting behind an entirely unrelated retry every time Discovery's first attempt came back empty.
- **Fixed**: the Discovery retry and `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()` now run inside the same `withTaskGroup`, concurrently rather than sequentially — matches the exact same "merge unrelated sequential legs into one wave" pattern `load()` already used once before (see this function's own top comment about the original ~12s-total cold-load fix).
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.

- **User re-tested: still noticeably late, and pushed back specifically on both "uniformly" and "immediately."** Re-examined the fix just made rather than assuming it was sufficient: it only pulled `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()` out of the same task group as the Discovery *retry* — but Discovery's FIRST attempt was still bundled in the SAME task group as `loadSpotify()`/`loadAppleMusic()`, and a `withTaskGroup` only completes once every member finishes. So "Recently Listened" was still gated behind Discovery's first attempt finishing (~6s), even though its own actual dependency (the recently-played lists) was ready seconds earlier — the previous fix addressed the wrong half of the sequencing.
- **Restructured `load()` into two fully independent `async let` chains** instead of task-group-interleaved steps: one for Spotify/Apple Music → `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()` (each step still correctly sequenced after its real dependency), one for Discovery + its retry — with zero coupling between the two chains at all now, not even via a shared task group. "Recently Listened" starts resolving the instant `loadSpotify()`/`loadAppleMusic()` finish, completely independent of how long Discovery takes on either attempt.

On success, swaps in the real `AlbumDetailView(release:)`; on a genuine catalog miss, shows a plain "Not in our catalog yet" message instead of a silent dead end.
  - Added `.navigationDestination(for: RecentlyPlayedDestination.self) { ResolvingAlbumView(item: $0) }` to `SearchView`'s own `NavigationStack` (the only stack this destination is ever pushed from).
  - **Left `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()`'s eager background resolution running unchanged** — still needed to populate the Apple Music row (`appleMusicRecentlyPlayedReleases`), which keeps its original eager-resolution behavior for now since it wasn't part of what was reported broken. Flagged as a likely future follow-up, not changed unilaterally, per the same reasoning as the `time_range` note earlier this round.
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- **Committed and pushed** (`2e88ba1`). This is a real design change (approved by the user via `AskUserQuestion`, not assumed), not another sequencing tweak.
- **User confirmed instant + tappable worked, but flagged two real gaps in the new design**: (1) the loading screen re-appeared on *every* tap of the same item, not just the first, and (2) even a resolved item never gained the rate button ("flower button") or type-label chip every other album card has — it just stayed on the stripped-down preview forever.
- **Root cause: nothing cached a resolution once made.** `ResolvingAlbumView` resolved the release fresh every time it was pushed (its `@State` resets on each new navigation), and `recentlyPlayedPreviewScroll` had no way to know an item had already been resolved even once, so it always rendered the same bare preview card regardless of history.
- **Fixed with a shared cache, fed from both resolution paths**: added `DiscoveryViewModel.resolvedPreviewCache: [String: Release]`, keyed by the Spotify item's id. `resolveCatalogMatches()` (the background eager-resolution helper `resolveRecentlyPlayedIfNeeded()` already calls) changed to return one `Release?` per input item instead of a compacted list, so its caller can `zip` the original items back against their results and populate the cache — meaning most items are often already cached by the time the user even looks at the row, from the background job alone. `ResolvingAlbumView` also writes into the same cache on a successful on-tap resolution (now takes `discoveryVM` directly, not just the raw destination). `recentlyPlayedPreviewScroll` checks the cache per item: if resolved, renders the exact same `DiscoveryAlbumCard`/`NavigationLink(value: release)` every other section uses (rate button, type label, direct navigation, real context menu, zero loading screen) instead of the raw preview — a resolved item now genuinely "acts as all other items," not just once but every time from then on.
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- **Committed and pushed** (`dc62440`).
- **User flagged the row only showing 1 item now, when it used to show more before deleting/recreating the account** — a real question about whether Spotify's raw data itself only has 1 track, or whether something is still silently dropping others. Checked the DB directly: `spotify_recently_played` genuinely only has 1 saved item (`MOHO` by `dress`) — but that alone doesn't answer whether Spotify's API sent back 1 track or several. The existing diagnostic capture (added two rounds ago) only fires when the final result is completely EMPTY, not when it's just suspiciously low but nonzero — no evidence either way for this case.
- **Widened the diagnostic**: `recentlyPlayed()` now captures a Sentry event whenever the final album count is LOWER than the raw item count (`albums.count < rawCount`), not only when it hits zero — covers both silent decode drops and legitimate deduplication (this endpoint returns individual *tracks*, deduped down to unique *albums*; someone who replayed the same single EP several times in a row would legitimately show 1 album from a raw response with several track entries, which isn't a bug). If NO event fires on the next test and the DB still shows exactly 1 saved item, that's conclusive proof Spotify's own response genuinely only contained 1 track right now — not something to fix, just an accurate reflection of very light recent listening (consistent with the user's own earlier "haven't been streaming recently").
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- **Committed and pushed** (`d96c20b`).
- **User re-tested; the widened diagnostic answered the question, but with a different finding than expected**: `SpotifyService.me (liveness check) failed: status=401` — the saved Spotify access token had simply expired (normal, Spotify tokens last ~1 hour; a lot of back-and-forth testing had elapsed). Since `validToken()` had no recovery path for this, `loadSpotify()`'s Layer 3 never even attempted a live fetch this round — the "only 1 item" the user saw was stale cached/DB data from an earlier successful fetch, not proof of the account's current listening history.
- **Real gap identified**: a Spotify refresh token WAS already being captured and saved at sign-in (`sillajukuApp.swift`'s `observeAuth()`, persisted both locally and to `spotify_taste_tokens` for a separate server-side job) — but nothing on the Add tab ever used it. Once the ~1-hour access token expired, the screen just silently stopped refreshing until a full manual disconnect/reconnect.
- **User asked to build the fix rather than just flag it as a known limitation.** Added `SpotifyService.refreshAccessToken()`: POSTs directly to Spotify's own `accounts.spotify.com/api/token` (grant_type=refresh_token), bypassing Supabase entirely — Supabase's `signInWithOAuth`/`session(from:)` only ever handle the initial sign-in exchange, there's no Supabase-side equivalent for refreshing a provider token later. Needs `Config.spotifyClientId` (new — the Spotify app's client_id, not a secret, same value already used web-side in `.env.local`'s `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, safe to embed per Spotify's own PKCE docs, same trust tier as the Supabase anon key/Sentry DSN already in that file). On success, updates the locally-cached access token and (when Spotify rotates it) the refresh token too, in both UserDefaults and the DB-persisted copy. `validToken()` now calls this automatically when `tokenIsLive()` fails, instead of just giving up. Every failure path logged via the same Sentry pattern as the rest of this file.
- **Flagged one real uncertainty to the user rather than claiming certain success**: this refresh call includes only `client_id`, no client secret — correct for a PKCE/public-client Spotify app registration (the standard setup for a Supabase-brokered mobile OAuth flow, and consistent with Sentry's own `pkceGrantCodeExchange` error naming seen earlier this session), but if Spotify's registered app for this integration is instead a confidential client requiring a secret, this specific call will fail with an auth error — which the new logging will make immediately visible on the next live test, rather than silently failing again.
- **Verified via clean simulator build** — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**. NOT YET COMMITTED. NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE — genuinely uncertain until tested against a real expired-token scenario, flagged honestly rather than assumed.

**2026-09-20 (Mac) — iOS: fixed a fresh Spotify signup showing zero Spotify suggestions on the Add tab's first visit, with no way to recover short of reopening the app.**

- **User signed up fresh via Spotify and saw only 3 rows on the Add tab** (Popular/New Releases/Trending — the only sections that don't depend on Spotify data or rating history) — no "Your Top Artists," no "Recently Listened." Investigated via a research agent first: `SearchView.swift`'s `DiscoveryViewModel.loadSpotify()` already has three fallback layers (device cache → DB → a live, on-device Spotify API call gated only on a valid token, no rating history required), so this should work immediately on a same-day signup — not something to wait on the daily refresh cron for. Confirmed this is a real bug, not expected behavior.
- **First suggested a workaround (reopen the app) to see if it was a one-time race** — user correctly rejected this: "the user shouldn't be reopening the app to make this work," and asked for the actual fix, planning to test it live by deleting their account and re-signing up with the same Spotify connection.
- **Root cause, narrowed to two plausible timing races, both addressed by the same fix** (couldn't fully isolate which one without live device logs, so fixed both rather than guessing at one): `loadSpotify()` made exactly one attempt, synchronously, the moment the Add tab first mounted — but right after a *brand-new* signup specifically, two things it depends on can still be settling: the account's `appMetadata["providers"]` identity list (read directly off `supabase.auth.currentUser`, no forced refresh), and the locally-cached Spotify provider token (saved by `sillajukuApp.swift`'s `observeAuth()` on the same auth event, but not guaranteed to have landed in `UserDefaults` before `SearchView`'s own `.task` fires). A single failed check on either gave up permanently, with no automatic retry until the user backgrounded/foregrounded the app or switched tabs.
- **Fix**: wrapped `loadSpotify()`'s entire existing body (unchanged otherwise) in a bounded retry — up to 5 attempts, 600ms apart, ~3s worst case, re-checking both the `providers` list and the token fresh on every attempt rather than trusting a single early read. Only commits to "not linked" / "needs reconnect" UI state on the final attempt, so a fast-settling race never even flashes an incorrect state. Confirmed safe to add this delay: `load()` already runs `loadSpotify()` inside a task group alongside Discovery/Apple Music, and every section renders independently and progressively as its own state lands (established pattern, see that function's own comment) — so in the rare race case, only the Spotify row pops in a couple seconds after the rest of the page, nothing blocks. Left the existing scenePhase/notification-triggered retry (`refreshSpotifyIfNeeded()`) in place unchanged as a second, later safety net.
- **Not yet verified live**: couldn't reproduce a genuine fresh Spotify OAuth signup from this environment without going through a real, interactive sign-in flow (deliberately not attempted, consistent with not creating new accounts/sessions for verification purposes) — confirmed via a clean production build and close reading of both plausible failure points, not a live repro. The user is testing this directly by deleting and recreating their own account.

**2026-09-20 (Mac) — Root-caused the app/website being completely non-functional to the 2026-09-19 Windows session's `sync-ig-artists-to-catalog.ts --all` incident (not the regular catalog pipeline, confirmed idle), fixed the missing throttling, confirmed the database had already self-healed, and gave the user a clear answer on their bigger question: is this a Supabase reliability problem or a workload problem.**

- **User suspected a large data-collection batch on their other device had "depleted something" and paralyzed both the app and website, and asked point-blank whether this meant Supabase itself was unreliable enough to switch database vendors.** Investigated live before answering either question.
  - **Confirmed the outage was real and current, not a stale complaint**: ran the project's own `debug-web-queries.ts`/`pipeline-status.ts` scripts and found nearly every ordinary app query — feed, charts, rankings, search — either timing out (`57014`) or, in one case (`get_charts_pulse`), failing at the connection-pooler level entirely ("upstream connect error... connection timeout" after 79s) with no Postgres response at all. This is a materially different, more severe symptom than a merely-slow query.
  - **Root-caused precisely by pulling the other device's own session notes (via `git pull`, resolving the expected README/SESSIONS.md merge conflicts the same way as prior cross-device syncs — keep both sides' content), not by guessing.** The Windows session's own incident log names the exact cause: `npm run ig:sync-catalog:all` (a new Instagram-watchlist full-catalog backfill, unrelated to the existing MusicBrainz pipeline) ingested only 4 artists (Beyoncé — 102 release-groups/599 recordings — Kendrick Lamar, Ariana Grande, The Weeknd) before hitting "timed out acquiring connection from connection pool" errors, after which a direct test showed the Postgres Data API returning zero response at all while the separate Auth microservice answered normally.
  - **When the user asked to double-check this wasn't actually the regular data-collection pipeline instead**, re-verified rather than re-asserting: the regular pipeline was independently confirmed idle both by the Windows session's own pre-work audit ("hadn't run in 18 days") and by this session's own earlier `pipeline:status` check (16-18 day stale heartbeats) — two separate confirmations agreeing it could not have been the cause, only the new Instagram script was live-observed causing the failure in the same session that ran it.
  - **Answered the underlying "should we switch off Supabase" question directly rather than just fixing the immediate bug**: the diagnosed mechanism (a script ingesting several large-discography artists back-to-back with zero pacing, exhausting the connection pool) is a workload-design problem that would occur against any database vendor under the same access pattern — not evidence Supabase itself is unreliable. Recommended checking the current Supabase compute add-on size (separate from the Pro plan tier) and considering a read replica to isolate future batch/pipeline work from live traffic, rather than migrating vendors.
- **Fixed**: added `INTER_ARTIST_DELAY_MS = 5000` to `sync-ig-artists-to-catalog.ts`, pausing 5s between each artist's ingestion (skipped after the last one) — directly targeting the diagnosed mechanism, matching the Windows session's own prescribed remediation ("inter-artist delays/smaller batches") rather than inventing a different fix. Left `ingestArtist` itself untouched (it's already sequential internally, reused elsewhere, and not what was broken) and didn't add extra machinery (a circuit breaker, batch chunking) beyond the specifically-diagnosed gap, per the standing "don't add complexity beyond what's needed" instruction. `tsc --noEmit` clean (the codebase's one pre-existing error, a missing `playwright` module in `render-ig-poster.ts`, is unrelated — already flagged in the other session's own notes as a needed one-time install on this device).
- **Re-checked live after the fix**: the database had already self-healed on its own (same pattern as the two prior incidents) — a fresh run of the same query check that showed near-universal timeouts earlier now showed everything back to 200-600ms, except `get_silla_leaderboard`, which is the separate, already-diagnosed issue from earlier in this same session (see the Vercel/Silla entry below), unrelated to this incident.
- **Not yet done**: actually resuming the `--all` backfill for the remaining 73 watchlist artists (now safe to attempt given the throttling fix, but not run this round — the user hadn't asked for that yet, only the fix); checking the Supabase dashboard's actual compute tier (recommended to the user, not something this session has credentials to check directly).

- **🐛 Real bug: the user's full review pass was silently lost.** `read_db` came back completely empty — confirmed via a manual test write that the artifact's database had *zero* documents before that write, meaning every toggle the user made had looked like it worked but saved nothing. Root cause: `const db = window.claude && window.claude.db` was evaluated once at top-level script execution, and if the capability attaches even slightly after that line runs, `db` stays permanently falsy for the rest of the page's life with no visible sign beyond an easy-to-miss grey status line. Fixed with a retry loop (~6s of polling before giving up), a loud, impossible-to-miss warning banner replacing the quiet status text, and a localStorage backup as a second line of defense.
- **User then said 110 was still too small — "we need to be as exhaustive as possible."** Rebuilt using the same Wikipedia-category-aggregate technique already proven in the growth-content thread above, this time for real candidate generation rather than a trend metric: queried `ko.wikipedia.org`'s `categorymembers` API directly (via Bash/Node, not guessed category names — verified real category titles first) across 9 real categories (대한민국의 힙합 음악가/그룹, R&B 가수/그룹, 인디 밴드/록 밴드/팝 밴드, 록 밴드, 싱어송라이터), filtered to `ns=0` real articles, deduped → **1,075 real Korean niche artists/groups**, none hand-typed. Combined with the 66 kept mainstream names (Latin/Afrobeats dropped per the user's direction) for **1,140 total candidates**.
- **Second real bug, caught before publishing rather than after:** the candidate id scheme (a slug of the name) let raw Hangul through, but the artifact database's doc-id grammar is ASCII-only (`[A-Za-z0-9_.~:@+-]+`) — every KR-named doc would have rejected with `invalid_argument`. Fixed by switching to a stable FNV-1a hash of the name as the id. Also deliberately avoided array-index ids (the obvious simpler fix) — this repo's own `build-suitability-pool.ts` had already hit this exact problem before and worked around it with a fixed-seed shuffle specifically so re-runs don't scramble ids out from under already-collected labels; a content hash is the more robust version of that same lesson, immune to any future reordering.
- **Republished to the same Artifact URL** (picks persist across versions since the db is keyed by artifact, not file version) — [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/1c05ccf5-4bec-4928-a013-2a3bd8fa9631](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/1c05ccf5-4bec-4928-a013-2a3bd8fa9631). **The user has not yet redone their review against this 1,140-candidate version.**
- **User reported the failure banner was still showing (persistently, not transiently) after the rebuild.** Diagnosed live: confirmed via `action: "list"` that the artifact is owned by the *currently active* account — relevant because the account this session is signed in as had changed earlier in the day (a separate task-notification confirmed this: "Stopped watching 2 artifact watches (the signed-in account changed)"). Since `db` capability requires the viewer to be a signed-in org member, a stale-account browser tab would show exactly this symptom. Pointed the user at checking which account their browser tab is signed into — not yet confirmed resolved.
- **🔴 Separately, and more seriously: ran `npm run ig:sync-catalog:all` (the one-time full-catalog backfill for all 77 watchlist artists) in the background, and it triggered a live Supabase "Data API" Critical alert (5xx errors) mid-run.** The backfill log showed real connection-pool exhaustion errors ("timed out acquiring connection from connection pool," "connection reset before headers") after successfully ingesting only 4 artists (Beyoncé — 102 release-groups/599 recordings, Kendrick Lamar, Ariana Grande, The Weeknd). Stopped the background task immediately once the user reported the alert.
- **Diagnosed precisely rather than guessing, since the user asked "which exact limit is depleted."** A single fresh minimal request to the Data API got **zero response** (`HTTP:000`, full 15-20s timeout) — not an error, nothing at all — even well after the backfill script was killed. The same zero-response result came back from the raw Metrics API (`/customer/v1/privileged/metrics`, authenticated with the existing service-role key as Basic Auth — no new credential needed). But `/auth/v1/health` (a separate microservice, doesn't touch Postgres) answered in 0.5s, and DNS/the bare project root also responded instantly. **Conclusion: the Postgres instance itself is unresponsive, not gracefully rejecting requests** — a materially different and more severe symptom than a merely-full connection pool (which rejects quickly) or the project's prior 2026-09-02 Disk I/O Budget alert, where the Management API had confirmed the DB stayed `ACTIVE_HEALTHY` and responsive throughout that whole incident.
- **User asked directly whether this is the same problem as the 2026-09-02 Disk I/O incident and whether the fix ("stop everything, wait") still applies.** Checked SESSIONS.md rather than answering from memory: that incident's actual fix was more targeted than the user recalled (disabling one specific crash-looping `qc` lane via `--no-qc`, not a blanket stop — other lanes kept running through the fix), and critically the DB was confirmed still responding throughout it. Answered honestly that this time's total non-response is a different, more severe symptom, so "wait it out" alone isn't confirmed to be sufficient this time — recommended checking the dashboard's I/O budget gauge once reachable, and that a database restart may be needed if it's genuinely wedged rather than just credit-depleted.
- **Session ended here — incident NOT confirmed resolved.** Full state captured in README's START HERE checklist (items 10-12): do not run `ig:sync-catalog:all` or anything else DB-heavy next session until the user confirms the database is responding again, and redesign the backfill to throttle between artists (delays, smaller batches) before resuming on the remaining 73 watchlist artists.

**2026-09-20 (Mac) — iOS: fixed a real TestFlight bug — the "Create a username" onboarding step could spin forever with no error if the availability check hung or failed, blocking signup entirely. Investigated a Sentry alert reported alongside it and determined the two were unrelated.**

- **User reported a friend stuck on "Create a username" during TestFlight signup (infinite loading), and separately forwarded a Sentry email for `Auth.AuthError: pkceGrantCodeExchange` around the same time, asking if they were related.** Investigated both via a research agent rather than assuming the user's hypothesis was correct.
  - **Determined the two are almost certainly unrelated, with concrete evidence, not just a hunch.** Apple Sign-In on iOS (`AuthViewModel.signInWithApple()`) uses the native `ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider` + `supabase.auth.signInWithIdToken(...)` — a direct ID-token exchange with no authorization-code/PKCE step at all, so this error class can't originate from that path. The error message's code fragment ("4/0A...") is the distinctive format of a **Google** OAuth authorization code, not Apple's — meaning the Sentry event was very likely an unrelated user's failed Google sign-in, coincidentally close in time. Sentry's "apple-ios" project name is just the iOS app's platform label (confirmed the same `SentrySDK.capture(error:)` call fires generically for any provider's auth failure), not a signal that Apple sign-in specifically was involved.
  - **Found the actual, real bug**: `StepUsername`'s `scheduleCheck()` (`Onboarding/StepGenre.swift`) ran a Supabase `profiles` query with no timeout of its own, and its `catch` block silently set state back to a neutral "unchecked" look (`usernameAvailable = nil`, `isChecking = false`) with zero user-facing error or retry path. A hung request (bad connection, server up but unresponsive) would leave the spinner running indefinitely with `Continue` permanently disabled and no explanation — exactly matching "infinite loading."
- **Fix**: added `checkFailed: Bool` state; the network call is now raced against a 10s manual timeout via `withThrowingTaskGroup` (the Supabase client has no built-in per-call timeout), and any failure — including the timeout — now shows a real inline error ("Couldn't check availability — check your connection.") with a tappable **Retry** button, matching the same inline-error visual style the step already uses for "That username is already taken." Also guarded the final `isChecking = false` against a stale/superseded task (an old check that got cancelled or outlived by a newer one for an edited username) clearing the spinner out from under a still-running newer check — a latent, related race the original code already had, tightened while touching this exact function rather than left to compound with the new timeout path.
- **Not yet done:** could not live-verify the timeout/retry UI against an actual hung or failing network condition (would need to simulate a real network failure, not attempted this round) — confirmed via a clean production build and close reading only; the fix follows standard, well-understood Swift concurrency and SwiftUI patterns (a `withThrowingTaskGroup` timeout race, an existing inline-error visual style already used one line above in the same file), so risk is low, but this is a logic fix without a screenshot to point to. Committing the change.

**2026-09-12 (Windows) — Built a real, data-driven "suitability" filter for Sillajuku's Instagram content pipeline: a two-pathway logistic regression predicting whether an artist/album fits the brand (anti-commercial/underground taste, not mainstream K-pop). Interactive labeling tool, 500-item labeled pool, iterated through 10 model versions, found and fixed 6 real pipeline bugs, and landed on a real unresolved limitation the session ended on.**

- **Interactive labeling tool built first** (design canvas, real cover art embedded as base64 after discovering the Artifact CSP blocks external image hosts) to hand-label a 500-item pool (300 artists + 200 albums, ranked by real Sillajuku rating engagement) as suitable/neutral/not_suitable.
- **Model architecture: two-pathway, not one flat score**, matching the user's own reasoning that an album can be suitable for genuinely different reasons — Path A (mainstream Korean fame AS a real musician, e.g. G-Dragon) and Path B (global significance + music-fan recognition even without Korean fame, e.g. Playboi Carti's *Whole Lotta Red*), combined via `max(pA, pB)` (a probabilistic-OR combination was tried and proven live to wrongly inflate two merely-moderate probabilities into an almost-automatic "yes").
- **6 real bugs found and fixed, each via live diagnosis, not guessing:**
  1. Discogs `master.main_release` pointed to an arbitrary low-engagement pressing, not the most-collected one (Whole Lotta Red: 341 want on the wrong pressing vs. 3,915 on the right one) — fixed by sorting search results by `want+have` directly.
  2. The "timelessness" (one-hit-wonder vs. lasting relevance) formula broke 3 times on real edge cases (a death-spike month, a multi-month viral spike, a degenerate always-1.00 output) before landing on a recency-ratio formula (recent-12-month median ÷ 90th-percentile reference peak) that actually discriminates.
  3. Path A leaked a "keep" for artists with zero real Korean signal at all — fixed by hard-gating Path A on `is_korea=1 OR has_views_ko=1`.
  4. The 50-item holdout scan (30 original + 20 new albums, none seen in training) revealed `country` was silently `null` for every holdout item — the holdout-picker scripts never joined to `artists.country` the way the original 500-item pool builder did. Fixed via `backfill-holdout-country.ts`.
  5. Korean Wikipedia resolution for K-pop holdout items was matching the catalog's English album title directly against Korean article titles (e.g. searching "IVE EMPATHY" when the real article is "엠파시") — failed almost universally. Fixed via `fetch-holdout-korean-artist-fame.ts`, resolving at the artist level using `artists.name_native` the way the original training pipeline did.
  6. Fixing bugs 4-5 made K-pop idol groups score *higher*, not lower — proving the "creative involvement" and genre-tag features meant to separate real musicians from manufactured idol acts don't actually track the user's judgment (cross-tabbed against the real training labels: real singer-songwriters like Heize/Hoody/Colde are mostly labeled not_suitable despite writing their own material).
- **Real new signal researched and verified before building: the Korean Music Awards (한국대중음악상)**, a critic/journalist-panel award explicitly distinct from fan-vote/sales awards (MAMA, Melon Music Awards, Golden Disc, Seoul Music Awards, Circle Chart). Verified live via real Korean Wikipedia categories before committing to the fetch: 5/10 user-confirmed "suitable" Korean artists carried the KMA category vs. 0/9 not-suitable idol-group acts — a real, clean separation. Built `fetch-kma-status.ts`, coded the signal bipolar (+1 win / -1 confirmed non-win / 0 unresolved, not a plain flag — a plain 0/1 flag can only ever reward winners, it can't penalize a confirmed non-winner).
- **Root cause of the remaining K-pop false positives, found by inspecting the training LABELS directly, not more feature engineering:** BIGBANG and BTS are labeled "suitable" as *artists* in the training pool, while their own specific albums are labeled "neutral"/"not_suitable" (BTS's *WINGS* explicitly so) — a real contradiction in the ground truth, since the model shares the same fame features across an artist's artist-row and album-rows. User's resolution: artist-level cultural significance and a specific album's suitability are different questions — raw Korean fame can carry an artist-level judgment but must not be enough on its own to carry an album; an album now needs real corroboration (KMA win, confirmed creative involvement, or >500 Discogs want+have) before Korean-fame features count toward it at all, applied consistently at both training and scoring time (a predict-time-only version of this exact pattern collapsed the model once already, when genre was zeroed only at scoring time in an earlier version).
- **Net effect on the 50-item holdout**, verified by the user against their own real judgment, not just CV metrics: PENTAGON/창모/BEAST correctly flipped to exclude; SHINee/DAY6/2PM/IVE/CHUU all dropped sharply toward the decision boundary (e.g. SHINee 0.78→0.57). Still not resolved: of the current 29 "keep" predictions, the user flagged 22 as false positives.
- **Session ended on a real, unresolved finding, not a fix:** award status, Discogs engagement, and timelessness cannot separate the user's confirmed-correct Western keeps (Kendrick, Doechii, Chance the Rapper, Ed Sheeran) from confirmed-wrong ones (Muse, Vampire Weekend, Coldplay, Killer Mike, Rolling Stones, Wolf Alice) — their numbers overlap or even favor the wrong side. A live check of a "Korean popularity" hypothesis (the user's own theory) also didn't fully hold: Coldplay has *higher* real Korean Wikipedia traffic than Ed Sheeran, and Muse's is comparable to Kendrick's, yet both are still flagged wrong despite real Grammy/Mercury wins and strong Discogs numbers. Session paused here rather than making another blind feature-engineering attempt — see START HERE.
- **All model/data work this session lived in the session scratchpad** (labeling tool, 10 model versions, holdout scoring/viz scripts) except the real data-pipeline scripts, which are in `apps/web/scripts/`: `build-suitability-pool.ts`, `pick-holdout-albums.ts`, `pick-holdout-extra20.ts`, `enrich-and-score-holdout.mjs`, `enrich-extra20.mjs`, `fetch-korean-names.ts`, `resolve-korean-wikipedia.mjs`, `fetch-suitability-covers.ts`, `fetch-awards.mjs`, `fetch-discogs.mjs`, `fetch-creative-involvement.mjs`, `fetch-timelessness.mjs`, `recompute-timelessness.mjs`, `fetch-new-training-cases.mjs`, `fetch-new-training-discogs.mjs`, `backfill-holdout-country.ts`, `fetch-holdout-korean-artist-fame.ts`, `fetch-kma-status.ts`. None of this is wired into the live app yet — it's still in the research/validation phase.

**2026-09-20 (Mac) — Web: diagnosed and fixed a Vercel "function duration spike (9.2x)" alert on the music-rating project, traced to `/api/charts/silla` (~48.6% error rate). Migration applied (user ran it in the Supabase SQL editor); pending redeploy + a post-deploy error-rate check.**

- **User forwarded the raw Vercel alert email, then asked "what's happening here?"** Investigated systematically before touching anything: ruled out a recent deploy (nothing shipped since 2026-09-11) or migration (nothing since 2026-09-01) as the trigger; confirmed the catalog pipeline itself was **not running** (all lane heartbeats ~16-18 days stale, last activity ~2026-09-02/04), ruling it out as the thing actively hammering the database. Ran the project's own `pipeline:status`/`pipeline:verify` health scripts as a live diagnostic anyway (not the scheduled weekly check, an ad hoc one triggered by this investigation) — `pipeline:verify` alone took **several minutes** to complete even with the pipeline fully idle (normally sub-minute or a ~180s hard timeout), a live, current signal that the database itself was under real strain independent of anything actively writing to it. Logged this ad hoc check + its findings to `PIPELINE_CHECKS.md`'s Check log.
- **User then said they didn't understand the Vercel dashboard or the alert email at all ("lack of knowledge in software engineering") and pasted the raw Functions tab table.** Read every row rather than assuming: nearly everything sat at 0% error rate except one glaring outlier — **`/api/charts/silla`: 175 invocations, 48.6% error rate.** Explained the dashboard's columns in plain terms (invocations / total duration / time-since-last-call / error rate) and why a route that fails after running a long time (a timing-out query) is exactly the kind of thing that would drive a *duration* alert even though the visible number of interest was really the error rate.
- **Traced the route to its RPC and read the actual SQL** (`get_silla_leaderboard`, latest definition in `20260706000019_primary_genre_join.sql`) rather than guessing from the route's code comment alone. Found the comment itself already flagged this as a known ~7s query, mitigated only by a 15-minute cache + running under the service role's larger time budget instead of the browser-facing anon role's 3s one.
- **Confirmed live, not just from the comment**: used the project's existing `scripts/debug-web-queries.ts --service`/(default anon) harness plus a one-off probe script (`_tmp_silla_probe.ts`, deleted after) to actually call the RPC. Under the `anon` role it reproduced the exact `57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout` in 3.4s (just over the role's 3s cap, matching the code comment precisely). Under the `service` role (what production actually uses) it succeeded, but with wildly inconsistent timing across repeated identical calls (773ms one run, 4.2s another, 6.8s on a genre-filtered call) — a variance pattern consistent with a query that's genuinely borderline-expensive and whose pass/fail outcome depends on momentary DB load/cache state, not a single clean "this specific filter is slow" story.
- **Root-caused the actual waste, not just "it's a big query"**: `get_silla_leaderboard`'s `user_stats` CTE recomputes `AVG`/`STDDEV`/`COUNT(score)` grouped by `user_id` over the **entire** `ratings` table on **every single call** — and this value is completely unfiltered (doesn't depend on the request's genre/country params at all), so it's pure, exact, repeated waste, not merely "expensive but necessary" work. Confirmed `ratings` has no index on `user_id` at all (checked every migration touching that table) — meaning this CTE has always required a full sequential scan + sort, on every request, since day one; it's only become slow enough to matter as `ratings` has grown.
- **Fix, written as a new migration** (`20260920000000_silla_leaderboard_user_stats_cache.sql`): a new precomputed table `user_score_stats` (one row per user, `mean_score`/`vol`/`n`) plus `refresh_user_score_stats()` to populate it, replacing the live `user_stats` CTE inside `get_silla_leaderboard` with a plain `LEFT JOIN` against the precomputed table. Deliberately did **not** also precompute `global_mean` (the query's other whole-`ratings`-table CTE) — it's a single-pass `AVG` with no `GROUP BY`, not the bottleneck, and switching it to an average-of-per-user-means (the naive way to reuse `user_score_stats` for it too) would silently change the Bayesian prior's math (equal-weight-per-user vs. the original equal-weight-per-rating) — a real behavior change this fix has no business making as a side effect. The migration's final line calls the refresh function immediately so the fix is live the moment it's applied, not just at the next cron tick.
- **New cron** `/api/cron/refresh-silla-stats` (matching `refresh-spotify-taste`'s exact `CRON_SECRET`-gated pattern) calls `refresh_user_score_stats()` on a schedule; wired into `vercel.json` at `0 16 * * *` (daily, an hour before the existing Spotify-taste cron). **Deliberately chosen as daily, not more frequent**, despite the stats being cheap to refresh and the leaderboard's own cache already being 15 minutes — Vercel's Hobby tier has historically restricted cron frequency to once/day, and the *existing* cron already proves daily works on whatever plan this project is on; a schedule that might silently fail to register isn't worth the freshness gain for a statistic (per-user calibration) that moves slowly by nature. Noted in the docs that this can be tightened later if the Vercel plan supports it.
- **Could not apply the migration directly** — this environment's `.env.local` has no `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (checked; only `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, which drives `supabase.rpc()` calls through PostgREST but can't run arbitrary schema-changing SQL). `scripts/db-exec.ts` exists in this repo for exactly this (Management-API SQL execution) but needs that same token. Matches this project's established convention anyway (migrations are hand-applied via the Supabase SQL editor) — told the user directly they need to paste the migration file into the SQL editor and run it, then redeploy so the new cron entry in `vercel.json` takes effect. `tsc --noEmit` clean on the new route file; the migration's SQL itself was unverified against the live schema (couldn't execute it) beyond close structural comparison against the original, still-live function it replaces — until the next line.
- **User ran it and pasted back the SQL editor's result**: a result table headed `refresh_user_score_stats` with one empty cell. Confirmed this is success, not a silent failure — the function's final line calls `SELECT refresh_user_score_stats()`, which returns `void`, so an empty cell is exactly what a correct, error-free run of a void-returning function shows in the SQL editor (an error would have surfaced as a red message instead). Migration is now live in production.
- **Also explained the fix in plain, non-technical terms** per the user's explicit sequencing ask ("first fix then explain in simple terms") — a restaurant-recalculating-its-whole-wine-list-for-one-customer analogy for why the per-user stats CTE was wasteful, and "calculate once a day and save it" for the fix, avoiding SQL/query-plan jargon entirely since the user had directly said they lack a software engineering background.
- **Not yet done**: a redeploy (needed for `vercel.json`'s new cron entry to actually register with Vercel — the migration alone doesn't make that happen); confirming post-redeploy that `/api/charts/silla`'s error rate in the Vercel Functions tab has actually dropped to ~0%, the real proof this is fixed rather than just "should be fixed" from code reasoning.

**2026-09-11 (Mac, continued) — iOS Taste tab redesigned as a full-screen vertical pager (Reels/Shorts-style); found and fixed a non-obvious SwiftUI scroll-alignment bug along the way. In progress, not yet committed.**

- **Why:** the iOS Taste tab was a direct SwiftUI port of web's single long-scroll report. User wanted it redesigned specifically *for* mobile: each section (worlds map, #1 album, stat tiles, years, score, scene, canon, standings, disliked) as its own full-screen page, swiped between like Reels/Shorts, with mobile-native interactions (haptics) instead of a scaled-down desktop layout.

- **Built `TastePagerContainer`** (`apps/ios/sillajuku/sillajuku/Main/TasteView.swift`) — a vertical, one-screen-per-page `ScrollView` using iOS 17's `.scrollTargetBehavior(.paging)`, the same recipe `HomeView`'s existing horizontal feed swiper uses. A trailing dot rail (`PageIndicatorDots`) shows position and jumps to any page via `ScrollViewReader.scrollTo`; a light haptic (`Haptics.light()`, a new small helper — first haptics usage anywhere in this app) fires on every settled page change. `TastePageChrome` replaces the old `ReportSection`/`ReportCard` chrome, stretching the numbered-title + card layout from "one card in a scroll" to "the whole screen." The "Your #1 Album" ring got split out into its own page instead of sharing one with the stat tiles.
- **"You vs the community" (standings) redesigned as a horizontal, one-genre-per-card carousel** (`StandingsCarousel`) instead of a long vertical list of dumbbell rows — the list is unbounded (could be a dozen+ genres) so it doesn't fit one screen as a static block; swiping it sideways is also orthogonal to the pager's vertical swipe, so the two gestures never compete. Added a light haptic per card change, matching the outer pager.
- **Haptics added at every tap-to-reveal point**, not just the pager: `HallOfFameView`'s ring now fires a light haptic on every front-album change (drag, auto-rotate tick, or dot tap all funnel through the same `activeIndex` change); `StatTileView`'s info-icon tooltip toggle and `DumbbellView`'s tap-to-reveal both got `Haptics.selection()`.
- **🐛 Found and root-caused a real SwiftUI bug mid-build, not just shipped the shell blind.** Jumping to a page several screens away (the exact thing tapping a far dot does) landed mid-page — the target's own top already scrolled past, the *next* page's title bleeding in at the bottom — and got worse the farther the jump (barely visible on a 1-2 page hop, roughly a half-page misalignment by the 8th/9th page). Spent real effort ruling out the wrong causes first: confirmed via live testing that it was **not** `LazyVStack` estimation drift (switching to a plain `VStack` didn't change it), **not** the jump API (`scrollPosition` binding vs. `ScrollViewReader.scrollTo` produced byte-identical results), **not** settle timing (4s vs 1s delay before the jump, identical), **not** distance-of-jump specifically (reaching page 8 via 8 discrete sequential adjacent hops landed at the exact same wrong offset as one direct jump), and **not** `RevealSection`'s `.onScrollVisibilityChange` (removing it entirely, no change). The actual cause: a `GeometryReader` sizing each page reports its *safe-area-excluded* size, but `.scrollTargetBehavior(.paging)` was snapping against the view's *full* bounds (this file already had a `.background(...ignoresSafeArea())` in the tree) — a small, constant per-page gap between "declared page height" and "actual snap distance" that compounds linearly with page index. **Fix:** `.ignoresSafeArea()` on the `GeometryReader` itself (not just the background) so it reports the true full bounds, with status-bar/home-indicator clearance re-added manually via the real device safe-area insets (read from the key window, since a `GeometryProxy` on a reader that ignores its own safe area reports ~0 for `.safeAreaInsets`). Confirmed fixed by re-testing the same far jumps (pages 4, 8, 9, 10) that previously showed the bleed — all landed clean.
- **Live-verified in the Simulator, not just `xcodebuild`-clean.** Built a temporary `#if DEBUG` bypass (`MOCK_TASTE`/`MOCK_TASTE_PAGE` env vars read by a mock harness + a fabricated `TasteProfileResponse` with representative data for every section) to screenshot every page without needing a real signed-in account with 25+ ratings — this screen is gated behind that threshold and no test credentials were available. Iterated the bug fix against real screenshots at each step rather than guessing blind. **Fully removed before finishing**: `git diff` on `sillajukuApp.swift` shows zero net changes; `TasteView.swift`'s diff contains no leftover `MOCK_TASTE`/`previewMock`/mock-harness code (grepped to confirm). Re-confirmed the real (non-mock) app still launches cleanly to the normal login screen afterward.
- **Round 2, same session: user reacted to the first pass** ("still doesn't feel optimized to the mobile app's screen") — asked what specifically felt off rather than guessing (`AskUserQuestion`), confirmed it was: too much empty space, and content still read as a "card," not a native screen. Diagnosed correctly from the screenshots already sent: `TastePageChrome` was centering a small `Color.sjSurface`-boxed card (with big flanking `Spacer`s) on an otherwise-empty page — visually a shrunk desktop card, not a full-bleed mobile screen.
  - **Removed the boxed-card chrome entirely.** Content now sits directly on the page's own cream canvas — matching the layering every *other* screen in this app already uses (colorful content directly on `sjCream`, not everything wrapped in a white card) — filling the available height instead of being centered inside dead space bounded by a visible box.
  - **Scaled up every page that read as sparse once un-boxed**, rather than just deleting the box and calling it done: hero's aurora wash now fills the entire screen (was a small rounded-rect card floating in empty space) with much bigger title (24→40pt) and stat (22→28pt) typography; Canon gauge 112→180pt (stroke 9→13pt); HallOfFame cover art 184→208pt; stat tiles gained bigger numbers (19→28pt) and padding; the 12-month activity chart's bars grew 24→52pt max height; the standings carousel's cards grew a genre title (13→22pt), got their own visible white surface panel (a deliberate *smaller* featured card inside the page, not the whole page being one card), and its dumbbell dots/axis ticks grew too.
  - **Fixed a real contrast bug this uncovered**: `StatTileView` and the 12-month-activity panel both filled with `Color.sjCream` — invisible before only because they sat *inside* an outer white card (cream tile on white card = visible layering); removing that outer card would have made them blend straight into the now-cream page.   - **Re-read the whole trigger chain from scratch rather than patching a third time.** `runLoopTransition` was invoked from `Color.clear.onScrollVisibilityChange(threshold: 0.6) { visible in ... }` on the invisible loop-trigger row. This fires as soon as that row crosses 60% visible in the viewport — a purely geometric observation with no awareness of touch state. For a real finger-drag swipe, the invisible row very plausibly crosses 60% visibility *while the finger is still down*, well before release: a swipe has to travel most of a page's height (further still, given round 11's resistant gate requires crossing 82% of a page to even commit) before the user typically lifts their finger.
  - **This means `runLoopTransition` was very often starting the cover/reset sequence mid-gesture, with the drag still live.** The reset's `currentPage = 0; scrollTo(0)`, firing from an async `Task` ~455ms later, would then race against whatever the *same, still-active* drag did in the meantime — additional finger movement, and eventually `LoopGuardedPaging.updateTarget` computing yet another settle target on release, landing wherever that gesture actually ended up, potentially fighting or overwriting the programmatic reset. A single continuous touch that starts before the shield/overlay even exists is never intercepted by anything built in rounds 13 or 16 — a shield or `scrollDisabled` can only block *new* touches, never a gesture already in progress when it appears.

The existing `.onChange(of: currentPage)` handler (previously just a haptic trigger) now checks `new == count` and calls a new `scheduleLoopCheck(proxy:)`, which cancels any pending check and starts a fresh 220ms wait; only if `currentPage` hasn't changed again by the time that wait elapses does `runLoopTransition` actually fire. Every subsequent `currentPage` change (the drag continuing, the gesture ending somewhere else, anything) cancels and restarts the wait, so the real trigger only ever commits once the position has genuinely gone quiet.
  - **Deliberately chosen to not depend on knowing exactly when `currentPage` updates relative to touch-up** — whether `.scrollPosition(id:)` reflects the page continuously during an active drag or only after it settles was never confirmed either way, and couldn't be from this environment. A debounce is correct either way: continuous updates just mean more cancel-and-restart cycles before the quiet period is finally reached, not a different outcome.
