**2026-09-02 (Windows, continued) — a monitor notification caught LIVE data corruption on a real artist ($NOT) minutes after it happened; root-caused, fixed, cleaned up, and while restarting found a second, more serious bug where the new Spotify recency lane was actively degrading production search.**

- **🐛🚨 Data corruption: 28 releases from an unrelated iTunes catalog got falsely attached to the real artist "$NOT"** (a US rapper — legit MB tracks like DRIP, PAIN4REAL, 0%). The monitor flagged titles totally inconsistent with his identity ("Christmas Violin, Vol. 3," "Canon In D," "River Flows in You [Violin & Orchestra]") — recognized this immediately as a wrong-artist match, not a win, and stopped the pipeline before more could land.
- **Root cause: `pickAlbum()` in `itunes-client.ts` had a second-tier fallback that matched on title ALONE, with zero artist verification.** `$NOT`'s own short/generic titles ("SIMPLE," "0%," "DRIP" — exactly the shape of real album titles) collided with an unrelated stock instrumental-covers catalog's identically-named albums, and the fallback accepted the match blind. This function is shared by `discover-itunes-recency.ts`, `mb-gapfill.ts`, `discover-itunes-backfill.ts`, `audit-caa-covers.ts`, and `verify-coverage.ts` — a pre-existing bug (not introduced this session), not scoped to just the recency lane.
- **Fix: added a loose-but-nonzero artist check to the fallback** (`artistLooseMatch` — one name contains the other, or shares a first token — mirroring the proven `titleArtistOk()` guard already used in `backfill-rg-covers-all.ts`), so a title-only collision with an unrelated artist can no longer pass silently. Verified directly against the real scenario: `SIMPLE`/`0%` by `$NOT` now correctly return no match; `DRIP` by `$NOT` still correctly finds the real single.
- **Cleaned up the damage:** deleted the 28 bad `[itunes]` release groups + their `releases` rows (0 user ratings existed on any of them — confirmed before deleting, nothing lost). Audited the blast radius before declaring this done rather than assuming it was isolated: checked all 64 other `[itunes]`-sourced release groups created this session (comparing the RAW iTunes-returned artist name stored on `releases.artist` against our own artist) — **0 further suspects**, including the other artists that appeared in the same notification window (Ungu, Harry Stone, Nino Segarra, Antoon, Nadhif Basalamah, Sillkey — all legitimate, e.g. Antoon's own "Knalprobleem (feat. Milolaathetlukken)"). Also checked `mb-gapfill.ts`'s separate blast radius (it can write a wrong cover/tracklist onto an *existing* legit MB release rather than create a fake one) via the one surviving signal available — raw iTunes track-artist names on `gapfill`-created recordings — across 600 gapfill-checked groups this session: **0 suspects**. Caveat documented, not swept under the rug: the 44 gapfill cover-only fills in this window have no rasw-artist-name trail left to audit retroactively (only `cover_url` was written, no accompanying track data) — can't be fully verified after the fact, though the underlying collision mechanism (a short/generic title) is inherently rare, and this is now the *fixed* code path going forward.
- **🐛🚨 Second, independently-discovered bug found DURING the restart to ship the above fix: the new `recency-spotify` lane (built earlier this session) never actually checked the shared production Spotify circuit breaker before calling Spotify — despite `spotify-circuit.ts` existing specifically to prevent this.** On restart it burst through a batch of 25 artists with zero delay between requests (unlike `itunes-client.ts`, `spotify-client.ts` had no request spacing at all), tripped a real Spotify penalty, and kept calling anyway on every subsequent artist/batch, re-publishing an ever-fresh multi-hour block to the Redis key the **live production web server reads for its own Spotify search fallback** — i.e., this was actively degrading real users' search, confirmed directly (`spotify:rate-limited-until` read back ~18.8h out). Stopped the pipeline again immediately on discovering this.
- **Fix, three parts:** (1) added `REQUEST_DELAY_MS` (300ms + jitter) spacing to every Spotify call in `spotify-client.ts`, mirroring `itunes-client.ts`'s existing `ITUNES_DELAY` — this app's credentials are shared with prod, so bursting them was always going to be risky; (2) `spotifyGet()` now checks the shared circuit (new non-throwing `spotifyCircuitRemainingMs()` in `spotify-circuit.ts`) before every single Spotify call and short-circuits to `null` if it's open — a safety net at the lowest level so no future caller can bypass it; (3) `pipeline.ts`'s `recencySpotifyLoop` also checks the shared circuit BEFORE claiming a batch, not just before each call — necessary because the lane's cursor advances unconditionally per artist, so claiming a batch while blocked would have silently "swept" it (every artist resolving false-negative-fast) and permanently lost that slice of the catalog sweep once the circuit cleared. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Verified live immediately on the next restart:** `pipeline:status` showed `recency-spotify blocked (shared circuit) ... done=0 err=0 «~1125m remaining»` — correctly refusing to touch Spotify or advance its cursor, zero new Spotify calls logged, exactly the intended behavior. The 18.8h block itself is real Spotify-side state and has to expire on its own; nothing to do about that but make sure nothing keeps re-triggering or prolonging it, which is now the case.
- **Restarted the pipeline three times this session** (once for the $NOT fix, once after discovering the Spotify circuit bug mid-restart-verification, all with `--fresh-focus --no-embed --no-qc`) — each time confirmed the other lanes (freshness, gapfill, recency/iTunes, reconcile) carried over cleanly.
- **Lesson for next time a new external-API script lane is added: it needs BOTH a per-request delay (found missing here) AND an explicit shared-circuit check before consuming any cursor/queue state (found missing here too) — the iTunes lane already had the first from day one via `itunes-client.ts`, which is likely why only the Spotify lane (built fresh this session) had this gap.**

- **Restarted the pipeline twice this session for this feature** (once to wire the new lane in, once for the timeout fix) — confirmed each time that freshness/gapfill/`recency`(iTunes)/`qc`(off) all carried over healthy, no lost state.

**2026-09-02 (Windows, continued) — Supabase Disk IO Budget alert arrived mid-monitoring; root-caused and mitigated. Separately, user gave 11 concrete recent-release examples to check "are we collecting new releases" — found and fixed a real coverage gap in the iTunes recency bridge.**

- **The Disk IO alert.** Supabase emailed that project `bside` (mmbptchpetwdievhrdsj) is depleting its Disk IO Budget. Checked project health via the Management API (`ACTIVE_HEALTHY`, DB responding) — Supabase doesn't expose the actual IO-budget percentage through the API, only the dashboard, so the exact severity couldn't be confirmed directly. Went looking for what in the currently-running pipeline could plausibly be a real contributor instead.
- **Root cause: `qc`'s crash-loop was retrying an expensive query far more often than designed.** `qcLoop` runs `integrityCheck()` (a full scan for duplicate names, >1/0-canonical counts across 480k release groups) once per hour by design (`QC_POLL_MS` = 3.6M ms). But it had been timing out and throwing *before* ever reaching that hourly sleep — so the supervisor's standard "crash → wait 30s → restart the whole lane" behavior meant it was actually re-attempting the same costly full-table scan roughly every 30-60 seconds, continuously, since the pipeline restart the day before. That's a lot of wasted, never-succeeding disk IO. **Mitigation: restarted the pipeline with `--no-qc`.** Freshness (done=64, err=0) and gapfill (done=38 covers) carried over cleanly across the restart, no work lost. This is *a* real, clearly wasteful contributor — not provably confirmed as *the* cause, since the exact budget number isn't visible via API.
- **Then: "we also should fix the MB bottleneck... all the releases i mentioned should be collected."** User listed 11 real recent releases (K-hip-hop mostly, plus a few Western ones) to check against the catalog. Wrote a one-off script checking each against both our DB and live MusicBrainz/iTunes directly, rather than guessing:
  - **1 of 11 already collected** (수민/SUMIN — dinnermode).
  - **9 of 11 aren't in MusicBrainz at all**, confirmed via live MB API query — a genuine MB cataloging lag for exactly this class of release (recent/underground/regional), not something re-running our pipeline faster can fix.
  - Of those 9, **4 have artists overdue for a freshness re-poll** (Northfacegawd, SUPERBEE, Fat Joe, Lil Wayne) — moot until MB catches up regardless of re-poll timing. **2 have artists not due for weeks** (rosy, Hukky Shibaseki) — same story. **1 (Jay Worthy) was never actually scheduled for ingestion at all** — "resolved" state, `next_check_at: null`, a separate small gap flagged but not fixed this session. **2 (희대의, kii kii) aren't in our catalog or MB or iTunes** — nothing to do until a source catalogs them.
- **The real, fixable finding: the existing iTunes "recency bridge" (built specifically to work around MB's lag) was hard-scoped to Korean artists only, AND had a data-gap bug even within that scope.** `recencyLoop`'s query did `.eq('country', RECENCY_COUNTRY)` (`RECENCY_COUNTRY='KR'` always) — by design this meant Fat Joe/Lil Wayne/Jay Worthy (Western artists) get zero MB-lag mitigation, full stop. But it also turned out that **SUPERBEE and Rosy Pereira — both genuinely Korean — have `country: null`** in our own artists table (a data gap, not a scope decision), so the exact-match filter silently excluded them too, even though they were supposed to be exactly what this lane exists for.
- **Fix: dropped the country filter entirely, made the sweep catalog-wide.** Checked `itunes-client.ts` first — `searchAlbum`/`fetchDiscography` already try a store-agnostic lookup before falling back to a country-specific one, so this was a straight widening of scope, not a redesign. `scanArtistRecency`'s `country` option now receives each artist's own `country` field (used only as a search-language hint fallback) instead of one fixed constant for the whole batch — this naturally fixes the null-country bug too, since removing the WHERE filter includes those rows regardless of what's in the column. User asked for "both a [the null-country bug] and b [widen scope]" — turned out (b) subsumes (a) once the filter's gone, so one change covers both asks rather than two overlapping patches.
- **Throughput retuned so "catalog-wide" doesn't mean "10x slower."** Old: 5 artists per 30-min cycle, ~12k KR artists → full sweep ~52 days. Bumped to 25 per 10-min cycle; new population is ~68k (whole catalog) → full sweep ~19 days, comparably fast or faster than before despite covering 5.6x more artists. iTunes call volume roughly triples per unit time — judged acceptable against the existing shared 403-cooldown/backoff mechanism (already built for exactly this kind of over-rate scenario), and this was weighed explicitly against the disk-IO concern raised in the same conversation: unlike `qc`'s full-table scans, `recency`'s DB footprint is small indexed per-artist queries, so this widening isn't expected to meaningfully add to *that* problem even though it does add iTunes API load.
- **`tsc --noEmit` clean.** Live verification was attempted (a report-only CLI spot-check against SUPERBEE) but hung on the pre-existing iTunes IP-block issue this codebase has documented before — unrelated to this change, killed after ~3 min rather than block further on an external rate limit outside anyone's control.
- **Restarted the pipeline a second time this session** (`--fresh-focus --no-embed --no-qc`) to pick up the recency code change on top of the qc fix. Confirmed healthy post-restart — but `recency` immediately reported "idle (swept) · 0 ingested," the exact same status it had shown for a long time before this session touched anything. That similarity turned out to matter.
- **🐛 The bigger find: `recency`'s cursor query has been silently broken since the first time it ever wrapped around to empty.** `id` is a `uuid` column; the loop's `.gt('id', after)` with `after = ''` throws Postgres error `22P02 invalid input syntax for type uuid: ""` — NOT "zero rows." The code never checked `error` on that query, so `data` came back `null`, `artists?.length` was `undefined`, and the `if (!artists?.length)` branch read that as "swept the whole set," which re-saves the cursor as `''` and reports `0 ingested`. Every subsequent attempt hits the exact same error the exact same way — **once this lane's cursor ever reaches empty, it is permanently stuck reporting a clean "full sweep done" while doing nothing, forever.** Confirmed directly: ran the identical query standalone and got the 22P02 error back explicitly. This was NOT introduced by tonight's country-scope change — the empty-cursor state is reached at the end of every normal full sweep, so this had likely been silently no-oping for a long stretch of this lane's life, not just during this session.
- **Fix: only apply `.gt('id', after)` when `after` is non-empty, and check the query's `error` instead of trusting `data` alone.** Verified with the exact fixed query standalone: 25 real rows back, including a `country: null` artist (the exact class the earlier scope-fix was also chasing) — confirming this single cursor fix and the scope-widening fix reinforce each other. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Restarted a third time this session with the cursor fix. Immediately, dramatically confirmed live**, not just by a clean typecheck: the very first real batch surfaced genuine gaps MB doesn't have — **Matheus & Kauan (Brazilian sertanejo duo) +8 releases** spanning Oct 2025–Jul 2026, then **DJ CHARI (Japanese) +5 releases** — both non-Korean artists, both proving the catalog-wide widening and the cursor fix work together exactly as intended. This lane had almost certainly been contributing nothing for a meaningful stretch of time before tonight; as of this restart it's demonstrably doing real, valuable work again.
- **One thing to watch, not yet resolved:** `recency` is NOT watchdog-armed the way `ingest`/`freshness` are (`supervise(db, 'recency', recencyLoop)` — no stale-timeout argument) — a single truly-hung `scanArtistRecency` call (network fetch with no response) would have nothing to force a restart. Not observed happening tonight (the first post-fix batch was genuinely slow — 10+ minutes for 25 artists, consistent with real iTunes latency across per-artist store-rotation retries — but kept producing new output the whole time, so it was working, not stuck). Worth adding the same watchdog pattern if a real hang ever shows up.

**2026-08-31 (Windows, continued) — user-reported search bug: "Masta Wu - Father EP doesn't appear." Root-caused, fixed, and APPLIED to prod. One dangerous false start along the way, caught immediately and reverted.**

- **Data was never the problem.** The release group exists, is correctly linked to the Masta Wu artist row, has a cover (filled by the running backfill), and shows up fine both on the artist page (`get_artist_release_groups`) and when searching by title alone ("Father", rank 1) or artist alone ("Masta Wu", rank 4).
- **Real bug: `search_release_groups` (the hybrid search RPC) fuzzy-matches the whole query string against `title` and `artist_display` INDEPENDENTLY — never together.** A combined "artist + title" query — how people naturally search for a specific release — fails both the substring LIKE and the trigram similarity checks: the full phrase isn't a substring of either field alone, and the extra words from the other field dilute the similarity score below threshold on both sides at once. Reproduced live: `"masta wu father"` returned one unrelated result; `"Masta Wu Father EP"` returned zero. Not specific to this release — any combined artist+title query can hit it.
- **⚠ First fix attempt broke search entirely — caught within minutes via my own verification, reverted immediately.** Added a WHERE branch matching against `artist_display || ' ' || title` concatenated. Per this repo's own 2026-07-06 lesson (`20260706000017_search_rg_trgm_indexed.sql`): Postgres can only build a BitmapOr plan when *every* arm of the OR is index-backed, and a concatenated expression has no matching index. Result: every single query — including "Father" alone, previously instant — started seq-scanning all ~413k release_groups and timing out (57014). **Verified this immediately with a follow-up test script rather than assuming the fix worked, caught it in the same turn, and reverted to the known-good function before moving on.**
- **Second, correct fix: never touch the proven-fast single-field OR.** Added a separate candidate source (`combined_matches`, mirroring the existing `genre_matches` CTE's `CROSS JOIN LATERAL` pattern) that only activates for a 2–5 word query: look up each word individually — same index-backed 4-arm shape as the existing single-term search, just parameterized per word — then keep only release groups where every word hit somewhere across title-or-artist (a `GROUP BY id HAVING count(DISTINCT w) >= word_count`). Never computes a new expression over the full table.
- **A second, subtler perf trap caught by `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` before it ever reached the live function twice: short words.** The first cut used a plain `JOIN` (not `LATERAL`), which planned as a full seq scan per word — caught immediately via EXPLAIN, rewritten as `CROSS JOIN LATERAL` (forces the per-row parameterized index probe). Then testing with the actual reported query (`"masta wu father"`) surfaced a second issue: `"wu"` is 2 characters, too short for pg_trgm to extract a full trigram — the GIN index barely filtered, and Postgres had to recheck ~160k rows for that one word alone (~8.6s). Raising the per-word minimum to 3 characters (matching a limit this codebase already documents for single-term search) dropped it to ~120ms for the same query, at the cost of not requiring very short words in the AND-set — an accepted precision/speed trade-off consistent with the rest of this function's fuzzy-match design.
- **Verified thoroughly before calling it done:** all 5 originally-broken/working queries pass (`"Father"` rank 0, `"Masta Wu"` rank 3, `"masta wu father"`/`"Masta Wu Father EP"`/`"Father Masta Wu"` all now find it, no duplicates in the result set); a stress pass across common-word queries (`"love story"`, `"taylor swift love story"`, `"iu through the night"`), a >5-word query (cleanly skips the new branch, 0 results, 59ms), a bare 3-char single word (`"bts"`), and a genre-style query (`"kpop"`) — everything returns in well under a second (57–339ms), nothing regressed.
- **Applied directly to the hosted Supabase project via `scripts/db-exec.ts`** (Management API, no dashboard needed) rather than left as an unapplied file — this project's migrations are otherwise hand-applied via the SQL editor across two devices, so the next session on the other device should still copy `supabase/migrations/20260831000000_search_artist_title_concat_match.sql` there for the tracked-migration history to stay consistent, even though prod already has it live.
- **Confirmed the concurrently-running cover backfill (see entries below) was never disrupted** — `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` doesn't lock the table the way an index build would have; checked the backfill's log kept advancing normally throughout.

**2026-08-21 (Windows) — pipeline ran clean for ~2 days on the claim fix. One earlier conclusion turned out to be wrong and is corrected here.**

- **⚠ Correction to the 08-19 entry below: there is NO unrefreshable "250–800 release-group" band.** That entry (and PIPELINE_CHECKS, and README) claimed a large artist's re-poll could never finish inside the 600s no-MB-activity watchdog, so such artists would fail once a day forever. **Wrong.** All three exemplars have since re-polled successfully: **Ella Fitzgerald (670 RGs) 2026-08-21T10:13** — the artist that was actually livelocking — **Dolly Parton (375) 11:04**, **Erik Satie (267) 2026-08-20T22:20**, each with a clean `next_check_at = last_ingested_at + 1 day`.
- **What actually caused those watchdog kills: environment, not artist size.** They occurred while MusicBrainz was 503-throttling *and* the Supabase client was wedging, which stretched an ordinary re-poll past the watchdog window. A re-poll of an already-ingested artist is mostly idempotent upserts and far cheaper than a cold ingest. **No watchdog change is needed** — the three fixes I'd proposed for it (raise `INGEST_STALE_MS`, count DB writes as activity, lower the freshness size cap) are all solutions to a non-problem.
- **The claim fix is still correct and still necessary**, just for a different reason than stated: it stops an interruption *of any kind* from causing a re-claim loop. Its value is robustness, not rescuing a doomed cohort.
- **Method note worth keeping:** the error came from generalising a rule ("artists >250 RGs can't finish") out of three failures observed during a single degraded window, then writing it into three documents as established fact. The correction came from *testing a prediction* — I said Dolly Parton's re-poll would fail, checked `last_ingested_at`, and it had succeeded. Predictions that can be cheaply checked against the DB should be checked before being documented.
- **`newreleases` steady-state data:** sweep 2 (08-20 04:11Z) `+428 flagged` in ~4 min; sweep 3 (08-21 04:14Z) `+521 flagged` in ~6 min, cumulative 949. Rising as predicted, because the claim fix moves more artists to future `next_check_at` values and thus into eligibility. Not yet a steady state.
- **Two days of run stats:** freshness passed **~2,800 re-polls**; release_groups 479,427 → ~480,600; covers 395,005 → ~396,620. Queue `failed` **unchanged at 8** throughout (unchanged since 07-19).
- **Still unresolved: the `fetch failed` client wedge.** It crashes a lane roughly hourly; the supervisor restarts it, costing the in-flight re-poll and resetting the lane counter (visible as `done` going backwards). Confirmed in the pipeline's own output. Fix offered (per-operation Supabase client, as already applied to the monitoring watch), not applied.
- **`gapfill` is effectively throttled out:** iTunes 403s in a ~2h-cooldown / short-run cycle all day, some runs filling a single cover. Not worth acting on — the Deezer backfill already covered that ground.

**2026-08-19 (Windows) — overnight pipeline run surfaced a SECOND freshness livelock (watchdog-triggered, not exception-triggered); fixed by making the claim a real claim. Cover backfill finished.**

- **The second livelock.** The **ingest watchdog** forces a lane restart on "no MB activity 600s". That timer measures *MusicBrainz calls* — but a large artist's re-poll spends minutes in a **DB-write** phase making none, so a perfectly healthy re-poll is mistaken for a hang. Caught live on **Erik Satie (267 release groups)**: restart every ~11 minutes, `last_ingested_at` frozen at 2026-06-30, `next_check_at` never advanced, zero progress. Same dead end as the first bug, two orders of magnitude slower.
- **Why the first fix missed it:** that one advances `next_check_at` inside `tryFreshness`'s `catch`. A watchdog restart tears the lane down — it is not an exception — so the catch never runs.
- **Fix: `claimDueFreshness` now actually claims.** It was named "claim" but only read. It now stamps `next_check_at` forward at pick time, before `refreshArtist` runs, with a `.lte('next_check_at', now())` lost-update guard so a concurrent pass can't double-claim. Any interruption — watchdog, crash, power cut — can no longer produce a re-claim loop, which is strictly stronger than catching exceptions. The same change removes a **latent head-of-line stall**: an artist with no `musicbrainz` external id previously hit a bare `return null`, blocking every artist behind it forever; it is now claimed and skipped. `tsc --noEmit` clean. **⏳ Needs a pipeline restart to take effect.**
- **General lesson:** "advance the schedule in the error handler" only covers failures that *are* errors. Anything that can interrupt work without throwing — a supervisor, a watchdog, a kill — needs the schedule advanced at **claim** time instead. Worth applying to any future lane that leases work this way.
- **Cover backfill COMPLETE:** 90,596 processed, **30,977 filled (34%)**, 59,619 misses. Null-cover release groups **106,488 → 84,425**; the net (22,063) is below the fill count because freshness keeps ingesting new groups, which start coverless.
- **Investigated and cleared:** freshness re-polls overwrite the backfill's Deezer covers with `coverartarchive` URLs (~2,400 so far, including both Tiffany Day albums I'd fixed by hand). Spot-checked with HEAD requests — all **200 OK**. MusicBrainz has genuinely gained art since the original ingest, so this is an upgrade to the authoritative source, not degradation. Current hosts: CAA 357,515 · Deezer 28,538 · iTunes 6,296.
- **Also:** the monitoring watch wedged overnight (`TypeError: fetch failed` for ~3h). The database was fine throughout — a fresh process connected immediately — so it was the long-lived watch process, not an outage. Restarted.

**2026-08-28/29 (Mac, iOS + web, session 4) — Beta invite-link system: one-time redeem tokens, iOS Universal Link/clipboard handoff, full web onboarding flow (`apps/web/supabase/migrations/20260828000001_beta_redeem_tokens.sql`, `apps/ios/sillajuku/sillajuku/Services/BetaInvite.swift`, `sillajukuApp.swift`, `apps/web/app/beta/[token]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/beta/claim/page.tsx`, `apps/web/components/BetaSwipeFlow.tsx`, `apps/web/app/(main)/onboarding/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association/route.ts`).** User asked how to actually deliver the beta badge/ad-free benefits to hand-picked influencers, landed on a personal one-time link, then wanted the on-open experience to be a real swipeable onboarding (philosophy → word definition → thank-you → sign up) ending in an explicit "claim your benefits" moment rather than a silent grant. Iterated the copy/layout extensively via published HTML Artifacts before writing any real code.

- **Backend** mirrors the existing referral-code system's shape almost exactly (`20260706000006_referral_system.sql`): a `beta_redeem_tokens` table (`token` PK, `redeemed_by`/`redeemed_at` nullable), `generate_beta_tokens(n)` (SQL-editor-only, ungranted — run `SELECT generate_beta_tokens(5);` to mint a batch) generating 12-char confusable-char-excluded tokens, and `redeem_beta_token(p_token)` — `SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path` pinned, atomically claims via `UPDATE ... WHERE redeemed_by IS NULL` (that clause is what actually prevents a double-redeem race) and flips `profiles.is_beta_tester`. **Applied by the user.**
- **Link shape:** `https://sillajuku.com/beta/<token>`, added to the Universal Link allowlist (`apple-app-site-association`) alongside the existing `/i/*` invite path.
- **iOS (`Services/BetaInvite.swift`, new):** `BetaInviteLink` parses the URL; `PendingBetaTokenStore` persists a token in `UserDefaults` until a session exists (mirrors `PendingReferralStore`); `BetaTokenClipboardHandoff` does the once-per-device post-install clipboard pickup (mirrors `ReferralClipboardHandoff`, same `UIPasteboard.detectValues(for: [.probableWebURL])` trick to avoid the "Pasted from X" banner). Wired into `sillajukuApp.swift`'s existing Universal Link handler and `observeAuth()`.
- **Web — the real design decision:** OAuth-only auth (Spotify/Apple/Google, no email/password) means "do you already have an account?" isn't a real branch — the same buttons resolve both cases. So `app/beta/[token]/page.tsx` now detects device type: **mobile** (app not installed, since an installed app would've intercepted the Universal Link before this page ever loaded) gets the existing clipboard-handoff-then-App-Store-redirect treatment, now in Korean; **desktop** renders the new `BetaSwipeFlow` component — 4 pre-auth pages (philosophy quoting the app's actual tagline, a dictionary-style "mélomane / 멜로마니아" definition entry positioning sillajuku's own term for a music enthusiast — a deliberate parallel to "씨네필," which has gone viral in Korean online culture as the term for a film enthusiast — a thank-you page, then real Spotify/Apple/Google sign-in reusing the exact OAuth call + icons from `app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`) ending in a 5th page, `app/beta/claim/page.tsx`, that isn't part of the swipeable pre-auth track since it needs a real session: two benefit rows (rocket badge, shield ad-free) and a "혜택 받기" button that calls `redeem_beta_token` on tap, with an animated checkmark/claimed state — an explicit claim, not a silent grant.
- **Token threading across the OAuth round-trip:** stashed in `localStorage` (`sj_pending_beta_token`) before `signInWithOAuth`, since it has to survive navigating out to the provider and back. An already-onboarded user is routed to `/beta/claim` via `redirectTo`'s `next` param at `/auth/callback`. A **brand-new** account can't be routed there directly — `/auth/callback` always sends a profile-less user to `/onboarding` regardless of `next`, and `redeem_beta_token`'s FK to `profiles` means the RPC can't run until that row exists — so `onboarding/page.tsx`'s `finish()` was given a one-line check: redirect to `/beta/claim` instead of `/` if a pending token is sitting in `localStorage`.

The aside body is a flex column: a fixed header (world/tag title + avg), the **ratings list as the flex-growing scroll region** (`flex-1 min-h-0`), and the recs pinned below (`shrink-0`). **2026-08-26 (Windows, web, session 3b) — YearChart trend now spans the whole range (`components/sj/TasteCharts.tsx` → `YearChart`).** User: "the 5 year trend stops at 2001. make sure it spans through whole range."

- **Diagnosis (reproduced numerically, not guessed).** The path already spanned the full width (last point at viewBox x=100) — the line wasn't truncated. The real cause: over recent years with nothing rated, the 5-year moving average is 0, which mapped to `y = H` (=100), exactly the SVG's bottom edge. There the stroke is clipped by the viewBox edge and hidden behind the chart's `border-b`, so the flat zero-tail is invisible and the trend *looks* like it stops at the last non-empty year (e.g. 2001). Confirmed with a zero-tail series: every tail year computed `y = 100.0`.
- **Fix.** Inset the trend's y-map top and bottom (`TREND_TOP = 4`, `TREND_BOT = 6` viewBox units): `trendY(v) = TREND_TOP + (1 - v/max) * (H - TREND_TOP - TREND_BOT)`. A zero stretch now lands at y≈94 — a few px above the axis, clearly visible — and the peak keeps headroom below the top. The line reads continuously end-to-end. Bars keep their own full-height mapping (unchanged). Verified all mapped y stay within `[0,H]`.

**2026-08-26 (Windows, web, session 3) — "Your library across the years" trend line smoothed + zero-year discontinuities handled (`components/sj/TasteCharts.tsx` → `YearChart`).** User: "make the Your library across the years interpolation smooth and handle discontinuities. (0)"

- **Context.** `YearChart` draws a bar per release-year over a **dense, zero-filled** year series (the API fills every year between first and last with `count: 0`), plus a **5-year centred moving-average** trend line. That trend was rendered as a piecewise-**linear** polyline (`M …L…L…`), so it looked angular, and any smooth spline naively fitted through it would **overshoot below the baseline** at the zero-count years (the "(0)" discontinuities the user pointed at).
- **Fix — a monotone cubic spline.** New module-level `monotonePath(pts)` builds a smooth SVG path using **monotone cubic Hermite interpolation** (Fritsch–Carlson tangents): endpoint tangents take the adjacent secant; interior tangents use the weighted harmonic mean and are **forced flat (0) at local extrema** where the secant sign flips. That makes the interpolant **shape-preserving** — it never overshoots the values it connects — so the trend curve is smooth yet still eases down onto the axis across a run of zero years instead of dipping below it or ringing. The only render change in `YearChart` is `path = monotonePath(trend.map(...))` in place of the old `L`-segment join; the 5-year moving average, bars, era band, ticks, and hover are unchanged.
- **Verified.** `next lint` + `tsc --noEmit` clean (source; the usual stale `.next/types` route-validator noise aside). Numerically checked the spline on a spike-then-zeros series (`[0,1,4,6,3,1,0,0,0,0,2,5,2,0,0]`): the sampled curve stays within `[0, H]` — no below-baseline overshoot at the discontinuities, no above-max overshoot at the peak. **Not yet eyeballed live** (≥25-ratings gate).

**2026-08-26 (Windows, web) — Taste map reconstructed for stability + calm (`components/sj/TasteGraph.tsx`).** The map's idea/visuals were good but it had three UX defects the user called out ("buggy… hovering hides the All worlds ▸ genre button… overall height changing around").

- **Diagnosis.** (1) *Breadcrumb hidden on hover:* `.taste-tile:hover{z-index:30}` lifted the hovered tile above the breadcrumb (which had no z-index), so hovering a top-left tile covered `All worlds ▸ …`. (2) *Height jumps:* the outer grid was `md:items-stretch` and the canvas was `flex-1 min-h-[440px]`, so the map stretched to match the inspector column — and the inspector's height changes with its content (0–10 rated albums + 0–5 recs, varying per world/sub-genre), so every drill-in resized the whole map. (3) *Jittery hover:* the pointer-tracked 3D `rotateX/rotateY` tilt (imperative, per-frame) plus the `.taste-tiles:has(.taste-tile:hover) …` sibling-dimming rule read as buggy/unstable.
- **The rebuild** (data contract, treemap math, drill-down, inspector, legend, i18n keys all unchanged — presentation + interaction only):
  - **Fixed-height stage.** The tile box is now a fixed `h-[430px] sm:h-[520px]`, and the grid is `md:items-start` (not `items-stretch`). The map is the single source of its own height; the inspector sizes itself independently below/beside it. Drilling in never grows/shrinks the map. The `ResizeObserver` now only fires on real viewport resizes (never on a drill-in), which is what removes the jump.
  - **Always-on-top chrome.** The breadcrumb moved into a dedicated `absolute inset-x-0 top-0 z-20` layer (pointer-events gated so only the pill is interactive); the hovered tile lifts to just `z-10`, so it can never overlap the breadcrumb. The legend stays in its footer strip.
  - **Calm hover.** One CSS transform: `.taste-tile:hover .taste-tile-face{transform:translateY(-2px) scale(1.02)}` + a static soft-light sheen that fades in. No imperative JS, no refs, no re-render on pointer move, no `:has()` sibling-dimming. Selecting a sub-genre still dims the others (via a plain `opacity` on the tile), and a `focus-visible` outline was added for keyboard users. Level changes cross-fade via a single `taste-level` scale-in keyframe; the fragile per-tile "grow to fill the canvas" open animation (the `entering`/`enterState` machinery) was removed.
- **Removed:** `OPEN_MS`, `prefersReducedMotion()`, the `entering`/`enterTimer` state + `openWorldTile` timer, `faceRef`/`glowRef` and the `onMove`/`onLeave` handlers, the `enterState` prop.

**2026-08-25 (Mac, research only) — sillajuku passed App Store review, awaiting release. User: "there are a few more improvements i want to make before official launch, but at the same time i want to release it so that my friends have access to it" — does release timing affect the app's long-term App Store discoverability/growth, and what do professionals do?**

- **No code changed this entry — pure research to inform a launch-timing decision.** Three rounds of web research (general ranking-algorithm mechanics, then "new app boost" specifics, then explicit ask for objective numbers).
- **Round 1 — does a slow start permanently hurt future ranking?** No. Apple's developer forums explicitly call "day-1 downloads determine your ceiling forever" an outdated myth; ranking is recalculated on rolling signals (retention, engagement, rating quality), not a fixed launch-day snapshot. The one real mechanism is the "new app boost" — a temporary organic-search visibility bump, not a permanent gate.
- **Round 2 — how large/long is the boost?** Not officially disclosed. Consistent pattern across ASO sources: core window is **~7 days** post-launch (one source: the specific title-keyword auto-suggestion boost lasts ~5 days), broader organic-ranking uplift sometimes cited up to a few weeks. It's a one-time, per-country effect (doesn't retrigger on updates or later re-marketing). It only matters for organic keyword *search* discovery — irrelevant to friends installing via a direct link.
- **Round 3 — user explicitly asked for objective/numeric answers to 3 questions; answered honestly where data doesn't exist rather than inventing precision:**
  1. *Odds of success if the boost is captured* — no study isolates this as a variable at all. Reported the unconditional base rate instead (GoPractice data study, success = $100K+ cumulative revenue in 12mo): **~0.4% of new apps** succeed by that bar today (down from 0.6-0.7% in 2018); **2.78%** for games vs **0.57%** non-gaming. Broader/looser bars: ~0.5% "successful" per Zippia/Fyresite, 68% of apps never cross 1,000 downloads (Business of Apps/Statista).
  2. *How much harder if the boost is missed* — also not quantified anywhere. Directionally supported (not proven) by the same rolling-signal argument from round 1: the $100K/12mo outcome tracks a full year of retention/monetization, not launch week.
  3. *Professional launch playbook* — real data here: soft launch to a small controlled cohort (industry figure: 50-500 users, explicitly for iteration not hype) **first**, held separate from a later coordinated "hard launch" (waitlists commonly built to 5,000-25,000 signups beforehand, 8-12 weeks of ASO/community/press prep, demand concentrated into launch day on purpose to land inside the boost window). Product Hunt flagged as increasingly unreliable alone (feature rate reportedly dropped from 60-98% to ~10% after a Jan-2024 algorithm change).
- **Recommendation given (not a code decision, no action taken):** release to friends now under the current build — matches the professional "small cohort first" pattern rather than working against it. Treat ASO/press/public-launch work as a deliberately separate later event once the planned pre-launch polish is done, since nothing found suggests releasing quietly now costs anything structural later.
- Sources used, for reference if revisited: GoPractice's mobile-app-success study, Business of Apps / Statista performance-rate data, Fyresite failure-rate stats, Sensor Tower's keyword-ranking-drop-off piece, RadASO's boost-mechanics writeup, SplitMetrics' ranking-factors guide, Designli's soft-launch playbook, Waitlister's launch playbook, and an Apple Developer Forums thread on the "day-1 downloads" myth.

**2026-08-23 (Mac, web) — User: "website > home: when i scroll down, i don't immediately see some album covers" then "Add tab takes too long to load especially at first visit" (turned out to mean web's `/quick-add` Add page, not iOS's Add tab — clarified mid-session after an initial wrong-platform assumption).**

- **Home feed cover pop-in — fixed.** `components/sj/Cover.tsx` relied on the browser's native `loading="lazy"`, which only starts fetching once an image is already close to/inside the viewport — often still mid-fetch by the time it scrolled into view. Replaced with an explicit `IntersectionObserver` (`rootMargin: '1200px 0px'`) that mounts the `<img>` ~1200px before it scrolls into view. `Cover` is shared by Home, album/artist/song/chart/search, and quick-add, so the fix applies everywhere covers render, not just Home. `tsc`/lint clean; not live-browser-verified (no browser tool available this session).
- **Quick Add (web `/quick-add`, nav-labeled "Add") slow-load — root cause found and fixed via live `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, not guesswork.** `get_quick_add_candidates` filters `artist_display = ANY(p_artist_names)` (exact equality), but the only index on that column was `idx_release_groups_display_trgm` — a GIN trigram index built for fuzzy/LIKE search. Postgres used it anyway (only option) but a trigram bitmap scan for `=` is inherently imprecise: confirmed live (service_role `_debug_explain` helper from the 08-18 session) that a single-artist shelf query spent ~78 of its ~80ms entirely inside that one Bitmap Index Scan. This is the identical shape of bug `20260712000011` already fixed on the sibling song-candidates RPC (`recordings.artist_display`) — that migration's own comment predicted this: it called `release_groups`'s trigram index "good enough" only because the table was ~10x smaller at the time (~50k rows in July; ~480k now and still growing via the pipeline). Fix: `20260823000000_quick_add_candidates_artist_display_index.sql`, a plain btree `idx_release_groups_artist_display`. **Applied to production** (user ran it via SQL editor — this Mac has no `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` to apply it directly, see CLAUDE.md's device-split note). Re-verified post-apply with a second live `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`: plan changed to `Index Scan using idx_release_groups_artist_display`, execution time **80ms → 1.58ms** (~50x). Quick Add's own seed-assembly + shelf-fetch queries were separately timed fast in isolation (~60-90ms each), so this index was the real dominant cost on the page's critical path (seed-assembly must finish before the 4 concurrent shelf fetches start).
- Also briefly went down a wrong path: assumed "Add tab" meant iOS's bottom-tab-bar Add screen (`Main/SearchView.swift`'s `DiscoveryViewModel`) and built a first-visit loading-skeleton fix there (`ShimmerView` visibility bump + `isFetchingFirstWave` state) — build-verified but **reverted** once the user clarified they meant the web page. No iOS files were left changed.

- **What was actually wrong with the first fix:** embedding `headerContent` once per tab (inside each of the 4 separate `TabView(.page)` pages) meant each tab kept its own independent scroll offset — standard `.page`-style `TabView` behavior. The tab bar is the `Section`'s pinned header, so it sticks once scrolled past. Tab content is chosen via a plain `switch selectedTab { case 0: albumsContent; case 1: songsContent; case 2: communityContent; default: statsContent }` inside the `Section`'s content closure — `Section` content is `@ViewBuilder`, so a `switch` there works exactly like it does in `body`.

Tap-to-switch on the tab bar still works and now additionally preserves scroll position across the switch (previously each tab had its own independent position; now there's only one position, period).

Separately confirmed scrolling to the very top shows the hero exactly once, tab bar directly beneath it, matching what the user asked for.

**2026-08-18 (Mac, launch loading screen — percentage gauge + offline notice, new session) — User: "loading screen: create a percentage gauge + raise error if device is not connected to network." Two candidate screens exist in this app (`RootView`'s auth-wait splash vs. `MainTabView`'s Home-feed splash); asked which, user picked the launch/auth one specifically.**

- **Why that one matters more for the "no network" half of the ask:** `RootView`'s `.loading` case (`sillajukuApp.swift`) gates on `observeAuth()` awaiting Supabase's first `authStateChanges` event — the very first thing rendered on a cold launch, before there's even a session to know signed-in/out. It was previously `Color.white.ignoresSafeArea()`, no content at all. A signed-out-with-no-cache device with zero network could sit there indefinitely with nothing telling the user why. `MainTabView`'s `AppLoadingView` (Home feed load) only runs post-auth and was left untouched, per the user's explicit scope choice.
- **New `Services/NetworkMonitor.swift`** — `@Observable final class`, `.shared` singleton, wraps `NWPathMonitor` on a dedicated serial queue. `isConnected` is push-updated by the path-update handler (main-queue dispatch), starts optimistically `true` so app launch doesn't flash a false error before the monitor's first callback fires.
- **New `LaunchLoadingView`** (private struct, appended to `sillajukuApp.swift`, mirrors — doesn't share code with — `MainTabView`'s private `AppLoadingView` for the same flower/wordmark branding, kept separate since only this file was in scope): a percentage-ring gauge reusing the exact ring-drawing pattern `ScoreBadge.swift` already established (`Circle().stroke` track in `sjBorder` + `Circle().trim(from:to:).stroke(sjAmber, lineCap: .round).rotationEffect(-90°)`), filled by a `Task`-driven time-based ease (`0.92 * (1 - exp(-elapsed/1.4))`, 50ms tick) rather than tied to discrete load steps — there's only one opaque async wait here (unlike Home's multi-fetch load, which has real sub-steps to report against), so this approximates progress by feel and deliberately never reaches 100% on its own; `RootView` swaps the whole view out the moment auth genuinely resolves. Swaps to a `wifi.slash` "No internet connection" notice via a cross-fade the instant `NetworkMonitor.shared.isConnected` flips false — no retry button, since the monitor is push-based (reconnecting flips it back automatically) and the real auth task never stopped running underneath.
- **Verified live in Simulator, honestly scoped to what's actually testable here.** A cached session resolves auth in ~150-250ms, too fast for any single fixed-delay screenshot — used a tightly-spaced sequential screenshot series (0.12s, +0.06s increments) and caught the new gauge mid-render showing a live "0%" at ~240ms, then confirmed the transition into the (unchanged) `AppLoadingView` still renders correctly right after. **Did not live-test the actual offline path** — simulating real no-network on the Simulator means cutting the host Mac's own WiFi, judged too disruptive to do mid-session; the `NWPathMonitor` → `@Observable` → `if/else` wiring is standard, well-precedented framework usage, but this is flagged explicitly rather than claimed as verified when it wasn't.

**2026-08-18 (Mac, search_artists — real EXPLAIN ANALYZE + final fix, same session) — User applied `20260818000001` (clean): re-timed at ~1.3s, a real improvement (from ~2s) but still not fast. User approved ("Yes, add it (recommended)").

- **First real query plan, read via `_tmp_explain.ts`, overturned the working assumption both prior migrations shared.** Total execution time 5.57s, but **4.39s of it was a single `Seq Scan` on `artists` (all 67,634 rows)**, with `Filter: (EXISTS(SubPlan 6) OR EXISTS(SubPlan 7))` — the "has releases" gate added back in `20260728000000_search_hide_empty_artists.sql`. That migration's own comment had called both EXISTS probes "index-backed... cheap despite running before the LIMIT" — true for each individual invocation (both did hit `Index Only Scan`s), but the planner had chosen this AND-clause as the table's *driving* access path, running each probe once per table row (67,634 + 44,811 times) and only applying the now-properly-indexed text-match arms afterward as a `Join Filter`. The alias CTE fix from `20260818000001` was confirmed working exactly as designed in isolation (SubPlan 8: 9.3ms) — it just never got the chance to matter, since Postgres wasn't driving the scan from that side of the `WHERE` at all.
- **Named the actual shape of the problem:** "has releases" is true for ~87% of artists (58,911 / 67,634 in the sampled plan) — a bad column to drive a full-table scan from — while a real search query's text-match conditions are highly selective. One big `AND` of two `OR`-groups gives the planner no way to know that without already having scanned everything.
- **`20260818000003_search_artists_union_candidates.sql` — the actual fix, shaped by the plan data rather than inspection alone.** Restructured `search_artists` as a `UNION` of five independently-indexed single-condition queries (name/name_native/name_phonetic_ko `normalize_text ... LIKE`, alias `normalize_text ... LIKE`, and the `<%` trigram operator on `lower(name)`) producing a small candidate id set, *then* joined that back to `artists` and checked "has releases" against only those rows — a handful of index probes instead of ~112,000. `ORDER BY` left unchanged (confirmed by the same plan it was never the expensive part — only runs over the `LIMIT`-sized final result). User applied via SQL editor.
- **Verified with both timing and a second real `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, not assumed from the first fix's plan matching this one's intent** (`_tmp_verify3.ts`): repeat timing landed 231–555ms across several query terms (the known short-query "IU" 2-char outlier still hit 1655ms — pre-existing, documented, unrelated to this fix). Second plan confirmed every `UNION` branch hitting its own dedicated `Bitmap Index Scan`, **Execution Time: 231.642 ms** — a 24× improvement over the original 5572ms.
- **Live-verified in Simulator, not just via script:** navigated Add tab → Your Top Artists → Tiffany Day; two sequential screenshots (~0.6s and ~1.6s post-tap) confirmed the full page — avatar, stat tiles, album list with covers, own rating — settles completely in well under 2 seconds.
- **`20260818000004_drop_debug_explain_helper.sql`** — cleanup migration dropping `_debug_explain(text)` now that it served its purpose; flagged explicitly as not urgent, apply whenever convenient (`service_role`-only, doesn't widen any real capability).
- **Two minor, non-blocking things noted from the second plan, not fixed:** ~185ms of the remaining 231ms is `ORDER BY`'s exact-alias-match ranking boost (still a full `artist_aliases` scan, but only affects ordering, not correctness — a plain btree index on `normalize_text(alias)` would tighten it if it matters later). Very short queries (2 chars) still fall back to an unindexed path — pre-existing caveat from the original 2026-07-06 sibling fix, unrelated to this session.

**2026-08-18 (Mac, search_artists follow-up, same session) — User applied `20260818000000` (clean, no errors) and re-timed `search_artists` per the earlier ask: unchanged, still ~2-4s. Wrote a second migration for the residual cause its own comment had already flagged as unverified.**

- **Re-timed `search_artists` myself first, independent of the user's report, before theorizing further** (`apps/web/scripts/_tmp_verify_search_artists.ts`, deleted after use): `4551ms` cold, `~1960-2030ms` warm across 3 repeat calls, plus 3 different query terms all landing in the same 1.6-2s band. Essentially identical to the pre-migration numbers from earlier this session. Asked the user directly whether the SQL editor run had actually completed without error (rather than assuming either "it silently failed" or "my fix was wrong") — confirmed clean, no errors — which narrowed it to the one thing `20260818000000`'s own comment had explicitly flagged as unresolved: the alias-match arm.
- **Confirmed the mechanism rather than assuming it from the comment alone.** The alias arm (`EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM artist_aliases al WHERE al.artist_id = a.id AND normalize_text(al.alias) LIKE '%'||nq.qn||'%')`) is a correlated subquery used as an OR-arm — same disease class as the `word_similarity()` arm the first migration already fixed (a non-index-backable arm forces Postgres to fall back to a full seq scan for the *entire* OR clause, not just that arm, regardless of how well-indexed the other four arms now are). Checked `artist_aliases`'s actual size before assuming a fix would help (`96,719` rows, via a direct count query) — larger than `artists` itself (67,629), so simply moving the correlated lookup elsewhere needed to land on something index-backed itself, not just "run once instead of 67k times" and hope that's enough.
- **New migration `20260818000001_search_artists_alias_subquery_fix.sql`:** hoists the alias match into a `matched_alias_artists` CTE (`SELECT DISTINCT al.artist_id FROM artist_aliases al, nq WHERE normalize_text(al.alias) LIKE '%'||nq.qn||'%'`), computed once per top-level call instead of once per candidate `artists` row, with a new supporting GIN trgm index (`idx_artist_aliases_alias_norm_trgm` on `normalize_text(alias)` — the existing `idx_artist_aliases_alias_trgm` only indexes the *raw* `alias` column, same "index exists but for the wrong expression" pattern found twice already this session). The outer `WHERE`'s alias arm becomes `a.id IN (SELECT artist_id FROM matched_alias_artists)` — a semi-join against `artists`'s own primary key, which Postgres's planner can fold into a bitmap/index-based combination with the other four now-indexed arms, unlike the correlated `EXISTS` it replaces. `ORDER BY`'s own alias-exact-match `EXISTS` left untouched, same reasoning as the first migration: it only runs over the already-filtered, already-small result set, never the expensive part.

**2026-08-18 (Mac, load-time + avatar root cause, same session) — User: "artist page still takes a few seconds to load. also, artist avatar doesn't show up--all i see is a placeholder initial." Both investigated to a hard, measured root cause rather than guessed at again.**

- **Load time: proved the client-side fix from earlier this session wasn't enough, then found the actual bottleneck with a timed script rather than assuming.** Wrote a one-off script (`apps/web/scripts/_tmp_time_search.ts`, deleted after use) to time `search_artists` directly against prod: **4110ms cold, then ~2021ms / ~2111ms warm** on repeat calls. For comparison, `get_artist_release_groups` (the other RPC on this page's critical path) timed at 55–153ms in the same session — so `search_artists` alone accounts for essentially all of the perceived "few seconds." This RPC is called by `DiscoveryViewModel.resolveArtistId` (`Main/SearchView.swift`), which `ArtistPageView.load()` runs **first, sequentially, before its own parallel releases/artist-row fetch even starts** — and it runs unconditionally on every navigation from Add tab's Spotify/Apple Music artist rows (`ArtistDestination(artistId: nil, ...)`), since those rows never carry a resolved catalog UUID.
- **Root cause, read directly from the migration history rather than guessed: `search_artists`'s `WHERE` clause has the identical anti-pattern already diagnosed and fixed for the sibling `search_release_groups` function on 2026-07-06** (`20260706000017_search_rg_trgm_indexed.sql` — its own comment explains the mechanism in full: a plain `word_similarity(...) > threshold` function call is never an index qual, and Postgres can only build a `BitmapOr` across an `OR` clause when *every* arm is index-backed — one non-indexable arm forces a full sequential scan of the whole clause, not just that arm). That 2026-07-06 fix was never ported over to `search_artists`, which kept carrying the same `word_similarity(nq.ql, lower(a.name)) > 0.5` arm forward through three later revisions (`20260703000006`, `20260710000001`, `20260728000000`) without anyone revisiting it as the `artists` table grew to 67,629 rows. Also found two of the three normalized-`LIKE` arms wrapped in `coalesce(col, '')` — read `normalize_text()`'s own definition to confirm it already does `coalesce(t, '')` internally (`20260630000000_search_normalize.sql`), so the wrapper changes nothing about behavior, it just doesn't match the GIN trgm indexes already built on the bare `normalize_text(col)` expression, breaking index matching for zero benefit — same redundant-coalesce disease the sibling fix also called out.
- **New migration `20260818000000_search_artists_trgm_indexed.sql`, mirroring the proven 2026-07-06 fix exactly:** `word_similarity(...) > 0.5` → `nq.ql <% lower(a.name)` (new `idx_artists_name_lower_trgm` GIN index); dropped the two redundant `coalesce()` wrappers on `name_native`/`name_phonetic_ko` in the `WHERE` clause (new `idx_artists_name_native_norm_trgm` index — the existing `idx_artists_name_native_trgm` indexes the *raw* column, not `normalize_text(name_native)`, so it never matched this arm either; `idx_artist_phonetic_ko_norm_trgm` already existed and now actually gets used). `ORDER BY` deliberately left untouched (still calls `word_similarity()` directly) — it only runs over the already-filtered, already-small row set, never the expensive part. Signature unchanged, no client changes needed.
- **One honestly-flagged gap in the fix, not resolved:** this session had no way to run a live `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` against production (no raw-SQL execution path from here — Supabase's JS client only exposes PostgREST + RPC calls, and there's no `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` on this machine for the Management API, same limitation noted in multiple prior sessions). So this fix is based on the same reasoning already *validated* for the sibling function, not a directly-confirmed query plan for this one. The alias-match arm (`EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM artist_aliases al WHERE al.artist_id = a.id AND normalize_text(al.alias) LIKE ...)`) is a correlated subquery, which Postgres generally can't fold into a bitmap index scan as an OR-arm either — `idx_artist_aliases_artist` (on `artist_id`) keeps each individual subquery invocation cheap, but that's about the subquery's own cost, not whether the *outer* scan on `artists` can use an index. Documented in the migration's own comment as the next thing to check with a live `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` if the latency doesn't fully resolve.

- **Diagnosed the "badge looks off" complaint precisely before picking a fix**: `ScoreBadge` (`Components/ScoreBadge.swift`) is a fixed composition — a Liquid Glass circle, a flower watermark at `badgeSize * 0.66`, a progress ring drawn *outside* the badge at `badgeSize + 2*(ringGap+ringStroke)` — built to read correctly at its ~48pt app-wide default. Forcing it to `badgeSize: 26` for the artist row (this session's own earlier fix) proportionally shrank every one of those elements at once: the ring got hairline-thin, the flower watermark went nearly illegible, the digits got cramped. That's a real design failure mode (a composition tuned for one size doesn't just "scale down" gracefully), not something a smaller `badgeSize` argument could fix.
- **The right fix already existed in the codebase: `AlbumRateButton`/`FlowerRateControl` has its own native "already rated" rendering** — a single filled circle (`ScoreSpectrum.fill(for: score)`), with the score number sized proportionally (`size * 0.4`) inside it, no separate ring element to break down at small sizes. It was already sitting on this exact row (as the cover-corner "add a rating" overlay for unrated releases) without anyone using its rated-state rendering.

Directly resolves "flower on the right" (there's now exactly one flower, always on the trailing edge) and "the badge looks off" (it's not a badge being scaled anymore — `AlbumRateButton`'s own rated-state visual does the job, and it's designed to hold together at this size). `initialScore: userScore` seeds it correctly per `AlbumRateButton`'s own doc comment ("seeds the button when nothing else on the page needs to know about changes") — nothing else on this row reacts to the score independently, so no `externalScore` binding was needed.

- **Delegated the initial investigation to a research agent** (read-only, `ArtistPageView.load()` in `Main/SearchView.swift` plus `CachedImage`/`ImageCache`), then independently corroborated its DB finding with a direct one-off Supabase query (`apps/web/scripts/_tmp-check-tiffany-day.ts`, run via `npx tsx --env-file=.env.local`, deleted immediately after) rather than taking either source at face value alone.
- **Slowness — real bug, root-caused and fixed.** `ArtistPageView.load()`'s releases fetch was already parallel (`async let releasesFetch`/`artistRowFetch`), but the code *after* that ran three sequential round trips: a `ratings` query for aggregate stats (avg/count/my-rating), then `loadCommunityFeed()`'s own separate, almost-identical `ratings` query (id/user_id/release_group_id/score/created_at/review_text, ordered, limited to 60), then a third `profiles` query keyed off that feed's user ids, manually joined client-side via a `pMap` dictionary. This is the exact "serial-await waterfall" shape SESSIONS.md's 2026-07-xx/2026-08-07 sessions already fixed on Home/Charts/Add — just never applied here. Confirmed via a quick timing script (`_tmp_time_rpc.ts`, also deleted after) that the `get_artist_release_groups` RPC itself is fast (55–153ms, confirming the 2026-07-18 UNION-rewrite migration is live in prod) — the waterfall downstream of it was the actual cost.
- **Fix, in two parts:** (1) `loadCommunityFeed` now selects `profiles!ratings_user_id_fkey(username, display_name)` embedded directly into its `ratings` query — the identical join idiom `HomeView.swift`'s `feedSelect` already uses (`profiles!ratings_user_id_fkey(...)`), and one this file's own `CommunityRating` struct was already shaped to decode (it already had a `profiles: CRProfile?` field with matching `CodingKeys` — just never fed by a query that actually embedded it). This alone collapsed `loadCommunityFeed`'s two queries into one, deleting the `CFRow`/`ProfileRow`/`pMap` manual-join code entirely. (2) In `load()`, the stats `ratings` query and the now-single community-feed query are independent of each other's results, so they're launched together via `async let` and awaited as a pair (`let (rows, feed) = await (statsRowsFetch, communityFeedFetch)`) instead of one blocking the other. Net: 3 sequential round trips → 2 concurrent ones.
- **Verified live in Simulator, not just compiled** (the account was still logged in from earlier in this session — see the taste-map entries above for why that mattered): tapped Tiffany Day from Add tab's "Your Top Artists," page pushed instantly with a spinner, and by the very next screenshot (~1s later) showed fully-loaded stats (2.4 community avg, "You 2 rated · 2.4 avg", 25 releases) and the complete album list — versus the reported ~5s. Also opened the Community tab specifically to confirm the new embedded-join query actually decodes right in practice, not just compiles: real usernames/avatars/timestamps/scores rendered correctly (`@junnwest`, HALO 4.3, THE GRATITUDE PROJECT 0.5).
- **Missing covers — investigated fully, turned out not to be a bug at all.** Queried `release_groups` directly for the two flagged titles: both **"CONSTANTLY" and "Start Over" (Tiffany Day) have `cover_url: null`** in the database — no MusicBrainz/CAA cover was ever ingested for either release; every other Tiffany Day release has a populated `coverartarchive.org` URL. This is the same class of gap SESSIONS.md's cover-art audits have already sized catalog-wide (~23% null). The "forever" (not just slow) part is explained by `Components/CachedImage.swift`: a `nil` `coverUrl` makes `CoverImage` build `URL(string: "")`, which is `nil`, so the `.task` returns immediately with no fetch attempted, no timeout, no error — permanently stuck on `ShimmerView` with nothing to ever distinguish it from "still loading." That's a minor, genuinely separate UX polish item (a nil-cover state could show a static placeholder instead of an eternal shimmer) — **not fixed this pass**, and the missing cover art itself was **not treated as a bug to auto-fix** per this repo's CLAUDE.md convention ("don't auto-fix data, just report and propose") — flagged for a future cover-art backfill run instead.

Queue drained 48 → 0 pending, `failed` still **8, unchanged since 07-19**. The `reconcile`/`gapfill`/`qc` heartbeats came back after 30–32 days stale. Full row in PIPELINE_CHECKS.md.

Probed read-only: `source='spotify'` rows still present in all three tables, and a direct count returned 3,563,782 recordings in 5.8s once load eased. Same stale-`mb-qc.ts`-allowlist non-issue as 08-10.
- **`newreleases` ran for the first time ever** — completed in ~21 min, `+27 flagged`, err=0. **That 27 is not a measurement.** The lane only moves `next_check_at` *backward* (`.gt('next_check_at', dueAt)`, deliberate anti-starvation), and after 4 weeks down essentially the whole catalog was already overdue, so genuine matches were skipped as "already due" and never counted. **The first real number is the next daily sweep.** Also corrected a wrong expectation I'd stated before the restart: the 4-week gap does *not* enlarge the sweep — the window is a fixed 45-day lookback + 30-day lookahead every run, a re-swept window rather than an incremental cursor.
- **🐛 The real find: a FRESHNESS livelock that made the pipeline collect nothing while every lane reported healthy.** ~20 min after the queue drained the catalog went flat (last ingest 03:42 "Urbanus"; `next_check_at`, `last_ingested_at`, and the `search_misses` backlog all frozen for 90+ min). **Root cause:** FRESHNESS claims the hot tier's head (Bob Dylan), `ingestArtist` throws `HeavilyFeaturedError` (> `MAX_INGEST_RGS` = 800 — the Mozart/Bach class), and the catch in `tryFreshness` logged it and returned `true` **without rescheduling `next_check_at`**, so the next pass re-claimed the same artist and failed identically, forever. **It was silent because the lane's heartbeat sits at the END of `refreshArtist`** — so the lane never beat and never reported an error, and a stale `idle` freshness lane beside an `idle` ingest lane is indistinguishable from a healthy drained queue. The **queue** path has guarded this exact hazard since 07-01 ("skip terminally, don't fail+requeue into a loop"); the **freshness** path never got the same guard, and the **2026-08-10 hot-tier-first ordering fix made it reachable immediately**, since the >800-RG artists are concentrated in the hot tier. The fix meant to stop serving dormant artists first walked the worker straight into the first landmine.
- **Diagnosis was DB-only, and two earlier hypotheses were tested and refuted** rather than assumed: (a) "a due artist with no `musicbrainz` external id parks the lane" — refuted, the head has a valid MBID and 2,086 hot-tier artists are due; (b) "`tryMisses` is looping on the 68 unqueued `search_misses` it can never mark" — refuted, that backlog is flat, and `tryFreshness` is called first anyway. The clincher was the ~10–20s loop period, which matches paging 800+ release groups at MB's ~1 req/s.
- **Fix** (`scripts/pipeline.ts` `tryFreshness`): the catch now **always advances the schedule**. Heavily-featured parks `FRESHNESS_HEAVY_SKIP_DAYS` (~10y — the freshness equivalent of the queue's terminal `skipped`; **deliberately not `null`**, because `bootstrapFreshness()` re-schedules every null `next_check_at` at startup and would walk straight back into the loop); anything else backs off `FRESHNESS_ERROR_BACKOFF_DAYS` (1d, transient-friendly). A failed reschedule logs a distinct `WARN … may retry-loop` rather than blending into the normal error line. `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Self-heals on restart, no data fix needed** — each heavily-featured artist now costs one failed attempt (~15s) and is then parked.
- **✅ Restarted and VERIFIED LIVE.** On restart Bob Dylan's `next_check_at` jumped `2026-06-28` → **`2036-08-15`** (the heavily-featured park) and the worker moved on instead of re-claiming him. 2 artists parked, then FRESHNESS did **6 real re-polls** — including `Anuel AA +2 new groups`, corroborated independently by a `release_groups` count that rose by exactly +2 in the same window, versus 0 movement across 90+ minutes pre-fix. Post-restart `status`/`verify` logged as a second row in PIPELINE_CHECKS.md (5/7 — `integrity`'s known set plus a `tiering` timeout that had *passed* hours earlier, the difference being the concurrent cover backfill's write load; `tiering` is simply borderline against a 4.6M-row `release_tracks` and shouldn't be read as signal from one run).
- **Learned while verifying, and worth not re-learning:** under `--fresh-focus`, `pipeline:status`'s `last 60m 0/hr` is **not** a stall — it counts queue drains only, and the queue is supposed to be empty (`discover`/`area` off). All the real work is FRESHNESS re-polls, which that metric ignores. I nearly called a healthy pipeline stalled twice on this. Also: a re-poll re-ingests an artist's whole discography at MB's ~1 req/s, so several minutes of apparent silence mid-re-poll is normal — catalog counts climb during it even though `last_ingested_at` and the lane heartbeat (both written at the *end*) stay frozen.

- **Pipeline retuned for recency: new `NEWRELEASES` lane + a freshness ordering fix.** User: *"less expansion, focus on fetching new releases… not just famous, but all artists. we have to update new releases asap."*
  - **Why the old design couldn't deliver that.** FRESHNESS asks MB "anything new?" once **per artist**, and a re-poll costs ~3 MB requests (`getArtist` + `browseReleaseGroups` + `browseArtistReleases`). Across 67,522 artists that's ~200k requests ≈ **2.3 days of solid MB time per full cycle**, forever, plus rewriting 478k release groups each pass. Whole-catalog recency is simply unreachable that way — it's a throughput ceiling, not a tuning problem.
  - **Inverted the question.** MB indexes `firstreleasedate` on release-group search and returns credited artist MBIDs in the result. So ask once per date window instead of once per artist. Measured live: ~340 new release groups/day worldwide; a 2-day probe returned 1,078 groups / 754 artists, **151 of them ours** → only ~**75 catalog artists/day** actually have a new release. Daily cost ≈ 4 sweep requests + ~225 re-poll requests ≈ **4 minutes**, versus 2.3 days. ~3,000× less MB time, and it covers every artist we own rather than a prioritised slice.
  - **New `scripts/discover-mb-newreleases.ts` + `newreleases` pipeline lane (daily, ON by default, `NEWRELEASES=0` disables).** It **does not ingest** — it only sets `next_check_at = now()` on catalog artists credited on something new, so the existing idempotent FRESHNESS path does the actual work, now aimed only at artists that demonstrably have a new release. Deliberately a **re-swept overlapping window (45d back / 30d ahead), not an incremental cursor**: MB search can only filter on release *date*, not on when the row was *added*, and editors routinely add back-dated releases weeks late — a cursor would permanently miss those. Only moves `next_check_at` **backward**, so repeat sweeps can't shuffle the queue or starve a long-overdue artist. Artists we don't own are counted and reported but never queued (this lane is freshness, not expansion). New `searchReleaseGroupsByQuery` in `mb-client.ts`.
  - **Fixed a real ordering defect in FRESHNESS.** `claimDueFreshness` ordered purely by `next_check_at` ascending = *most overdue first*, which **inverts** the intended priority after any pause: a dormant artist scheduled 90 days ago outranks a hot artist scheduled yesterday, so the backlog drains least-important-first. Now queries tier by tier (`hot → active → known → dormant`, oldest-due-first within a tier) — the composite index `idx_artists_priority (ingest_priority, next_check_at)` already existed for exactly this and nothing was using it.
  - **`--fresh-focus` preset** (`npm run pipeline:fresh`) = `--no-discover` + `AREA_DISCOVERY=0` + `FRESHNESS_EVERY=3`, NEWRELEASES still on. Every part is still settable individually.
  - **Note for whoever tunes tiers later:** `recompute_ingest_priorities()` derives tiers from release recency + *whether anyone in our DB rated the artist*. With a pre-launch user base the rating signal is nearly empty, so tiers are effectively "released recently" — there is **no fame/popularity signal stored on `artists`** (Last.fm listeners are used at discovery time and thrown away). Not a problem for this design, since NEWRELEASES targets by actual new-release evidence rather than by tier, but it makes "prioritise famous artists" a bigger job than it looks.
  - **Verify:** `tsc --noEmit` clean for everything touched (the lone `scripts/backfill-rg-covers-kr.ts:88` error is pre-existing, untracked, out of scope). Sweep smoke-tested live on a 2-day window in dry-run. **The lane has NOT been run for real and the pipeline is still stopped** — deliberately, so it doesn't fight the video-cleanup scan for MusicBrainz.

  - **Why classification was added rather than just running `--write`.** "Absent from MB's audio list" has more than one cause. Only one is a bug: MB flagging `recording.video = true`. The others are a recording MB **merged** away or a release an editor **re-tracked** — real audio that moved, where deleting is a data judgment, not a fix. **2026-08-15 (Mac) — Fixed a user-reported bug: tapping an artist in Add tab's "Your Top Artists" (Spotify-sourced row) took 5+ seconds to open the artist page with zero loading indication, reading as a dead/broken tap.**

- **Root cause, `Main/SearchView.swift`:** `spotifyArtistScroll`'s avatar `Button` (was line ~1185) ran an async `resolveArtist(name:)` (a `search_artists` RPC + name/native/alias overlap gate, added in an earlier session to fix a *correctness* bug — the old bare `artistId: nil` fallback could show an empty or wrong artist) and only pushed the page (`spotifyArtistNavTarget = ...`) once that resolution finished. Every sibling artist row (search results, Apple Music's "Your Top Artists") uses a plain `NavigationLink(value:)` that pushes instantly. So this row alone paid the full resolution latency **before** the user saw any navigation at all — and `.buttonStyle(.plain)` on top meant not even a press-state dim during the wait. The multi-second part specifically is the same cold-launch network contention already diagnosed in the previous Add-tab fix (session 2 below) — this RPC competes with `DiscoveryViewModel.load()`'s own burst of concurrent fetches for the same host.
- **Fix:** moved the identity-aware resolution *into* `ArtistPageView.load()` instead of gating navigation on it. `spotifyArtistScroll` now uses a plain `NavigationLink(value: ArtistDestination(artistId: nil, ...))`, identical in shape to the Apple Music row — the page pushes immediately and shows its own existing spinner (`ArtistPageView.swift`'s `isLoading` → `ProgressView()`, already there, previously just unreachable during the wait). `ArtistPageView.load()`'s `artistId == nil` branch now calls the same alias-aware resolver (`DiscoveryViewModel.resolveArtistId`, widened from `private` to `fileprivate` so `ArtistPageView` — a different struct in the same file — can reuse it) before falling back to the weaker bare-ILIKE path, so the correctness fix from the earlier session is preserved (and now also benefits the Apple Music row, which had never gotten it). Deleted the now-fully-dead `SearchView.resolveArtist(name:)` (was only ever called from this one site) and the `spotifyArtistNavTarget` `@State`/`.navigationDestination(item:)` pair it required — the shared `.navigationDestination(for: ArtistDestination.self)` every other artist row already uses covers this now.
- **Verified live in Simulator, not just compiled:** tapped "Simon Dominic" (a real Korean-name-mismatch case — Spotify's plain-English rendering vs. this app's own artist row) from Your Top Artists; a screenshot taken ~150ms after the tap (mid-slide-transition) already showed the pushed `ArtistPageView` header with its spinner visible, and the fully-loaded page correctly showed 12 releases / 11 community ratings / the user's own 3 ratings — confirming both the instant-navigation fix and that the moved resolver still finds the right artist, not an empty or wrong one.
- **`xcodebuild` clean, no new warnings.** Nothing committed.

**2026-08-13 (Mac, session 3) — Fixed a user-reported Add-tab bug: occasionally only "Your Top Artists" showed up, everything else empty until a manual pull-to-refresh.**

- **Root cause, `Main/SearchView.swift`'s `DiscoveryViewModel`:** `loadDiscovery()` (line ~411), `loadRecommendations()` (~424), and `loadRatedArtists()` (~387) each silently swallow a failed fetch (`guard let resp = await WebAPI.get(...) else { return }` / `try? ... ?? []`) as "no data" rather than surfacing an error — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty response. `.task { await discoveryVM.load() }` (line ~700-701) only ever runs once per view lifetime (the tab stays mounted for the app session per this codebase's `visitedTabs` design), and unlike Spotify/Apple Music — which get a `refreshXIfNeeded()` retry hook wired into `.onChange(of: scenePhase)` — discovery/recommendations had **no retry path at all** short of the user manually pulling to refresh (`discoveryVM.refresh()`). "Your Top Artists" alone survives because `loadSpotify()` populates it from a synchronous local `UserDefaults` cache first (line ~304), immune to whatever network contention (cold-launch Home/Quest queries competing for bandwidth, most likely) killed the other three fetches. Notably, a comment already sitting in the code (lines 95-104) correctly diagnosed this exact failure shape and referenced the Taste tab's earlier same-root-cause bug — but the actual retry trigger the comment describes was never wired up.
- **Fix:** `load()` now retries `reloadDiscoverySections()` once, automatically, if `hasDiscoveryData` is still false after the initial fan-out — same "optional fetch, one retry" pattern already used by `TasteViewModel`/`MixLibraryViewModel` for this identical bug shape (see 2026-08-07 entry below). No user action required; fixes the bug at the point it actually happens (first cold load) rather than only via pull-to-refresh, which already worked and was the user's reported workaround.
- **Verified:** `xcodebuild` clean, no new warnings. Live in Simulator: fresh install → Add tab loaded every section correctly on the very first attempt (search bar, Quick Add banner, Your Top Artists, Popular, New Releases). Since the underlying failure is network-timing-dependent, the retry path itself couldn't be forced to fire deterministically in this pass — the fix reuses an already-exercised function (`reloadDiscoverySections()`) under a condition that's cheap and safe to hit twice, so risk is low, but flagging that the exact race wasn't reproduced live.
- **Flagged, not fixed (out of scope for this bug):** `Services/WebAPI.swift`'s failure paths (lines ~22-48) only `print()` on error, never reporting to Sentry (already initialized elsewhere in the app) — this whole failure mode is currently invisible in production. Worth a follow-up if these silent failures turn out to be more than occasional.
