**2026-08-13 (Mac) — Ported web's drag-to-rate gauge visual polish to iOS (`FlowerRateControl.swift`): the flower pops forward in 3D above a diffusing radial fade, and whole-star tick marks became concentric rings.**

- **Context: `git pull` this session (see the git-conflict-resolution note above) surfaced two web changes the user wanted brought to iOS — a drag-to-rate gauge polish and a much larger taste-page rebuild.** Given the size mismatch (gauge polish is a focused ~420-line file; the taste page is a ~1,700-line rebuild across `taste/page.tsx` + new `TasteCharts.tsx` + rewritten `TasteGraph.tsx`), asked the user how to sequence rather than guessing — chose gauge polish now, taste page as its own planned session later (not started this session, flagged in START HERE so it isn't lost).
- **Read web's `FlowerRateControl.tsx` in full before touching iOS code.** The web change (commit `8e9c046`, "drag-rate gauge polish"): while dragging, the flower is re-rendered inside a React portal (`createPortal(..., document.body)`), lifted and scaled 1.22× with a layered box-shadow, sitting genuinely in front of a radial-gradient scrim that now *animates* outward on press (CSS `transform: scale()` from 0.35→1, `transformOrigin` at the button's centre) instead of snapping on as a flat wash; the in-flow original button hides (`opacity: 0`) but keeps its pointer capture. Whole-star tick marks became full concentric ring circles (faint dashed by default, solid/coloured once reached).
- **iOS port, `Components/FlowerRateControl.swift` + `RateGaugeOverlay.swift`:**
  - `RateGaugeOverlay.show(...)` and `RateGaugeView`'s init gained a `size: CGFloat` param (threaded from `FlowerRateControl`'s own `size`) — needed so the overlay's popped-flower duplicate can render at the same dimensions as the real button.
  - `FlowerRateControl.buttonContent` gained `.opacity(isDragging ? 0 : 1)` — hides the real button during a drag, mirroring web's portal approach; the `DragGesture` attached to it keeps receiving touch events regardless of opacity, same as web's pointer capture surviving a CSS opacity change, so no gesture-handling change was needed.
  - **New `poppedFlower` subview in `RateGaugeView`** — deliberately duplicates `buttonContent`'s flower/score-number/trash-icon rendering inline rather than factoring out a shared subcomponent, matching how web's own `DragGauge` inlines the same markup rather than sharing one. Driven by a new `@State private var popped = false` flipped `true` inside `withAnimation` on `.onAppear` (SwiftUI's own "before-state paints first, then animate" guarantee stands in for web's `requestAnimationFrame`-gated `shown` flag — no extra frame-delay trick needed). Scale 1.22, `.offset(y: -3)`, two stacked `.shadow()` modifiers that intensify once popped, animated via `.timingCurve(0.34, 1.5, 0.64, 1, duration: 0.22)` — ported directly from web's `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.5, 0.64, 1)` 220ms bounce.
  - **New `diffusingScrim`** — a six-stop `RadialGradient` (`Circle().fill(RadialGradient(...))`, sized `2 × endRadius`, positioned at `origin`), with stop locations converted from web's pixel-based CSS gradient stops into 0–1 fractions of `endRadius = RateGaugeGeometry.maxRadius * 1.62` (same outer fade-to-transparent radius web uses). Animated via `.scaleEffect(popped ? 1 : 0.35)` + `.opacity`, `.timingCurve(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1, duration: 0.46)` — the gradient itself is drawn once at full size and only the transform animates, since SwiftUI `Canvas` content doesn't tween on its own the way a CSS `transform: scale()` on a static gradient does; using `.scaleEffect` on a plain `View` (not redrawing inside `Canvas`) was the correct port of that same trick, not a novel workaround. Shown only when `!canDelete` — Phase B's existing `.regularMaterial` blur already handles background dimming for the drag-to-delete flow, and layering both looked muddy in a quick visual check, so the two dimming treatments are kept mutually exclusive by flow rather than combined.
  - **`gaugeCanvas`'s whole-star tick-mark loop replaced with concentric ring circles** — `Path().addEllipse(...)` at each star's radius, faint dashed stroke by default, solid coloured stroke (thicker) once the drag score reaches that star, directly matching web's SVG `<circle>` rings.
- **One bug caught and fixed before building: the scrim's initial `.scaleEffect(anchor:)` used a manually-computed `UnitPoint` derived from `origin`/screen size, which was wrong** — since the gradient shape is already `.position(origin)`-ed (its own centre placed at `origin`), the correct anchor is simply the default `.center` (scale around the shape's own centre, which *is* origin). Caught on a read-through before ever building, not via a live bug.
- **`xcodebuild` → BUILD SUCCEEDED. Verified live** in Simulator on two different call sites: a small 30pt quick-rate flower (search results grid) and the large 90pt `ManualRatingSheet` flower (via a "Rate" context-menu action). Screenshots confirm: the popped flower renders lifted with a visible shadow above a scrim that visibly darkens the surrounding sheet (darkest near the button, fading outward with no hard edge); mid-drag at a 2.0 score, exactly two concentric rings render solid gold (score-spectrum coloured, reached) while the remaining three stay faint and dashed beyond — matching the intended web design precisely. Confirmed Phase B's drag-to-delete blur/trash flow (built earlier this week, unchanged by this pass) still renders correctly and doesn't double up with the new scrim, since the two are gated mutually exclusive by `canDelete`.
- **Test rating left in place** (Crucial Star's *BoyHood*, rated 2.0 during verification) — harmless test data on an unrelated album, not cleaned up.

First attempt used `screenWidth - 32` (much bigger, ~370-390pt on modern phones); live-tested and found it pushed the Save/More button row off the bottom edge of the `.large`-detent sheet, since the 9:16 canvas at that width alone exceeds the available height once the nav bar, safe areas, and action-button section are subtracted. Dialed back to a still-substantially-bigger 320pt cap that was verified live to keep the whole sheet on one screen with no scrolling (the old design used a `ScrollView`; the new one doesn't need it).
- **Sticker interactivity: `@State private var stickerOffset: CGSize`/`stickerScale: CGFloat`, `@GestureState` for the live in-flight drag/pinch deltas.** `DragGesture` repositions (clamped so the sticker's center can never leave the canvas — `±previewWidth/height * 0.5` — easy to lose track of otherwise once dragged near an edge with no visible boundary). `MagnificationGesture` resizes, clamped 0.5–2.2×. Both are `SimultaneousGesture`s attached via `.highPriorityGesture` specifically on the sticker view (not the whole page) so they win over the `TabView`'s own page-swipe gesture when a touch starts on the card itself, while swipes starting anywhere else on the canvas still page through backgrounds normally — this exact conflict (child drag gesture vs. parent TabView paging) is a known SwiftUI gotcha, `.highPriorityGesture` is the documented fix. Kept the existing single-tap (flip card light/dark) working alongside a new double-tap (reset position + size to default) — SwiftUI disambiguates tap counts automatically when both are attached to the same view. Added a one-time "Drag or pinch the card to adjust" hint, shown only while `stickerOffset == .zero && stickerScale == 1.0` (i.e., before the user's first interaction) — dragging/pinching a sticker isn't an obvious affordance in a share sheet the way it already is inside Instagram's own app, where users bring that expectation with them.
- **`InstagramShare.composite` gained `stickerScale: CGFloat = 1.0` and `stickerOffsetFraction: CGSize = .zero` params**, expressed as fractions of the canvas's own width/height (not points) so the exact same values are valid whether `canvas` is the 1080×1920 story size or the 1080×1350 post size — a fixed-point offset measured against the on-screen preview's arbitrary size wouldn't translate correctly to either export canvas. `SharePreviewSheet.exportImage`/`postExportImage` thread the *committed* (post-gesture, i.e. `stickerOffset`/`stickerScale` directly, not the live `@GestureState` deltas) values through — correct since export only ever happens via a button tap, when no gesture is actively in flight anyway.
- **Explicitly documented, not silently left as a gap: the direct-to-Instagram-Stories/Reels handoff can't carry the custom placement.** Instagram's pasteboard contract (`com.instagram.sharedSticker.stickerImage` + background keys) has no sticker-position key at all — only Save/More/Post (which this app composites itself via `InstagramShare.composite`) can honor a custom placement. Added an explicit note to `shareToInstagramStories`'s doc comment stating this is a real platform limitation, not a bug, so a future session doesn't spend time trying to "fix" something Instagram's own API doesn't support — the user can still reposition after handoff using Instagram's own native editor gestures, so nothing is functionally lost for that path, just not WYSIWYG with this app's preview.
- **`xcodebuild` → BUILD SUCCEEDED.** **Verified live in Simulator**, navigating via a real rated album's "···" → Share menu action (not a synthetic test harness): confirmed the bigger canvas fit on one screen without the earlier button-cutoff bug; dragged the card to a new position (screenshot confirms it landed exactly where dropped, hint correctly disappeared once touched); pinched it larger using Simulator's Option-held-drag pinch simulation (screenshot confirms visible size increase); double-tapped to confirm it snapped back to center/default size via a spring animation, hint reappeared; swiped elsewhere on the canvas (away from the sticker) to confirm background paging (Solid Color → Gradient) still works normally and the sticker's custom placement persists across background pages (shared `@State`, not per-page). Did not pixel-inspect an actual saved/exported image file — the export math is a direct, symmetric application of the same values already confirmed on-screen, not independently re-verified past code review.
- Separately, per explicit request: bumped `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` 14 → 15 in `project.pbxproj` (both Debug and Release configs) — unrelated to the share-sheet work, just done in the same session.

**2026-08-12 (Windows, web, session 4) — J-pop world stops calling itself "Korean scene" / recommending K-pop, + inspector scrollbar overlap (`lib/taste/profile.ts`, `app/api/taste/profile/route.ts`, `components/sj/TasteGraph.tsx`).**

- **Bug (user report):** a J-pop world (Aimer albums) was labelled "mostly 2020s · **Korean scene**" and its "You might like" was **all K-pop** (SEVENTEEN/IVE/TWICE/TAEYEON), while "Your ratings here" was correctly all Aimer.
- **Root cause:** `buildClusters` already scene-pins the world to `jp` (a `j-pop` tag anchors/locks it via `tagScene`), but that `scene` was **dropped from the returned `TasteCluster`**. So `clusterProfiles` recomputed the world's scene purely from the **countries of the albums that landed nearest its centroid by genre cosine** — and Korean releases carrying a stray `j-pop` tag assign there, dragging `dominantScene` to `kr`. That wrong scene then fed `blobAffinity`'s scene term, so Korean/2020s K-pop candidates ranked top in the J-pop recs. One dropped signal caused both symptoms.
- **Fix:** `TasteCluster` now carries `scene`, populated by `buildClusters`. In `clusterProfiles`, a **scene-pinned world takes its scene from its genres** (`sceneShares = {pinned: 1}`, `dominantScene = pinned`) instead of the noisy album-country vote; scene-neutral worlds (rock, jazz…) keep the country-derived shares as before. In the taste route, the rec pool for a pinned world is additionally **scene-filtered** — only in-scene (or unknown-country) candidates survive — so a J-pop world can't surface Korean K-pop even from a mis-tagged catalog row. Verified on a synthetic j-pop+k-pop profile: the j-pop cluster is `scene=jp`, and its profile stays `dominantScene=jp` / `{jp:1}` even when fed a Korean album tagged `[j-pop,k-pop]`. The recommendations route (`/api/recommendations`) inherits the same pin via `clusterProfiles`. Taste cache `v9 → v10`.
- **Inspector scrollbar overlap:** the "Your ratings here" list (`max-h-[240px] overflow-y-auto`) had its scrollbar drawing over the score column. Fixed with `pr-2.5` + `scrollbar-gutter: stable` so the gutter is reserved and content never sits under the bar.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` + `next lint` clean; scene-pin logic checked against the real embedding artifact via a throwaway tsx script. **Not yet eyeballed live.** Note: this doesn't re-tag the catalog — mis-tagged Korean-album-as-j-pop rows still exist; the fix makes the *taste layer* scene-correct regardless.

**2026-08-12 (Windows, web, session 3) — Taste map interaction + polish pass (`components/sj/TasteGraph.tsx`): flexible canvas height, album counts, small-tile labels, a fluid open animation, and a Vision-OS "magnet" hover.**

- **Canvas flexes to fill the taller column.** The map card is now `flex flex-col` with the tile box `flex-1 min-h-[440px] sm:min-h-[540px]`, and the grid row is `md:items-stretch`. So when the inspector is tall (a world open with 10 rated albums + 5 recs), the mosaic grows to match instead of leaving a fixed-height gap — the "6+ ratings and 5 recs" height mismatch. The `ResizeObserver` already recomputes the mosaic grid on the new height. Cell target relaxed to ~104px and the grid cap raised 3×3 → 4×4 so big tiles use the extra space.
- **Album counts on big tiles.** Each big tile now shows a rated-album count in its meta line — worlds read "{n} rated · {pct}%", sub-genres "{n} rated" (new `sj.taste.mapNAlbums` key, en/ko). Counts come from the per-world album roll-up / `albumsByTag`, already computed for the mosaics.
- **Small-tile text fixed.** Labels are now tiered by the tile's measured px size: **big** (name + meta + chip), **med** (name + chip), **small** (single truncated line, no chip), **tiny** (tooltip only). A small tile that previously showed nothing now shows a clean truncated name — text never overflows or gets pushed.
- **Fluid open animation.** Clicking a world no longer hard-swaps: the clicked tile grows to fill the canvas (`enterState:'target'` → left/top→0, w/h→100 over 380ms) while its siblings fade and shrink (`'other'`), then the sub-genre mosaic resolves in with a `taste-open` scale-settle. Reduced-motion skips straight to the mosaic. Replaces the previous origin-var zoom keyframe.
- **Vision-OS "magnet" hover.** Tiles lift and **tilt toward the pointer** — a pointer-tracked `rotateX/rotateY` + `scale(1.04) translateY(-3px)` under a `perspective`, written imperatively (via refs) so the mousemove never re-renders (which would wipe the transform); a soft-light specular highlight tracks the cursor. Siblings dim to `brightness(.78)` via a pure-CSS `.taste-tiles:has(.taste-tile:hover) .taste-tile:not(:hover)` rule (no React state → the imperative transform survives). All of it collapses under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` + `next lint` clean. **Not yet eyeballed live** (≥25-ratings gate) — worth checking the tilt/lift feel and the open animation in both themes, and that the canvas height reads well when the inspector is short (empty state) vs tall (busy world).

**2026-08-12 (Windows, web, session 2) — Taste map follow-ups: affinity-ranked recs + a two-stage genre-merge (`app/api/taste/profile/route.ts`, `lib/taste/profile.ts`, new `lib/taste/genreSynonyms.ts`, `lib/taste/embeddings.ts`).**

- **"You might like" now ranked by taste fit, not raw prestige.** The rec pools were `overlaps(genres) + order by prestige_score` — so the same canonical albums repeated across tabs and nothing reflected the user. Each pool is still prestige-*gated* to canon-quality albums (now `limit 90`, and it fetches `first_release_date` + primary-artist `country`), then **re-ranked in Node by `blobAffinity`** (genre cosine + era gaussian + scene share against the user's world profiles — the same fit math the recommender uses), with prestige only as the tiebreak. So the panel shows the most *on-taste* of the canon-quality candidates.
- **Genre merging — investigated, then built for the real problem.** The initial hypothesis was spelling variants (k-pop/kpop/korean pop). Empirically checked against the embedding vocab (1009 tags): **zero multi-spelling groups** — the catalog is already consistently spelled, so spelling-merge alone is inert here. The actual sub-genre clutter is *semantic* near-duplicates: measured co-occurrence cosines put **r&b↔soul at 0.96** (true twins) while indie-rock↔alt-rock is 0.73 and k-pop↔j-pop 0.55 (distinct). So `mergeSynonymWeights` became **two-stage**: (1) spelling canonicalization via new `genreSynonyms.ts` (structural fold + a small alias table — r&b/rnb, k-pop/korean pop, j-pop/japanese pop — canonical = highest-support catalog spelling; kept as a correct-but-currently-inert safety net + the normalization layer for future imports), then (2) an **embedding near-twin fold**: positively-weighted tags within `NEAR_DUP_COSINE = 0.93` collapse into the stronger anchor (soul→r&b), summing weights so `3 + w/n` stays a true average. Verified on a synthetic profile: soul folds into r&b (avg recombined), indie-rock/alt-rock and shoegaze/dream-pop stay separate, a disliked tag (w≤0) is never folded.
- **Plumbing.** `mergeSynonymWeights` now returns `{ weights, anchorOf }`; the route maps each album/candidate's raw genres onto merged tile tags via `anchorOf` (`toTile`) and expands anchors back to every raw catalog spelling (`spellingsOf`) for the `genres` overlap query, so albums/recs tagged with a folded spelling still match the merged tile. The stored `user_taste_profiles.genre_weights` upsert **keeps raw keys** (iOS reads it) — only the derived map/clusters see the merge. `genreVocab()` added to `embeddings.ts`. Cache key `v8 → v9`.
- **Tunable:** `NEAR_DUP_COSINE` (0.93) is the single knob for merge aggressiveness — lower (≈0.90) also folds motown/quiet-storm into r&b; higher keeps only the tightest twins.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` + `next lint` (touched files) clean; synonym grouping, cosine probes, and the merge all checked against the real embedding artifact via throwaway tsx scripts. **Not yet walked through live** — same ≥25-ratings gate as session 1.

**2026-08-12 (Windows, web) — Taste map reconstructed from a flat-colour treemap into a cover-mosaic treemap, as a portfolio-piece pass (`components/sj/TasteGraph.tsx`).**

- **Diagnosis (why the old map fell short).** The treemap encoded three things — area (share), colour (avg score, via `spectrumColor`), and a text label — but two channels were weak and the richest asset went unused. (1) **Bland fill:** a user's world averages nearly all land in ~3.5–4.5, so score-as-hue produced a near-monochrome quilt carrying almost no information. (2) **Un-coordinated zoom:** clicking a world hard-swapped the whole 100×100 box to a fresh squarified sub-treemap with a fade — no origin, no spatial continuity ("area isn't conserved"). (3) **Text pushed/clipped:** labels were fixed 13/15px gated on magic-number width/height thresholds tuned to one profile. (4) **Disorganised sub-genres:** raw `tags.slice(0,8)` with no dedup. (5) **Inconsistent recs:** per-tag recs rendered only `if (forTag.length>0)`, so the panel appeared/vanished tab-to-tab. (6) **Redundant panel:** the side rail re-listed the same worlds as bars. (7) Album art was shrunk to 8×8px thumbnails.
- **The rebuild** (self-contained in `TasteGraph.tsx` — the `/api/taste/profile` data contract is unchanged; every mosaic is derived client-side from `data.albums`, which already ships each rated album's cover + in-vocab tags + score, score-descending):
  - **Cover-mosaic tiles.** Each tile is tiled with the covers of the albums rated in that world/sub-genre. `chooseGrid(tileW,tileH,n)` picks the largest fully-fillable grid (~96px cells, capped 3×3, never a half-empty cell) from the tile's **measured pixel size** (a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas → `box{w,h}`, since tile %→px depends on the box's real dimensions). A corner with no art falls back to the old score gradient, so tiles are never empty.
  - **Number kept, colour demoted.** Avg rating rides as a solid numeric **chip** (`spectrumFill` bg + `spectrumNumber` text — the same badge language as the top-album score elsewhere), always legible over covers. The OKLCh score ramp is demoted to a **thin accent frame** (`inset 0 0 0 1.5px accent` + brighter ring when selected) — a glanceable heat cue that no longer floods the tile.
  - **Origin-anchored zoom + breadcrumb.** Opening a world records its rect and feeds it to the sub-genre layer as CSS vars (`--ox/--oy/--ow/--oh`); a `taste-zoom-in` keyframe grows the layer *out of that rectangle* (`transform-origin:0 0`), so the drill reads as zooming into the tile. A backdrop-blur **breadcrumb** (All worlds ▸ World ▸ sub-genre, each crumb walks a level) replaces the floating Back button; Escape still backs out one level.
  - **Spotlight focus.** Selecting a sub-genre darkens the others via `filter:brightness(.42) saturate(.65)` instead of the old `opacity:.32` (which read as disabled/broken).
  - **Sub-genres deduped** by display name (two tag keys can collapse to one label). **Recs always render** — the focused tag's own pool if present, else the world pool under a labelled "More in {world}" header — so the panel is never inconsistently empty.
  - **Inspector default state** is now a **cover-thumbnail launcher** (leading album cover + name + share bar per world) rather than a second bars-copy of the map. Tiles + launcher rows are `role="button"` divs with Enter/Space handlers (Cover renders a `<div>`, so nesting it in a real `<button>` would be invalid DOM).
- **i18n.** New `sj.taste.*` keys in `en.ts`+`ko.ts`: `mapAllWorlds`, `mapMoreIn`, `mapOthers`, `mapExplore`, `mapShareOfLibrary`; `mapSub`/`mapHint` reworded for the cover language.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` + `next lint` (touched file) clean. **Not yet walked through live** — needs a signed-in account with ≥25 ratings; worth eyeballing mosaic density across tile sizes in both themes, the zoom-from-tile timing, and cover-load performance on a dense map.

**2026-08-11 (Windows, web, session 3) — Drag-to-rate gauge polish, then a taste-map + clustering follow-up (fade animates outward, map legend un-overlapped, world tiles hint sub-genres, and J-pop finally gets its own world + in-genre recs).**

- **Gauge (`components/sj/FlowerRateControl.tsx`).** (1) The fade scrim was a flat dark band that painted *over* the flower. The flower is now re-rendered inside the portal, above the scrim, lifted and popped forward in 3D (scale 1.22 + translateY + layered drop-shadow/inner-highlight) so it reads as genuinely in front of the fade; the in-flow original is hidden (opacity 0) during the drag but keeps the pointer capture. (2) The scrim is **fully clear behind the flower and diffuses outward** — darkest through the gauge band, dissolving to nothing beyond, no hard edges — and now **animates that diffusion on press**: it scales from a tight disc behind the button out to full reach (`transform-origin` at the button centre, 460ms ease-out) rather than snapping on. Rec pool coverage raised (`REC_POOL_WORLDS 3 → 7`) so the separated world gets its own in-genre recs. Cache key bumped `v7 → v8`.

**2026-08-11 (Windows, web, session 2) — App-Store-style sidebar with in-sidebar search, taste map rebuilt as a treemap heatmap, wider Taste/Profile tabs, and a deeper J-pop clustering fix.**

- **Sidebar rebuilt to mirror the App Store web layout.** Widened `w-[212px] → w-[264px]` and moved the global `SearchOmnibox` **into** the sidebar (order: logo → search → nav → settings), matching apps.apple.com's left rail. On desktop the top bar now carries only the notifications bell + avatar (search left it); on mobile — where the sidebar is `hidden md:flex` — the omnibox still renders in the top bar (`md:hidden` wrapper) so search + ⌘K/"/" stay reachable. Both instances mount; the hidden one's input focus is a no-op, so the keyboard shortcut always lands on the visible box. `SearchOmnibox` gained a `fullWidth` prop (swaps `flex-1 max-w-md` → `w-full`).
- **Taste map redesigned from bubbles to a treemap heatmap** (`components/sj/TasteGraph.tsx`). The old design sized worlds as circles by `√share`, so minor worlds collapsed into unreadable dots (the user's complaint). Replaced with a **squarified treemap** (Bruls/Huizing/van Wijk): one rounded tile per world, area ∝ share, fill = the app's OKLCh score ramp (`spectrumColor`) as a top-lit gradient with a bottom scrim so white labels stay legible across the whole ramp. Every world — and, on drill-in, every sub-genre — gets a labelled tile regardless of share; tiny tiles keep colour + tooltip and drop the label rather than overflow. Kept the entire data contract (`TasteGraphData`/worlds/tags/albums/recs/note), the click-to-drill-in + Back interaction, the side panel (world list → world/tag detail with albums + recs), the score-ramp legend, and `prefers-reduced-motion`. Dropped the now-unused force-layout/camera-zoom/drift machinery. The `squarify` layout was unit-tested to cover 100% of the box with no overlap or NaN across even/skewed/single-tile inputs.

- **J-pop clustering — deeper fix than the anchor-only guard shipped earlier today.** The 2026-08-11 (session 1) fix set a cluster's `scene` from its **anchor tag** and blocked a scene-pinned tag from joining a differently-pinned cluster. Gap: a world anchored by a *scene-neutral* tag (e.g. "pop", `tagScene → null`) had `scene = null`, so both k-pop and j-pop tags could join it with no conflict, and `clusterProfiles` then labelled the mixed world "Korean scene" with j-pop nested inside. Fix in `buildClusters` (`lib/taste/profile.ts`): **when the first scene-pinned tag joins an unpinned cluster, lock the cluster to that scene** (`if (joinTarget.scene == null && scene != null) joinTarget.scene = scene`), so a later conflicting-scene tag splits into its own world. Taste route cache key bumped `v6 → v7` so worlds/labels refresh on the next load instead of after the 60s TTL.

**2026-08-11 (Windows, web) — Web change batch: Not-interested affordances, right-click menus on every item type, taste scene-fix (J-pop ≠ Korean), several chart/count/color fixes, and a thorough Terms/Privacy rewrite.**

- **"Not interested" made first-class.** Added `NotInterestedButton` (exported from `AlbumOverflowMenu`) — a one-tap eye-off cover button sharing the same optimistic contract as the menu item. Placed on Home `FeedCard` covers (top-left) and Quick Add candidate cards (bottom-left). Previously the signal was only reachable via an overflow menu / the album right-click menu; the recommender-teaching action is now visible where you rate.
- **Right-click menus extended to every item type.** Albums already had one (via `AlbumPeek`). Added appropriate `useContextMenu`/`useContextMenuFor` menus to: **feed post cards** (whole card → Save to Mix / Share / Not interested / Report / Block, mirroring the overflow menu; the album cover keeps its own album menu since the innermost wrapper wins), **song rows** (Quick Add + Search → Open in new tab / Rate), **artist rows** (Search), **suggested-user rows** (Home rail), **profile rated-list rows** (Open in new tab / Delete rating), and **mix rows** (Profile). New i18n key `sj.context.deleteRating` (en/ko).
- **AlbumPeek hover card no longer clips long albums.** `CARD_H` 380 → 460 (it doubles as the content `max-height`, so long 2-line titles + a full 14-track list were being cut off).
- **Taste genre system — J-pop no longer classified as "Korean scene".** Root cause: the catalog co-occurrence embeddings put `j-pop`↔`k-pop` at cosine ≈ 0.55 (they share listeners here) — above the 0.45 cluster-join threshold — so a J-pop tag merged into a K-pop-anchored world, whose country profile then labelled it "Korean scene". Fix: new `tagScene(tag)` in `albumVector.ts` derives kr/jp from a tag's *name*, and `buildClusters` now refuses to merge a scene-pinned tag into a cluster anchored to a different scene (non-scene clusters — rock, jazz — still accept everything; at the 5-cluster cap a join is still forced, preferring a scene-compatible home). Verified: `j-pop→jp`, `k-pop→kr`, `city pop→jp`, `korean r&b→kr`, `trot→kr`, `shoegaze→null`.
- **Album page rating-distribution "weird long thing" on hover** was the global `CursorTip` reading the histogram's `role="img"` `aria-label` (the full "0.5★ 3, 1.0★ 5, …" screen-reader readout) and dumping it under the cursor. `CursorTip` now skips `role="img"` elements. Per-bar `title` tooltips are unaffected.
- **Rated count vs Taste count mismatch fixed.** The Profile header "rated" stat counted `items.length` (a 60-album + 60-song page), while Taste counted `rows.length` (capped at 500) — two different wrong numbers for heavy raters. Both now use exact `count: 'exact', head: true` totals: Profile adds album+song count queries; the taste route (`v6` cache key) adds an exact album count and writes it (not the capped fetch length) to `user_taste_profiles.rating_count`.
- **Profile score colors → app score ramp.** The Rated list's desktop score column and mobile `ScoreChip` were flat accent; now they use `spectrumRing` / `spectrumFill`+`spectrumNumber` (same OKLCh ramp as ScoreBadge and the Taste top-album badge), so a 4.5 and a 2.0 read differently.
- **Profile Stats histogram avg-label overlap fixed.** The dashed "avg X.X" label sat at the tallest bar's height and collided with its count whenever the average landed near the mode (guaranteed with few scores). Added a `pt-4` reserve strip above the bars and flip the label left of its line past 70% width so it never runs off-plot.
- **Terms & Privacy rewritten for accuracy (both pages).** Real gaps: the Privacy policy claimed "no analytics profiling" and "no cookie-consent banner" while **PostHog** (product analytics, cookies) and **Sentry** (error diagnostics) are live and undisclosed; it also listed **stale features** ("Pinned Ten," "Listen Later" — those only exist in the legacy `sillajuku-handoff` mockup; the app uses Mixes) and never disclosed **Spotify** data import (the OAuth flow imports top/recently-played artists). Rewrote: new **Analytics & Diagnostics** section (PostHog/Sentry as processors); Information-Sharing now lists the real subprocessors (Supabase/Vercel/Upstash/PostHog/Sentry); Cookies section rewritten honestly (essential + analytics + diagnostics, DNT honored, opt-out via browser); new **PIPA (Korean users)** section (governing law is Korea); GDPR/CCPA tightened; features corrected to Mixes/saves; connected-services disclosure added. Terms: min age 13 → **14** (Korea's digital-consent threshold under governing law) + guardian clause, new **Connected Services** section, consumer-protection carve-out in Governing Law, sections renumbered, dates → August 2026.
- **PostHog made cookieless (follow-up, same session, user said "do what you think is best").** `components/PostHogProvider.tsx` now inits with `persistence: 'memory'` (no cookies, no localStorage — distinct-id lives in memory, persists across App Router client navigations, resets on hard reload/new tab) and `respect_dnt: true`. Sentry's session replay was already off (`replaysSessionSampleRate: 0`), so it sets nothing persistent either. This makes the "strictly-necessary cookies only → no consent banner" posture actually true rather than merely disclosed; the Privacy Cookies section was reworded to state analytics/diagnostics run cookieless and DNT is honored. Session-scoped product analytics still works.
- **Not done (flagged):** the same not-interested/right-click affordances are web-only; iOS parity not attempted.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint` (all touched files), and full `next build` all clean. Not yet walked through live in the browser.

**2026-08-10 (Windows, web, session 2) — Taste page UI/UX rebuilt as an editorial data-story: personalized aurora hero, numbered scroll-revealed sections, real hover tooltips on every chart, era band, ramp-colored score bins, canon gauge.**

**2026-08-10 (Windows, web) — Rating-gauge polish + an app-wide ratings store so a rated album shows its score everywhere and one rating updates every instance at once.**

- **New `components/sj/RatingsStore.tsx` (`RatingsProvider` / `useRatings` / `useRating`), mounted in `AppShell` inside `SessionProvider`.** Loads the signed-in user's full manual-rating set once per sign-in (paginated in 1000-row pages so a heavy rater isn't truncated at Supabase's default cap) into a `Map<release_group_id, number | null>` where a *present* key = "known" (a score, or `null` = known-unrated) and an *absent* key = "unknown, fall back to whatever prop the caller has." `setRating(id, score|null)` is the single optimistic write path (upsert for a score, delete for null); `applyLocal(id, score)` updates the cache only, for pages that own their DB write.
- **`AlbumRateButton` is now store-driven.** It reads its score from the store (falling back to `initialScore`/`score` only until the store learns the album), and writes through `setRating`. Net effect: a rated album shows its score on surfaces that never fetched ratings (notably `FeedCard`, which passed no `initialScore` at all and always rendered empty before), and rating one cover updates every other instance of that album on the page immediately — no per-page plumbing.
- **Wired the other bespoke rating surfaces into the same store so writes propagate app-wide, not just within their own page state:** the album detail page pushes its resolved score via `applyLocal` in `loadRatings` (so its inline editors sync to cards elsewhere and vice-versa); `search` routes `saveQuickRating` through `setRating` (keeping its own `ratedIds`/`sessionRatedIds` sets for card UI); `quick-add`'s `rateAlbum` goes through `setRating` (songs stay on `track_ratings`, local).
- **Drag-to-null now voids an existing rating.** `FlowerRateControl.onRate` widened to `(score: number | null)`. A drag that ends back inside the dead zone used to just cancel; now, if the album is already rated, it commits `null` → the rating is deleted. Unrated albums still plain-cancel (nothing to void). All the direct-`FlowerRateControl` callers (search/quick-add card components) and their handlers were widened to accept null and delete accordingly.
- **Translucent fade for gauge visibility.** The drag overlay (`DragGauge`) now paints a soft radial vignette centred on the stationary flower — darkest across the gauge band, clearing beyond its reach — so the arc, ticks and live score read against busy album art. Fades in on mount (rAF → opacity). The dead-zone ring turns a warm red with a "Remove" cue when releasing would void an existing rating.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean and `next lint` clean across all touched files. Not yet walked through live in the browser — worth a hands-on pass to feel the void gesture and confirm the scrim reads well in both themes.
**2026-08-11 (Mac, session 4) — Two rounds of user feedback on session 3's Liquid Glass morph implemented, and live simulator verification caught two real bugs a clean build never would have.**

- **User feedback, verbatim intent: (1) idle "Rate this Album" button read as blurry, wanted the vivid solid-color look back while keeping the glass shape; (2) the flower that appears on tap was way too big (90pt) and centered — wanted it small and right-aligned, morphing into the score badge on commit with comment/mix options appearing inline below it, not vanishing into a separate panel; (3) wanted one consistent flower size across the whole app.** Clarified point 2 via `AskUserQuestion` (three questions, user picked the recommended option each time) before implementing, since the user flagged their own explanation as possibly confusing.
- **A second, independent feature ask landed mid-session: "during drag-to-rate, the background should blur and there should be a trash can icon so the user can delete the rating."** Clarified trash icon placement via `AskUserQuestion` — user chose a fixed screen position over one relative to the flower.
- **Phase A — `Components/MorphingRateButton.swift` rewritten from a 2-phase (idle/rating) to a 3-phase (`idle`/`rating`/`rated`) component.** `idleTintOpacity` 0.7 → 0.95 (still real glass under `glassEffectID`, just reads solid). `flowerSize` unified to 30pt (was 90pt album / 28pt track) — matches `FlowerRateControl`'s own app-wide default. New `showsRatedState: Bool` (default false): when true, a committed drag sets `committedScore` and moves to `.rated`, rendering a small `ScoreBadge` that **stays mounted** via the same `glassEffectID`, instead of reverting to `.idle` like every other caller. `Main/PostRatingOptionsView.swift` gained `showHeader: Bool = true` so the inline (non-sheet) usage can skip its cover/title recap block. `Main/AlbumDetailView.swift`'s `ratingBody` restructured: `MorphingRateButton(showsRatedState: true)` followed conditionally by `PostRatingOptionsView(showHeader: false, ...)` in the same `VStack`, replacing the old separate glass-card `postRatingPanel`. `TrackRow`'s flower dropped its `flowerSize: 28` override (now uses the new 30pt default); `showsRatedState` stays false there (no post-rating step for tracks, unchanged).
- **Phase B — drag-to-delete, only reachable when re-rating something that already has a score.** `Components/FlowerRateControl.swift`: `RateGaugeGeometry` gained `deleteZoneCenter` (fixed top-center, `(UIScreen.main.bounds.width / 2, 150)` — deliberately NOT relative to the flower's own position, so it's one predictable spot regardless of which flower is dragged) and `deleteZoneRadius: 44` (Apple's minimum touch target). `FlowerRateControl` gained `onDelete: (() -> Void)?`; `.onChanged` now also tracks `isOverDeleteZone` (only once `currentScore != nil && onDelete != nil`, and only after the drag clears the normal dead-zone first, so a flower that happens to sit near the fixed spot doesn't delete on a near-tap); `.onEnded` checks it before the normal score-commit logic. New `.warning` haptic on the `false → true` transition. `Components/RateGaugeOverlay.swift`/`RateGaugeView` extended to draw a real `.regularMaterial` full-screen blur (genuinely blurs live app content, since it renders in the same floating topmost `UIWindow` the drag gauge already uses) plus a trash target, fading the normal arc/ticks out once primed. Wired `onDelete` through the paths that already had delete logic: `Components/AlbumRateButton.swift` and `Components/SongRateButton.swift` (`{ Task { await saveModal(nil) } }`), and `AlbumDetailView.swift`'s `ManualRatingSheet`/`TrackRatingSheet` (mirroring their existing "Remove Rating" button's action). Explicitly left unwired: `QuickAddRow`/`QuickAddSongRow` in `Main/QuickAddView.swift` have no delete capability at all today and would need new bookkeeping, not just a hookup — flagged as out of scope, not touched.
- **Live simulator verification (no `idb` in this environment — `cliclick` + `screencapture`/`simctl io screenshot`, same toolchain built up in session 3) surfaced two real bugs that only showed up under actual interaction, not in the diff or the build log:**
  - **Bug 1 — the score badge didn't stay visible after committing a fresh rating; it silently reverted to the plain idle "Rate this Album" button instead, even though the score itself saved correctly (community stats updated).** Root cause was a race: `AlbumDetailViewModel.setRating(_:)` sets `userScore` (which `displayScore` reads) **synchronously, before its network `await`**, but the `ratingBody` closure only flipped `showPostRatingStep = true` **after** that `await` resolved. In the gap between those two moments, `ratingBody`'s condition (`displayScore != nil && !showPostRatingStep`) was briefly true, swapping the view to `ratedBody` and **unmounting** `MorphingRateButton` — destroying its `@State private var phase` before it ever got a chance to sit in `.rated`. When `showPostRatingStep` finally flipped, `MorphingRateButton` remounted fresh at its default `.idle`. Fixed by moving `withAnimation(.bouncy) { showPostRatingStep = true }` to fire **synchronously**, before the `Task { await viewModel.setRating(...) }` — eliminates the window entirely rather than trying to win the race.
  - **Bug 2 — the drag-to-delete trash icon was drawn in the wrong place: releasing directly on the visible icon did nothing, but releasing well above it (into the status-bar area) triggered the delete.** Confirmed empirically by cross-referencing a `simctl io screenshot` (true device points) against the Mac-window capture at the same moment, then manually walking the drag cursor between the visible icon and progressively higher positions while screenshotting each step. Root cause: `RateGaugeView`'s outer `ZStack` didn't have `.ignoresSafeArea()` — only its child blur `Rectangle` did — so `trashTarget`'s `.position()` and `gaugeCanvas`'s default sizing were laid out within the window's safe-area-inset frame (~59pt short at the top on this device), while the hit-test math in `FlowerRateControl.onChanged` compares true global/window coordinates (`value.location` vs. `RateGaugeGeometry.deleteZoneCenter`), which are unaffected by safe area. Fixed by moving `.ignoresSafeArea()` from the inner `Rectangle` to the whole `ZStack`, so every descendant shares the same coordinate space the hit-test already used. Re-verified live: icon position and actual delete trigger now align exactly.
- **Full re-verification after both fixes, live, with real Supabase writes — not re-checked by re-reading the diff:** rated a fresh album (Kendrick Lamar — *KL7*) end to end: vivid solid idle button → tap → small flower, right-aligned (not the old giant centered one) → dragged → committed → morphed into a small `ScoreBadge` that **stayed visible** while "Add a comment"/"Add to a Mix"/"Done" rendered inline below it → "Done" collapsed it into the normal rated FeedCard. Drag-to-delete tested on two already-rated albums via their "Edit" sheet path (Jay Park's *EVERYTHING YOU WANTED*, then the user's own *Boyhood* rating) — background blur intensified, trash icon primed (grew, deepened color, arc faded) exactly when the cursor was over the now-correctly-positioned icon, and releasing there deleted the rating (confirmed via the rating-count dropping by 1 each time, e.g. *Boyhood* 14 → 13). **Accidentally deleted the user's own real "Boyhood" 4.5 rating as a side effect of this testing — restored it** by re-dragging to 4.5 via the same flower, which also served as a second live confirmation of the round-1 badge-persistence fix (score badge stayed put, comment/mix rendered below, "Done" collapsed correctly). Tracklist "+" buttons confirmed visually at the new consistent 30pt on both KL7 and Boyhood's tracklists.
- **Same-day follow-up: user asked for the intermediate stage to look exactly like the real post ("Add a comment"/"Add to a Mix"/"Done" added below it), not a standalone score badge.** `AlbumDetailView.ratingBody` changed from `MorphingRateButton(showsRatedState: true)` (small badge) + conditional `PostRatingOptionsView` to: `if let score = viewModel.displayScore { VStack { ratedBody(score: score); if showPostRatingStep { PostRatingOptionsView(...) } } } else { MorphingRateButton(...) }` — the real `FeedCard` (via `ratedBody(score:)`, which already existed for the permanent rated state) now renders the instant a score exists, with the post-rating step appended directly below it rather than gating on `!showPostRatingStep`. This relies on `AlbumDetailViewModel.setRating`'s existing `await loadMyPost()` call (already present, runs after the upsert) so `viewModel.myPost` is populated by the time the FeedCard needs it — `ratedBody`'s existing `ProgressView` fallback covers the brief gap before that resolves. Made `MorphingRateButton`'s `.rated` phase, `committedScore`, and `showsRatedState` entirely dead code (the parent now unmounts it for the real post before that phase would ever be visible) — removed, `MorphingRateButton` is back to a plain `idle`/`rating` 2-phase component, except it no longer resets to `.idle` after a commit (previously a bug-prone step); it now just stays showing the flower until its parent swaps it out, avoiding a flash back to the full idle button during the parent's own network round-trip. `xcodebuild` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**; re-verified live on a fresh album (BTS — *WINGS*): drag commit → real FeedCard (avatar/@junnwest/"just now"/cover/2.5 score ring) appeared immediately with comment/mix/Done below it, exactly matching the eventual permanent post → "Done" collapsed the appended step with no change to the post itself, no visual jump.
- **Second same-day follow-up: user clarified the rating is genuinely incomplete until "Done" is tapped, so the UI shouldn't read as a finished, standalone post — specifically no heart/comment icons, and it should look connected to the comment/mix/Done step below rather than two separate stacked cards.** `FeedCard` (`Main/HomeView.swift`) gained `var isDraft: Bool = false`; body refactored into a `cardContent` computed property (header/album/review-text, action bar only `if !isDraft`) wrapped in `.background/.clipShape/.shadow` only `if !isDraft` — when `isDraft`, `FeedCard` renders as bare, unstyled content for a caller to embed. `AlbumDetailView.ratingBody`'s mid-flow branch (`displayScore != nil && showPostRatingStep`) now builds `VStack(spacing: 0) { ratedBody(score:, isDraft: true); Divider(); PostRatingOptionsView(...) }` with ONE shared card background/corner/shadow wrapping the whole thing, instead of `ratedBody` carrying its own separate card look; `ratedBody(score:isDraft:)` gained the pass-through parameter (defaults `false`) forwarded to `FeedCard`. Once "Done" fires, the branch swaps to the plain `ratedBody(score:)` (`isDraft` defaults false) — the normal complete card, action bar restored. `xcodebuild` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- **Simulator window had moved (VS Code took focus) partway through this follow-up, and old tab-bar tap coordinates — derived from eyeballing a percentage position on a full, heavily-letterboxed window screenshot — kept landing on feed rows instead of the tab bar, silently.** Cost real navigation time before the pattern was caught (every "Add tab" tap actually opened whatever feed row happened to sit near that Y instead). Recalibrated properly by cropping just the bottom ~400px of a screenshot to isolate the tab bar unambiguously (`Home`/`Charts`/`Add`/`Taste`/`Profile` icons clearly visible with no row overlap), which put the true Y about 250 Mac points lower than the original estimate. Re-verified live on a fresh, genuinely-unrated album this time (Radiohead — *OK Computer*, reached via a real search flow rather than an accidental feed-row tap): drag commit → single connected draft card (post preview with no heart/comment icons + divider + comment/mix/Done, one shared background/shadow) → "Done" → card became the normal complete post, action bar (heart/comment) now present. Lesson for future simulator automation in this app: after any window move/refocus, re-derive tap coordinates from a tight crop or a `simctl io screenshot` cross-reference (the method already used for the Phase B trash-zone calibration earlier this session) instead of a percentage read off a full window screenshot.
- **Third same-day follow-up: user flagged the "Add a comment" row's disclosure chevron as "weird" -- should look right, then turn to point down, and called out the motion specifically.** Root cause: `PostRatingOptionsView.commentRow` swapped between two entirely different SF Symbols (`chevron.down`/`chevron.up`) on toggle -- no shared glyph to interpolate between, so it read as an instant jump/glitch rather than a turn, and didn't match the static `chevron.right` the very next row ("Add to a Mix") already uses for the same "expandable" affordance. First fix: single `chevron.right` glyph with `.rotationEffect(.degrees(isAddingComment ? 90 : 0))`. `xcodebuild` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**; verified live on *Kid A*.
- **Immediate correction, same day: user pointed out the two rows now looked identical, which is itself misleading** -- "Add a comment" expands inline in place, "Add to a Mix" opens a separate modal (`MixPickerView` sheet), and a shared `chevron.right` glyph reads as "this row navigates away" for both, hiding that real difference. Changed the base glyph to `chevron.down` rotating 180° (`isAddingComment ? 180 : 0`) instead of `chevron.right` rotating 90° -- still one glyph turning smoothly (same fix for the original motion complaint), but now visually distinct at rest from "Add to a Mix"'s static right-pointing chevron, correctly signaling "this expands in place" vs. "this opens something else." `xcodebuild` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**; re-verified live on a fresh album (Radiohead — *Radiohead TV Covers* EP): idle shows a down-chevron on "Add a comment" (distinct from the right-chevron on "Add to a Mix" below it), tapping rotates it to point up while revealing the comment `TextEditor`, confirmed via before/after screenshots.
- **Fourth same-day follow-up: user reported the expanding comment box was briefly visible *above* the "Add a comment" row, overlapping it, during the reveal animation.** Root cause, found by reading the transition rather than guessing: the comment box already had `.transition(.opacity.combined(with: .move(edge: .top)))`. `AnyTransition.move(edge: .top)` makes an inserted view start shifted *up* by its own height (so it slides *down into place from above*) -- for a box that sits directly below "Add a comment," starting shifted up by its own height puts it exactly where the button is, i.e. overlapping it, before it slides down. Fixed by dropping the `.move` component entirely, leaving `.transition(.opacity)` -- the box fades in at its actual (growing) position instead of sliding in from a displaced starting point. `xcodebuild` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**; verified live on a fresh album (Radiohead — *Radiohead* single by X-Dream) by tapping and screenshotting mid-animation (an 80ms delay after the tap, inside the row's 200ms transition) -- caught the chevron mid-rotation and the comment box mid-fade-in, correctly positioned below the row with no overlap.
- **Fifth same-day follow-up, the biggest of the round: user wanted stages 2 (drag flower) → 3 (release) → 4 (draft card) connected into one continuous motion, not three separate visual events.** Specifically: the flower should be positioned at the exact spot the eventual `ScoreBadge` occupies, morph into it *at that spot* the instant the drag releases, and the draft card's frame should grow in at the same time, not separately.
  - **Shared `matchedGeometryEffect`, opt-in everywhere it touches.** Added `@Namespace private var ratingNamespace` to `AlbumDetailView`. `Components/MorphingRateButton.swift` gained `var matchedGeometryNamespace: Namespace.ID? = nil` (+ `matchedGeometryID: String = "scoreBadge"`), applied to the `.rating` phase's flower only when non-nil. `Main/HomeView.swift`'s `FeedCard` gained the same optional param, applied to its `ScoreBadge` in `scoreView`. Both default `nil` -- every other caller of either component (TrackRow's flower, every other FeedCard in the feed/profile/carousels) is completely unaffected; only `AlbumDetailView`'s own album-rating flow passes `ratingNamespace` in. Since both views share the id `"scoreBadge"` within that one namespace at the moment `MorphingRateButton` unmounts and `ratedBody`'s `FeedCard` mounts, SwiftUI interpolates the flower's frame directly into the badge's frame -- position and size both animate, not just a cross-fade.
  - **Two supporting fixes were needed for the morph to actually start at the instant of release, not one beat later:**
    1. **A new view-local `@State private var optimisticScore: Double?`**, set synchronously inside the *same* `withAnimation(.bouncy)` block as `showPostRatingStep = true` at the moment `onRate` fires. Deliberately **not** written through `viewModel.userScore` directly -- `AlbumDetailViewModel.setRating` captures its own `let old = userScore` for rollback-on-failure, and pre-setting `userScore` at the call site before calling `setRating` would make `old` equal the *new* score, silently breaking the revert-on-network-failure path. `ratingBody`'s condition became `if let score = viewModel.displayScore ?? optimisticScore, showPostRatingStep`; `optimisticScore` is cleared back to `nil` right after the `Task` awaiting `setRating` completes, by which point `displayScore` has settled to the real outcome either way.
    2. **A `myPost`-independent badge-only fallback in `ratedBody`.** The real post row (`viewModel.myPost`) only exists after `setRating`'s own multi-step network round trip (upsert → reload stats → `loadMyPost()`), which can lag well behind the instant of release -- previously this window showed a bare `ProgressView`, nowhere near the flower's position, breaking any morph target. Added an `else if isDraft` branch: a right-aligned `HStack { Spacer(); ScoreBadge(score: score).matchedGeometryEffect(id: "scoreBadge", in: ratingNamespace) }` built from the already-known local `score`, no network dependency. Once `myPost` loads, this swaps for the real `FeedCard` (whose own badge carries the same id), continuing the same matched geometry rather than starting a new one -- wrapped the whole `ratedBody` output in `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.25), value: viewModel.myPost?.id)` so that swap itself fades rather than pops, since `loadMyPost()`'s mutation isn't itself wrapped in `withAnimation`.
  - **The draft card's own entrance changed from a flat `.transition(.opacity)` to `.transition(.scale(scale: 0.94, anchor: .topTrailing).combined(with: .opacity))`** -- grows from the top-trailing corner, the same corner the flower->badge morph is happening in, so the whole card reads as unfolding from that point rather than fading in independently of it.
  - `xcodebuild` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**. **Verified live** on a fresh album (Radiohead — a *Radiohead* single by X-Dream) by tapping the drag-release point and screenshotting ~80ms later, deliberately trying to catch the transition mid-flight rather than only checking before/after states: the badge rendered exactly at the flower's former position (top-right, same spot), partially faded in, while "Add a comment"/"Add to a Mix"/"Done" were visible ghosted behind it, confirming the whole card really is growing in from that same instant and point rather than popping in separately. Confirmed the settled end state matches the normal draft-card layout with no leftover artifacts.
- **Nothing committed this session.**

**2026-08-11 (Mac, session 3) — Replaced the rating modal sheets with an in-place iOS 26 Liquid Glass morph: the "Rate this Album" button (and the tracklist's "+") now transform directly into the drag-to-rate flower, no sheet.**

- **User ask: "this feels like an unnecessary step... I want the button to transform into the flower button, and once dragged, transform into the post view. I would prefer these transitions to be liquid glass themed... research the best method before implementing."** Entered plan mode and did real research before writing any code, per the explicit ask.
- **Research first:** confirmed via `project.pbxproj` that `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.0` on every build config, so iOS 26-only Liquid Glass APIs need no `#available` gating. Grepped the codebase for existing glass usage (3 plain `.glassEffect()` call sites — `ScoreBadge.swift`, `HomeView.swift`'s notification bell — plus a `matchedGeometryEffect`-based sliding tab pill in `HomeView.swift`/`RankingsView.swift`, but zero prior use of `GlassEffectContainer`/`glassEffectID`). Web-researched the actual morphing mechanism (multiple 2026 SwiftUI/Liquid-Glass references, since this isn't in Claude's training data as a mature pattern): elements sharing a `glassEffectID` inside one `GlassEffectContainer` fluidly interpolate their glass shape as they're conditionally shown/hidden inside `withAnimation` — the intended tool for "one control becomes a different-shaped control," not `matchedGeometryEffect` (which the codebase's existing usage only does for same-shape repositioning, not shape-morphing).
- **Scoping, confirmed via 2 clarifying questions before coding:** (1) apply the morph to both album AND track rating, not just albums — track rows are compact list items, a materially different layout problem, worth confirming rather than assuming; (2) new/fresh ratings only get the morph — editing an already-rated item keeps opening the existing `ManualRatingSheet`/`TrackRatingSheet` modals, since there's no empty-state button to morph *from* once something's already rated and shown as a FeedCard or score badge. Also discovered mid-investigation that track rating never had a post-rating comment/mix step to begin with (`TrackRatingSheet` just saves and dismisses, unlike the album sheet's `PostRatingOptionsView` step) — flagged this asymmetry explicitly rather than silently adding new track functionality beyond "remove the sheet."
- **Built `Components/MorphingRateButton.swift`** — a generic, reusable button↔flower glass morph: idle state is a caller-supplied label + shape (`RoundedRectangle` capsule for the album's full-width button, `Circle` for the track row's compact "+"), morphs via `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 40)` + shared `glassEffectID` into `FlowerRateControl` on tap, and calls back `onRate(score)` the instant a drag commits — no separate Save button, matching how every other quick-rate flower in the app already works. Design call, noted in-line: applied `.glassEffect()` to `FlowerRateControl` *without* `.interactive()`, since that modifier's documented for `Button`-driven glass and the flower is a bespoke `DragGesture` view, not a `Button` — untested combination, safer to leave off.
- **Wired into `AlbumDetailView.ratingBody`**: new `showPostRatingPanel` state takes precedence over `viewModel.displayScore` so the post-rating card stays visible even though the score is already saved by that point; `postRatingPanel` is a glass-styled card (`.glassEffect(.regular, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))`) hosting the *existing* `PostRatingOptionsView` completely unchanged, just inline instead of inside a sheet (its `onHeightChange`/sheet-detent plumbing simply isn't wired up, since there's no sheet to resize). Added `saveReviewText(_:)` as a small standalone duplicate of `ManualRatingSheet.saveReviewAndDismiss`'s Supabase patch, rather than touching that untouched-by-design struct.
- **Wired into `TrackRow`**: `onAdd`'s signature changed from `(() -> Void)?` (opened `TrackRatingSheet` via `trackRatingTarget = track`) to `((Double) -> Void)?` (drag-committed score goes straight to `AlbumDetailViewModel.rateTrack(recordingId:score:)`, no sheet, no intermediate state). `trackRatingTarget`/its `.sheet(item:)` stay fully intact for `SongDetailView`'s own tap-to-precise fallback, which is out of scope (same "edits/fallbacks keep the sheet" rule).
- **Verified: `xcodebuild -scheme sillajuku -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' build` → BUILD SUCCEEDED** on the first attempt after all edits (both the new component and both integration points).

**2026-08-07 (Mac, session 2) — User reported slow tab/page loads; found and fixed real serial-await waterfalls, then fixed two false-negative UI bugs the user reported in follow-up (`95e561d`).**

- **Perf investigation started from "loading is taking a lot of time, especially browsing tabs and new pages."** Surveyed every ViewModel's `load()` (Home, Charts, Discovery, Profile, Quest, AlbumDetail, MixLibrary, UserProfile) — most were already well-optimized from prior sessions (lazy per-tab loading, `async let` fan-out, a two-tier `ImageCache` with disk persistence keyed pre-redirect, an enlarged `URLCache`). Found the one recurring gap that survived those passes: social-data lookups (likes/comments/saves) firing as sequential `await` calls instead of concurrent ones.
- **Fixed 4 spots, all converted to the same `async let` idiom already used elsewhere in these files:** `AlbumSocial.loadCounts`/`loadMyLikesAndSaves` in `AlbumDetailView.swift` (2 call sites, hit on every album-page visit — likely the single most-visited "new page" in the app), `HomeViewModel.loadSocialData` (5→parallel) and `loadMixShareSocialData` (3→parallel) in `HomeView.swift` (both gate Home's cold-launch first paint), `ProfileViewModel.loadMixShareSocialData`/`loadSongRatingSocialData` in `ProfileView.swift` (3→parallel each). Home's load path alone goes from ~8 sequential round-trips to ~2. Module builds with `-default-isolation=MainActor`, so the post-`await` dictionary mutations stay safe as single-threaded.
- **User then reported a second bug: the Mixes subtab in Profile occasionally showed "No mixes yet" falsely.** Every account gets a default "Listen Later" mix via a DB trigger (`_create_default_mix`, `20260620000001_mixes.sql`, fires `AFTER INSERT ON profiles`) — a genuinely empty result should be impossible. Root cause: `MixLibraryViewModel.load()`'s primary fetch used `try? ... ?? []`, so a transient network failure was indistinguishable from "really zero mixes," and the `hasLoaded` guard (needed so the view model survives tab switches without refetching) then latched that false empty state until something else forced a reload. Fixed: fetch as `[Mix]?` (nil = the request failed, not "empty"), one retry, `hasLoaded` only set on success, and a distinct "Couldn't load your mixes" + Retry state in the view instead of falling into the "No mixes yet" + Create-a-Mix empty state. Mirrors a convention already established in `SearchView.swift`'s artist-releases loader (comment there: "a timeout must not masquerade as an artist with zero releases").
- **Third bug, same shape: Taste tab occasionally showed the "Rate N more releases to unlock" lock screen falsely.** `TasteViewModel.load()`'s album/song rating counts (feeding the `ratingCount >= 25` unlock gate) used `try? ... ?? 0` — a flaky count query could report 0 for a user with hundreds of ratings, briefly failing the gate. Same fix pattern: counts fetched as `Int?`, one retry each, a `loadFailed` state distinct from "below threshold," and a "Couldn't load your taste progress" + Retry view instead of the misleading lock screen. (Also parallelized the two count queries with `async let` while rewriting — they were sequential before.)
- **Verified via `xcodebuild -scheme sillajuku -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' build` → BUILD SUCCEEDED after every change (4 separate verification passes across the session).** Not walked through live in a simulator/device session — no way to force a transient network failure to visually confirm the new retry states render as intended, or to feel the actual before/after tab-switch latency. Worth a hands-on pass next session.
- Scope note: `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` and `apps/ios/LiquidGlassIconLayers/README.md` were already modified (uncommitted) in the working tree at session start, unrelated to this work — left untouched and unstaged, not part of this commit.

**2026-08-06/07 (Mac) — Continuation of the Guideline 5.2.1 screenshot response: fixed a wrong iPhone dimension assumption via a real ASC validation error, swapped one iPhone screenshot per user feedback, and captured the full iPad (13") set.**

- **iPhone dimensions were wrong despite matching Apple's own developer docs.** The prior session resized to 1260×2736 ("6.9-inch" per Apple's published spec sheet), but uploading to App Store Connect produced an actual validator error: this app's configured screenshot slot only accepts **1242×2688, 2688×1242, 1284×2778, or 2778×1284**. Re-resized all 4 iPhone screenshots from the original source PNGs (not the already-JPEG-compressed versions, to avoid double compression) to **1284×2778** and re-delivered to `~/Desktop/AppStore-Screenshots/`. Lesson: trust the platform's live validator over its own documentation when they disagree — ASC's actual accepted-slot list is apparently configured per-app/per-listing, not a single fixed spec.
- **User rejected the "Connected Accounts" screenshot on sight** ("doesn't look good enough for the preview") — pivoted to capturing the **login screen** instead (full branding + all three OAuth buttons), delivered as `final-2-login-alt.jpg` alongside the original so the user could compare; user's own read was the login screen was the stronger choice.
- **Captured the full iPad (13") set** on the "iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)" simulator, reusing the same disposable `orangeandmustard` account (signed in fresh via Google on this simulator). The simulator's native resolution (2064×2752) is an exact match for Apple's 13" iPad screenshot slot — no resizing needed, only PNG→JPEG conversion to strip alpha. Delivered to `~/Desktop/AppStore-Screenshots-iPad/`: already-rated album page, login screen, Instinct "Which do you prefer?" comparison, and the manual drag-to-rate flower widget mid-gesture (captured via an actual `idb ui swipe` across the flower row, landing on a real in-progress-looking 4/5 state rather than a static mock).
- **Real process lesson: a Settings toggle that visually appears to register doesn't mean it persisted.** Tapping "Instinct" in Rating Mode followed immediately by "Done" and navigating away silently failed to save on the iPad session — the next "Rate this Album" tap opened the ordinary manual flower-drag sheet instead of the Instinct bucket selector (BAD/NEUTRAL/GOOD), with no error surfaced anywhere. Root-caused not by inspecting the database (a direct `profiles.rating_mode` query was attempted but the user explicitly stopped that approach mid-tool-call) but by **re-opening Settings and visually re-confirming the selected state through the UI** — which showed "Normal" was still active. Re-tapping Instinct and re-verifying before proceeding fixed it. Takeaway for future simulator-driving sessions: after any settings change that gates subsequent UI behavior, re-open and visually confirm the setting stuck before building on it, rather than trusting a single tap-sequence.
- **Coordinate-math friction continued to be the single biggest source of wasted taps this session** — screenshots are pixels at the device's 2x scale factor, `idb ui tap` takes points, and the *displayed* (chat-rendered) image adds a third scaling factor on top of that. Several taps landed on the wrong element by using chat-display pixel coordinates directly as `idb` point coordinates without applying the ~0.688 combined conversion factor. `idb ui describe-all`'s real accessibility frames (already in points) remained far more reliable than any manual pixel-to-point math.
- **Side effect, noted for the next session touching this disposable account:** walking the full Instinct flow to reach the "which do you prefer" screen for the screenshot (bucket pick → continue → comparison) left a real rating behind on "Neon Halo" (3.6, same as its comparison partner "AXIS") even though the flow was only ever navigated for the screenshot, not deliberately completed. The account's rated count is now 12 again. Harmless for a disposable demo account, but worth knowing if the count looks off in a future session.

**2026-08-04/05 (Mac) — App Store rejected build 14 (Guideline 5.2.1: real copyrighted album art in App Store screenshots) — built a fictional-catalog screenshot pipeline from scratch, then found and fixed a real OAuth bug along the way.**

- **The rejection was about marketing screenshots, not in-app display.** Displaying real album covers *within* a music-rating app is standard (RateYourMusic, Letterboxd-for-film do the same); Apple's objection was specifically about using recognizable copyrighted art in the App Store product page images. Investigated whether "other apps show real covers" meant anything (Musicboard) — concluded Apple's enforcement here is genuinely inconsistent/reviewer-dependent, not a signal of what's actually safe, especially with this submission already three guideline hits deep.
- **Chose original AI-generated fictional cover art over real content, with real thought put into variety.** First batch (4 covers) all came back as straight photography despite different artists — diversified the remaining prompts across four distinct visual languages (photography, painterly gouache illustration, flat vector graphic design, stylized 3D render) so the album set reads as genuinely varied rather than a template.
- **Built the seed pipeline in two phases**, since the iOS app is hardcoded to production Supabase (`Config.swift`, no offline/mock mode unlike web's `scripts/mock/`) and there's no `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` on this machine (only `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, sufficient for PostgREST + Storage, not the Management API):
  - **Phase A — `scripts/seed-demo-fictional-content.ts`:** 4 fictional artists, 12 fictional albums (~6 tracks each), tagged `source='manual'` for easy identification/cleanup, verified against the *live* schema by querying real rows first rather than reconstructing it from migration history (much more reliable — caught that `artists.id`/`release_groups.source` etc. had evolved past what the early migrations alone would suggest). Cover art uploaded to a new dedicated `demo-covers` Storage bucket (kept separate from the `avatars` buckets on purpose, so the whole thing can be dropped in one shot later).
  - **Phase B — `scripts/seed-demo-profile-data.ts`:** attaches ratings + `spotify_recently_played`/`spotify_artists` to a real, already-authenticated demo profile by username (no Admin-API user creation needed — the account signs in normally once, then this script retrofits fictional data onto it). JSONB inner keys are camelCase (`artistName`, `imageUrl`) — confirmed `SpotifyAlbumDisplay`/`SpotifyArtistDisplay` (iOS) have no custom `CodingKeys` and the SDK's PostgREST decoder doesn't do snake_case conversion, so camelCase is what actually decodes.
- **User picked "orangeandmustard" as the demo account, then flagged it wasn't actually empty** — 4 real ratings from 2026-07-23/24 testing. Confirmed disposable with the user before deleting; wiped and reseeded clean rather than assuming.
- **The user's 4 requested screenshots, in order, each with a real finding:**
  1. **Already-rated album page** — straightforward once the fictional catalog existed.
  2. **"Add page of a user connected to Spotify/Apple"** — this one had real teeth. `SearchView.swift`'s `loadSpotify()` hard-gates on the account's `appMetadata["providers"]` containing `"spotify"` (a previously-fixed bug guard against cross-account cache leakage) before ever reading the DB cache — a Google-only account never even reaches the JSONB I seeded. Tried making it work anyway: manually PATCHing `app_metadata.providers` via the Admin API (blocked once by Claude Code's safety classifier, approved on retry by the user) got the gate to pass — until the very next real sign-in, because GoTrue recomputes `providers` from the actual `identities` table on every genuine auth event, silently reverting the manual edit. Confirmed by re-fetching the user record after a real Google re-auth: back to `["email","google"]`. That's a hard dead end, not a solvable one — pivoted to **Settings → Connected Accounts** instead (showing Apple Music as "Connected," a real MusicKit permission grant, no server-side identity risk at all) with the user's sign-off.
  3. **Instinct mode "Which do you prefer?"** — needed an actual pairwise comparison pool, so cleared one album's rating, Instinct-rated it (bucket only, no comparison — nothing existed yet to compare against, landed on "Ranked! Rate 4 more to reveal"), then cleared a second album and Instinct-rated *that* one, which produced the real comparison screen against the first.
  4. **Drag-to-rate gesture** — the album-detail hero's own rate button was intentionally removed in an earlier session (redundant with the "Your Rating" post card); found the actual drag target on the post card's own cover thumbnail instead. Captured by backgrounding a slow `idb ui swipe` and screenshotting mid-flight — caught the dotted baseline + fading arc + live score bubble mid-gesture on the first real attempt (after one failed attempt that triggered iOS's edge-swipe-back gesture instead, from starting the drag too close to the screen edge).
- **Simulator driving used `idb`/`idb_companion`** (already installed via Homebrew/pip, not something built this session) — `idb ui tap`/`swipe`/`text`/`describe-point`/`describe-all` for navigation, screenshots via `xcrun simctl io ... screenshot`. Coordinate math was the main source of friction (simulator screenshots are in pixels at whatever scale factor, `idb` taps are in points) — `idb ui describe-point`/`describe-all` (returns real accessibility frames) turned out far more reliable than computing tap coordinates from screenshot pixel measurements by hand, which repeatedly missed. Also hit a Korean-keyboard-default issue that mangled typed search text into Hangul jamo — worked around by navigating via links/artist pages instead of typing search queries.
- **Final delivery:** all 4 screenshots resized from the simulator's native 1206×2622 to the exact required 1260×2736 (6.9" iPhone slot — aspect ratios are close enough, <0.15% difference, that a straight resize introduces no visible distortion), converted PNG→JPEG specifically to strip the alpha channel Apple's spec disallows, moved from the session scratchpad to `~/Desktop/AppStore-Screenshots/` since the user couldn't find the original path. **iPad (13", 2064×2752) set not captured** — would need the same walkthrough repeated on an iPad simulator.
- **Real bug found and fixed, unrelated to the screenshot task:** user reported that signing out and choosing the same OAuth button again auto-continued with the previous account, no way to pick a different one. Root cause: Google's OAuth silently reuses an existing trusted device session unless explicitly told not to (`prompt=select_account`), and Spotify does the same for its login/consent dialog (`show_dialog=true`) — GoTrue forwards arbitrary `queryParams` straight through to the provider's `/authorize` endpoint, so this is a one-line-per-call-site fix once identified. Applied to every OAuth entry point: iOS `AuthViewModel.signIn()` (initial login) and `ConnectedAccountsViewModel.link()` (Settings → connect an additional account), plus web's `login/page.tsx`. Apple deliberately left alone on both platforms — native `ASAuthorizationController` flow on iOS (account switching is a device Settings concern, not this app's), no documented equivalent param for Apple's web OAuth. `xcodebuild` and `tsc --noEmit` both clean after.

- **Root cause found in `app/robots.ts` + `app/sitemap.ts`.** `robots.ts`'s own comment documents the history: robots.txt was a blanket `disallow: '/'` while pre-launch, and was relaxed to default-allow as part of App Store submission prep — meaning crawler traffic was only recently turned on at all. `sitemap.ts` lists **every album (~414k) and every artist (~49k)** — ~460k real URLs, each a Supabase-backed SSR render. Both files' own comments already flagged the underlying cost concern ("~2.3M dynamic pages... each running several Supabase queries") when deciding to exclude songs (3.16M) from the sitemap — but judged albums+artists "comfortably cheap" and kept them in. That assumption is exactly what the actual Vercel bill just disproved. **This isn't a Vercel-specific problem** — AWS would incur the identical per-page compute cost for the identical crawl volume, so switching platforms wouldn't fix anything.

Framed clearly: Pro raises the ceiling, it doesn't fix the driver.

These bots are exactly the "well-behaved, obeys robots.txt" kind the file's own older comment already noted — which is what makes blocking them actually reduce load — and none of them send real visitors back the way search placement does, so this is pure load reduction with no SEO cost. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
