**2026-07-18 (Mac) — App Store rejection fixed (Guideline 4, Sign in with Apple asking for the name).** Apple rejected the submitted build ("The app requires users to provide their name after using Sign in with Apple. This information is already provided by the Authentication Services framework."). Root cause: `OnboardingView` always included the `.name` step and merely *pre-filled* it from the OAuth metadata — Apple requires not asking at all. Fix: `steps` and the metadata lookup moved into `init` (was `onAppear` — steps must never change after first render); the name step now only exists when NO provider name is available (`full_name`/`name` metadata keys, same lookup as before), otherwise the provided name is used silently and stays editable in Edit Profile. Applies to all providers (Google/Spotify supply names too), which is both consistent and what the guideline wants. `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` bumped 6→7 for the resubmission. Verified on-sim via probe (signed-in user has name metadata → onboarding opens directly on "Create a username." with 4 dots); the empty-metadata fallback path still shows the name step by construction. **User actions for resubmission:** archive/upload build 7 (manual — no App Store Connect API key on this machine), and in App Store Connect reply to the rejection message noting the name step is now skipped when Sign in with Apple provides the name, then resubmit. Note the fix ships together with the whole uncommitted 2026-07-17 Instagram-share batch below.

**2026-07-17 (Mac) — Instagram share: optional photo/video background behind the share card. Uncommitted at write time (3 files: InstagramShare.swift, SharePreviewSheet.swift, Localizable.xcstrings).**

- User: when sharing a post to Instagram, give the option of adding a background photo or video behind the widget (the share card). Instagram's Stories pasteboard contract already supports this via `com.instagram.sharedSticker.backgroundImage` / `.backgroundVideo` — the sticker rides on top of the user's media instead of the flat `backgroundTopColor`/`BottomColor` cream that was hardcoded before (those color keys now only apply when no background is picked).
- **`InstagramShare.swift`:** new `ShareBackground` enum (`.photo(UIImage, jpegData:)` / `.video(previewURL:, data:)` — carries both a previewable form and the raw pasteboard bytes, resolved once at pick time); `shareToInstagramStories(stickerImage:background:)` switches the pasteboard keys on it; new `composite(sticker:over:)` flattens the sticker over a photo backdrop at 1080×1920 (backdrop aspect-filled, sticker centered at 82% canvas width) so **Save to Photos / More Options export the same thing the Instagram handoff produces — for photos.** Video backdrops are deliberately Instagram-only (compositing video needs an AVFoundation export session — parked; Save/More export the card alone, footnoted in the UI).
- **`SharePreviewSheet.swift`:** "Add a background photo or video" pill under the card (PhotosPicker, `.any(of: [.images, .videos])` — same out-of-process picker EditProfileView already uses, no photo-library permission needed). Once picked, the flat card preview swaps to a 9:16 story mock: media aspect-filled (photos via `Image`, videos via a new `LoopingVideoView` — `AVPlayerLayer` + `AVPlayerLooper`, muted, `.resizeAspectFill`, because plain `VideoPlayer` letterboxes and shows controls), card overlaid at the composite's exact 82% relative width so preview == export. Change/Remove chips are **overlaid on the preview bottom** (black-45% capsules, white text) — first version put them below the preview and the 9:16 frame pushed them under the scroll fold, caught via screenshot. Same reason the video-only footnote sits at the *top* under the header hint, and previewWidth is 216pt (240 overflowed once the note line existed; and the narrower width made the original "Change background"/"Remove background" labels wrap → shortened to "Change"/"Remove"). Photos re-encode to JPEG 0.9 before the pasteboard so Instagram never sees HEIC; videos load as `Data` (temp-file copy for the player), capped at 100MB (a Story is ≤60s; a multi-hundred-MB pick would stall the pasteboard handoff), load failure shows an inline note.
- **ko strings** hand-added to `Localizable.xcstrings` (CLI builds don't sync the catalog): 배경 사진·영상 추가 / 변경 / 제거 + the load-failure and video-footnote lines. Kept the diff to +50 lines, no whole-file reformat.
- **Follow-up 6 (same day, user: "is it possible to change the dark/light mode of the widget on click?"): yes — tap the card to flip it.** The card is built entirely from adaptive color assets (sjCream/sjInk/sjSurface/…), so one forced `.environment(\.colorScheme,)` flips the whole thing. New `cardScheme` state (defaults `.light`, independent of the phone's appearance): the preview card gets the environment override + an `onTapGesture` toggle (0.2s ease animation), and `renderStickerImage` gained a required `colorScheme:` param (the sticker re-renders via `onChange(of: cardScheme)`, so Instagram handoffs and all composites automatically follow the pick — the export param also makes explicit what was previously implicit renderer-default traits). Verified dark render on-sim via `SJ_PROBE_DARKCARD` env probe (dark surface/white text/badge legible over the cream backdrop; the tap itself isn't CLI-testable but is a plain onTapGesture). Probe reverted, build clean. Discoverability note: the toggle is invisible until tapped — if users don't find it, a small sun/moon chip near the card is the obvious follow-up.
- **Follow-up 5 (same day, user: "the color selection modal is way too large. we don't have to give that much options"): system ColorPicker replaced with curated swatches.** The native `ColorPicker` opens Apple's full grid/spectrum/sliders/eyedropper sheet — far more control than a story backdrop needs. Solid page now shows 7 preset color dots (cream/ink/brand-blue/soft-pink/butter/terracotta/sage), Gradient page 6 preset top→bottom pairs (cream→blue default, peach→sunset, indigo→teal, night, sky→deep-blue, pink→periwinkle), rendered as 22pt circles in the same black-45% capsule, tap-to-apply with a white selection ring (shared `swatchRow` helper). `Color` equality drives the ring, which works because selections only ever come from the same static preset instances. "Top"/"Bottom" xcstrings keys deleted with the wells. Both rows verified on-sim via probe (reverted).
- **Follow-up 4 (same day, user): header hint removed, preview + card enlarged.** Dropped the "This is what gets exported…" hint (key deleted from xcstrings) and gave the carousel its space: previewWidth 216→248. Card enlarged from 72%→78% of canvas width — in **both** the preview scale and `InstagramShare.composite`, so preview still equals export. The two conditional notes that lived under the hint (video-applies-to-Instagram, media-load-failed) became overlay capsules pinned to the top of the photo page itself (`pageNote`, black-45% rounded rect, white text) — they're photo-page-specific anyway, and keeping them out of the layout keeps every page a fixed height with no fold overflow in any state. Verified solid + video states on-sim via probe (reverted).
- **Follow-up 3 (same day, user: "we should build export to reels and posts as well if possible. look into it"): Reels + feed-post export built.** Researched Meta's current docs first (WebSearch/WebFetch — gstack `/browse` still not installed on this Mac): **Reels** has an official pasteboard handoff mirroring Stories (`instagram-reels://share`, `com.instagram.sharedSticker.backgroundVideo` REQUIRED — Reels are video-only by API design, no color/image keys exist — plus optional `stickerImage` + the same app ID; video 3–60s, H.264/H.265, ≤50MB recommended, enforced by Instagram not pre-validated by us). **Feed posts** have no pasteboard API; the documented route is Document Interaction: JPEG written with `.igo` extension + UTI `com.instagram.exclusivegram` (the `.ig`/`com.instagram.photo` variant would offer all Instagram-capable apps) opens the feed composer; photo-only. Implementation: `InstagramShare.canShareToInstagramReels`/`shareToInstagramReels`; new `InstagramFeedShare` (NSObject singleton holding the `UIDocumentInteractionController` alive for the interaction — it dies with the tap otherwise — presenting from the key window's root VC); `composite`/`gradientImage` gained a `canvas` param + new `postCanvas` 1080×1350 (4:5, Instagram's tallest feed ratio — handing the 9:16 canvas over would just get force-cropped) with a `postExportImage` computed on the sheet; `instagram-reels` + `instagram` added to `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes`. UI: the second Instagram button **swaps with the background type** (video → "Share to Instagram Reels", static → "Share as Instagram Post") instead of stacking, and Save/More merged into one two-up row, so the button stack stays 3 rows tall. ko added for both new buttons **and backfilled for the previously-untranslated "Share to Instagram Story"**. Verified both button layouts on-sim via the probe with a `SJ_PROBE_IG=1` gate-force (sim has no Instagram; handoffs themselves untestable here). **Parked:** Reels for static backgrounds would need synthesizing a 3s+ video from a still (AVAssetWriter) — noted as follow-up if wanted.
- **Follow-up 2 (same day, user spec): background rework — swipeable carousel, no "Remove", camera option.** User: removing the background shouldn't be an option; instead 4 customizable background styles swiped through like a carousel — solid color (customizable), gradient (customizable), blurred album cover, photo — and the photo page's Change button should drop down with "take a new photo / choose from gallery". Implementation: new `ShareBackgroundStyle` carousel (a `TabView(.page)` of 9:16 story mocks, custom dots + page-title row below since the built-in index dots would collide with the per-page control chips; the old picked-media enum renamed `PickedShareMedia`, the old "no background" state deleted). Solid/gradient pages carry `ColorPicker` wells (defaults: cream #F8F8F5, gradient cream→sjBlue; **fixed cream, not adaptive `Color.sjCream`** — the exported story must not vary with the phone's dark mode) and hand off through Instagram's native `backgroundTopColor`/`BottomColor` keys, which render a real vertical gradient when they differ — no image needed. Blurred Cover: `InstagramShare.blurredCoverBackdrop` (cover aspect-filled to 1080×1920, `clampedToExtent` + gaussian sigma 60, precomputed off-main in a `.task`); preview approximates it with SwiftUI `.blur(12)` + 1.15 overscale (sigma 60 at 1080px ≈ 12pt at the 216pt preview; the overscale hides the blur's faded edges). Photo page: `Menu` dropdown → "Take a Photo" (new `CameraCaptureView`, bare `UIImagePickerController`, **new `NSCameraUsageDescription` in Info.plist**; entry hidden where no camera, e.g. simulator) / "Choose from Gallery" (`.photosPicker` modifier, still images+videos). New resolved-handoff enum `StoryBackground` (.colors/.image/.video); `shareToInstagramStories` takes it non-optionally (always a background now) with a new `hexString` UIColor→"#RRGGBB" helper; **Save/More now export the full 1080×1920 composite for every style** (solid/gradient via new `gradientImage`) except video (still card-only + footnote). ko added: 단색/그라데이션/커버 블러/사진·영상/위/아래/사진·영상 추가/사진 촬영/갤러리에서 선택; obsolete keys ("Add a background photo or video", "Remove") deleted. (User follow-up "no videos?" — videos were always supported through the gallery path, but the page/chip labels said "Photo"/"Add Photo" and hid it; renamed to "Photo & Video" / "Add Photo or Video".) Verified on-sim via the same env probe extended to `SJ_PROBE_BG=solid|gradient|cover|photo|photo-empty`: all 5 states screenshotted correct (wells legible on the media, dots/title under the carousel, everything above the fold). **Not verifiable on sim:** actual swipe gesture (same standard TabView paging as everywhere), camera flow (no sim camera), Instagram handoff. One localization gotcha fixed in review: `Text(condition ? "A" : "B")` with string literals resolves to `String` not `LocalizedStringKey` — silently skips localization; wrapped both branches in `String(localized:)`.
- **Follow-up (same day, user on-device feedback): baked-in card shadow removed.** The sticker PNG carried `ShareCardView`'s `.shadow(0.18, radius 18, y 8)` + the 24pt padding that existed only to keep it from clipping at the export bounds — over a real photo/video it "looks weird" (a static shadow direction can't match the backdrop's lighting). Both removed; the sticker's natural width is now 320 (was 368), so `composite`'s canvas factor and the preview's `scaleEffect` moved 0.82→0.72 to keep the visible card size identical (0.82 × 320/368). Verified on-sim via the same probe (card renders flat over the photo backdrop, same size), probe reverted again, build clean.
- **Verified on-sim** (iPhone 17 Pro) via a temp env-driven probe (`SIMCTL_CHILD_SJ_PROBE=share` → ShareProbeView presenting the sheet with dummy data; `SJ_PROBE_BG=photo` seeded a gradient, `SJ_PROBE_BG=video` + `SJ_PROBE_BG_PATH` seeded a real 3s H.264 clip recorded off the simulator itself with `simctl io recordVideo`): default state (pill under card), photo state (backdrop filled, card centered, chips legible), video state (clip actually playing aspect-filled behind the card, footnote visible at top). 3 layout iterations caught by screenshots (chips below fold → overlay; footnote below fold → top; chip labels wrapping → shortened). Probe fully reverted (`sillajukuApp.swift` via git checkout, SharePreviewSheet block edited out), final build clean. **Not verifiable from here:** the actual Instagram handoff with a background (no Instagram on the simulator — the pasteboard keys are Meta's documented contract, and the existing sticker handoff was device-confirmed back on 2026-07-08) and the PhotosPicker interaction itself (out-of-process). Worth one real-device tap-through with Instagram installed before the next App Store build.

**2026-07-19 (Windows) — 18-item web change list kicked off: gauge redesign + OKLCh score ramp, shared loading vocabulary, raw-ID flash, "Go to charts", "Not interested" + the shared overflow menu, right-click menus, bookmark-icon unification, album-page flower rating (row + cover button), the mix-page bug, grouped artist discography, the Stats-tab rebuild, @username-first identity. 13 items touched, 12 finished.** The list itself was handed over as a prompt doc and is now persisted (with a per-item status board) as `WEB_CHANGE_PROMPTS.md`. Worked in the stated dependency order — #2 and #12 first because the rest consume them, then #1 because #3 and #17 need its menu, then #5 with #16 in the same pass since both are album-page rating surfaces that have to agree. `tsc --noEmit` + `next lint` + `next build` clean; nothing browser-verified. #1's migration was applied to the hosted Supabase project later the same day.

- **#2 gauge redesign (`components/sj/FlowerRateControl.tsx`).** The old design hid the flower during the drag and drew five concentric rings plus a dashed line to the cursor. Now: the **flower stays visible and stationary**, and the gauge anchors to the button's `getBoundingClientRect()` centre rather than the press point (so it doesn't shift depending on where on the glyph you pressed). The rings are replaced by a **single thin arc** at the current score's radius, centred on the cursor's angle, spanning 52° — built from 22 short line segments with a `sin(t·π)^1.4` opacity falloff, which fades it out along its length without needing gradient coordinates in arc space. Underneath it, a **dotted horizontal baseline** with ticks at each whole star, drawn as *two* halves starting at the dead-zone edge so nothing crosses the flower. The score **reveals in place over the flower** — the glyph fades and shrinks to 0.82, the number fades up from scale 0.6 on a `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` overshoot — replacing the floating readout that used to track the cursor. **Layout gotcha worth remembering:** the glyph and the number are stacked via CSS grid (`grid place-items-center` + both children on `gridArea: '1 / 1'`) rather than `relative`/`absolute inset-0`, because several call sites (`FeedCard`, artist page, charts) pass their own `absolute bottom-1 right-1 …` through `className` and a `relative` on the base would have fought it. Radii recalibrated for the 0.1 scale: `OFFSET` 44→36 dead zone, `STEP` 52→34 px/star, full 0.5→5.0 sweep at ~206px, ~3.4px per tenth; `distanceToScore` now rounds to **0.1**, not 0.5. Tap→precise-modal, dead-zone-release→cancel, pointer capture and `touch-action: none` all preserved.
- **#2 color ramp (`lib/sj/display.ts`).** The score spectrum was an HSL hue sweep (0°→205.7° at fixed S/L), which is not perceptually uniform — the yellows blew out and the blues went muddy. Replaced with an **OKLCh ramp**: five hue/chroma anchors (deep red 25° → orange 58° → yellow-green 126° → teal 196° → blue 262°), linearly interpolated, rendered at a **fixed OKLab lightness per variant** — `spectrumFill` L .92 / chroma ×.28, `spectrumNumber` L .45 / ×.95, `spectrumRing` L .63. Added a full OKLab→linear-sRGB→gamma pipeline (Ottosson's matrices) and, for out-of-gamut colors, **walk chroma down by ×0.92 until it fits** instead of clipping channels — clipping would have destroyed exactly the lightness constancy the ramp exists for. Verified numerically: fill-vs-number luminance contrast stays **5.6–6.3 across all of 0.5–5.0**. New `spectrumColor(score, lightness, chromaScale)` export for gradient/chart consumers (#4's histogram, #6's heatmap). Function names unchanged, so `ScoreBadge` and every badge site picked it up at once. **Two side effects flagged:** `spectrumHue` now returns OKLCh degrees, not CSS HSL degrees (nothing external called it — verified by grep — but it would silently produce wrong colors if fed to `hsl()`); and **iOS `Components/ScoreBadge.swift` still runs the old HSL sweep**, so web and iOS badges no longer match — a new parity gap, left alone under the web-only rule.
- **#12 shared loading vocabulary (`components/sj/Loading.tsx`, new).** `FlowerSpinner` (rotating `icon-flower.svg`) and `PageLoader` for the no-known-layout case, plus skeleton primitives `Skeleton`, `SkeletonLine`, `SkeletonBlock`, `SkeletonCover`, `SkeletonCard`, `SkeletonCardGrid`, `SkeletonRows`. Everything animates through `animate-pulse`/`animate-spin` paired with the `motion-reduce:` variant, so `prefers-reduced-motion` yields a static placeholder. **Rollout is deliberately incomplete** — only album and artist are converted; roughly a dozen pages still hand-roll `animate-pulse` (taste, song, charts ×3, notifications, search, quick-add, post, home, `ProfileView`, `ProfileExtras`, `HeaderMenus`, `AlbumPeek`). Exact line references are listed in `WEB_CHANGE_PROMPTS.md` so the next session doesn't have to re-find them.
- **#11 raw ID during load.** The culprit was one expression: `artist/[id]/page.tsx` rendered `<h1>{name || rawId}</h1>`, and for a UUID route `name` initialises to `''`, so the bare UUID painted until the `artists` row resolved. Now renders a `SkeletonLine` when `name` is empty, with a skeleton circle standing in for the avatar and `SkeletonRows` replacing the tab body's bare `…` placeholder. **The album page turned out not to have the bug** — it early-returns a skeleton until `release` exists and never touches `params.id` in JSX (checked every use) — so it only got its hand-rolled skeleton rebuilt on the shared primitives.
- **#1 "Not interested" + the app's first reusable overflow (…) menu.** Until now the only feedback a user could give a recommended album was to rate it, so an album they never intend to hear came back forever — `NOT EXISTS (… ratings …)` was the only exclusion Quick Add had. New migration `apps/web/supabase/migrations/20260719000000_not_interested.sql`: `not_interested(user_id, release_group_id, created_at)` with a composite PK (so marking twice is a no-op upsert, not a PK violation), an owner-only `FOR ALL` policy in the wrapped-auth-call style (`(select auth.uid()) = user_id`) — deliberately **not** readable by other users, since "things I don't want" isn't social data — and a `CREATE OR REPLACE` of `get_quick_add_candidates` that re-issues 20260717000000's body verbatim plus a second `NOT EXISTS` against the new table. Signature/columns unchanged, so the server-side exclusion needs no client change. New `lib/sj/notInterested.ts` (`fetchNotInterestedIds` / `markNotInterested` / `unmarkNotInterested`) is best-effort by design: a missing table or an RLS refusal resolves to "nothing dismissed" rather than throwing, so an unmigrated environment degrades to client-side-only filtering instead of a dead feed. New `components/sj/AlbumOverflowMenu.tsx` splits into a `MoreHorizontal` button (styled to match `AlbumBookmarkButton`'s cover-overlay pill) and an exported **`OverflowMenuSurface`**, positioned from a plain viewport point rather than from the button — that split is what lets **#3's right-click menu reuse it at the cursor**. The surface portals to `document.body` (a menu opened inside a list row or an `overflow-hidden` cover would otherwise clip), clamps itself to both viewport edges, closes on outside-mousedown/Escape/scroll/resize, and defers registering the outside-click listener by one tick so the opening click doesn't immediately close it. Callers pass extra actions via `items`; **Not interested** is the built-in one and always renders last. Surfaced on **Quick Add** rows (bottom-right of the cover, opposite the bookmark) and in **Home explore**'s `FeedCard` menu (the existing inline menu got one more `MenuItem` rather than being swapped out — smaller diff, same result). Both surfaces filter at *render* against a `dismissed`/`notInterested` `Set` rather than splicing the fetched array, which keeps Quick Add's `albums.length`-based pagination offset honest. **Deliberate scope call:** the Following feed is *not* filtered — those are people you chose to follow, not a recommendation. i18n `sj.notInterested.{action,done,undo}` in en+ko (`done`/`undo` are unused for now — no toast was built; they're there for the undo affordance if the user wants one). `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint`, and `next build` all clean. **Migration applied 2026-07-19** to the hosted Supabase project with `npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/db-exec.ts supabase/migrations/20260719000000_not_interested.sql` (the Management API path — this machine has no direct DB URL; needs `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` in `apps/web/.env.local`). Verified afterwards: `not_interested` exists with `relrowsecurity = true`, 1 policy, 2 indexes (PK + release-group), and `get_quick_add_candidates`'s new body contains the `not_interested` exclusion. Dismissals now survive reload and Quick Add filters server-side.
- **#3 right-click context menus.** The point of the task was *not* to build a menu — #1 already shipped one — so `components/sj/ContextMenu.tsx` is deliberately thin: `useContextMenu(items)`, `useContextMenuFor(build)`, and a `<ContextMenu>` wrapper component, all of which capture `e.clientX/clientY` and hand them to #1's `OverflowMenuSurface`. Viewport clamping, the portal, and outside-click/Escape/scroll/resize dismissal are inherited, not reimplemented. Two decisions worth recording. (1) The handler calls `stopPropagation()`, so the **innermost** wrapper wins — a track row nested inside an album card opens the track menu only, instead of both firing as the event bubbles. (2) `wantsNativeMenu()` bails out (leaving the browser's own menu) over `input`/`textarea`/`select`/`contenteditable` and whenever there's a live non-collapsed text selection, because right-clicking a selection is essentially always "copy this". **Album covers were covered globally in one edit**: `AlbumPeek` already wraps every cover in the app (charts ×3, `charts/[slug]`, artist, search, home, Quick Add, `FeedCard`), so `useAlbumContextMenu` hangs off its *existing* root node — no new DOM that could disturb a cover's layout, and no per-page wiring. `AlbumContextMenu.tsx` is self-contained the way `AlbumRateButton` is: it owns the precise-rating modal, the mix picker, and its own `ratings` upsert/delete. It gained an optional `release` prop on `AlbumPeek` (passed where a full `SJRelease` was already in scope — FeedCard, search, artist; charts still synthesize one from display props, so their rating modal shows the generic "Release" type chip) and an `onNotInterested` passthrough so Quick Add and Home explore drop the card from the right-click path exactly as they do from the … menu. **The non-obvious bug this surfaced:** `Modal` is plain `fixed` markup, *not* a portal, and most covers sit inside a `<Link>` — rendering the rating dialog in place meant every click inside it bubbled to the anchor and navigated to the album page. The context menu's dialogs are therefore `createPortal`'d to `document.body`. (Portalling `Modal` itself would be the real fix but touches every modal in the app — noted, not done.) Also wired: **artist links** through a new `ArtistLink.tsx` drop-in that keeps a real `<Link>` underneath so middle-click/⌘-click still work natively (album page ×2, song page, search results), **album-page track rows** (one `useContextMenuFor` for the whole list rather than extracting each row into a component), and **mix rows** (Remove from Mix appears only for the owner, resolved per-open). New i18n group `sj.context.{openNewTab,rate,saveToMix,goToArtist,removeFromMix}` in en+ko.
- **#17 add-to-mix → bookmark icon.** Four affordances swapped to lucide `Bookmark`: `FeedCard`'s overflow "Save to Mix" (`ListMusic`), `PostRatingOptions`' add-to-list row (`PlusSquare`), the album page's header action (`ListPlus`), and `AlbumBookmarkButton`'s own "Add to another Mix" row (`ListMusic`) — which was the odd one out, since the button that opened it was already a bookmark. Behavior is untouched; they all still open `MixPickerModal`. **Left alone on purpose:** icons that denote *a mix* rather than *the act of adding to one* — `MixPickerModal`'s per-mix rows, the profile Mixes tab, the album page's "in public mixes" list, and the home empty states. Those stay `ListMusic`.
- **#5 album page: stars → flowers, click-to-rate at the manual step (`components/sj/InlineRatingEditor.tsx`).** The album page was the last rating surface still drawing lucide `Star`s, and its "half star" was a lie — the whole glyph rendered at `opacity-50`, so 3.5 and a dimmed 4 looked identical in the collapsed row. Both are gone. Each mark is now a **`FlowerGlyph` (`/icon-flower.svg`) with a real horizontal clip**: a base copy at `opacity-25` and, layered on top, a second copy inside an `absolute inset-y-0 left-0 overflow-hidden` span whose width is the fill fraction — so 3.5 draws literally half a flower and any tenth in between renders correctly, which matters because #2 made the drag gauge resolve to 0.1. **Click targets are derived from `step`, not hardcoded:** `segments = clamp(round(1 / step), 1, 10)` invisible absolutely-positioned buttons per flower (0.5 → halves, 1.0 → wholes, 0.1 → ten slivers, capped so an exotic step can't spawn hundreds of nodes), each labelled with its own value and each running the existing `clampSnap` before it commits. Hover state moved from `hoverStar: number` to `hoverValue: number` for the same reason — the preview has to be able to show a partial. `onFocus`/`onBlur` mirror the hover so the row previews under keyboard traversal too. Persistence is untouched: a click still routes into `openEditor(v)` / `update(v)`, so the existing debounced auto-save, undo, and remove-rating paths all apply and the album page's single `setRating` remains the only writer.
- **#16 flower rate button on the album cover.** `AlbumRateButton` (the #2 drag gauge) now sits at the bottom-right of the album-page hero cover — `Cover` was wrapped in a `relative` box sized `w-28 h-28 md:w-64 md:h-64` with the button absolutely placed inside it. It's hidden in **instinct** mode, where a 0–5 manual score isn't the page's rating model. **Keeping it in sync with #5's row needed two new optional props on `AlbumRateButton`**, both backwards-compatible so its ten existing call sites are unaffected: `score` (a controlled value the page pushes down, mirrored into internal state by an effect rather than read directly — otherwise the button would lag a drag while waiting on the page's refetch) and `onScoreChange` (fired **after** the write resolves, so the page's `loadRatings()` refetch sees the committed row). Its internal `score` state was renamed `shown` to make the "optimistic display value, not the source of truth" role explicit. `saveModal` was also restructured while adding the callback — the delete branch used to `return` early, which meant a rating removed through the precise modal would have skipped the new notification; it now falls through to a single shared exit.
- **#18 "Go to charts" removed.** Deleted the trailing `<Link href="/charts">` from `TrendingRail` in `app/(main)/page.tsx` and the now-dead `sj.home.viewCharts` key from `lib/i18n/en.ts` + `ko.ts`. `Link` and `t` are both still used elsewhere in that component, so no imports moved. Charts stay reachable from the sidebar.
- **#10 mix page — the bug was a PostgREST embed, not the UI.** Worth recording how it was found, because three plausible hypotheses were wrong first. The reported symptom ("clicking a mix shows nothing") suggested a stuck loading state, a bad id param, or RLS. The schema check ruled out the id: `mix_items.release_id → releases` from the original migration was replaced by `release_group_id → release_groups` in `20260624000001_db_renovation.sql`, and every reader and writer (`MixPickerModal`, `AlbumBookmarkButton`, the album page) agrees on the new column. The `20260708000001` RLS rewrite left the mix policies intact. Live data was healthy: 171 mixes, 14 items, zero null `release_group_id`, and all 14 join to a real release group. What actually broke it only showed up by replaying **the page's exact two queries through PostgREST with the anon key**: the mix query returned **`PGRST201` — "Could not embed because more than one relationship was found for 'mixes' and 'profiles'"**, status **300**, because `mix_likes` (`mix_likes_mix_id_fkey` + `mix_likes_user_id_fkey`) is a second `mixes ↔ profiles` path alongside `mixes_user_id_fkey`. So `.select('*, profiles(username, display_name)')` failed on *every* mix, public or private, and since the page destructured only `{ data }` the failure arrived as `data: null` and hit the `if (!m) { setLoading(false); return }` branch — rendering "Mix not found". The `mix_items` query, the one everybody suspected, was correct and returned both albums with covers and titles; it simply never ran. Fix is one FK hint: `profiles!mixes_user_id_fkey(username, display_name)`. **The same bare embed was live on `album/[id]/page.tsx:272`** for the "in public mixes" section, which had therefore been rendering empty for as long as `mix_likes` has existed — fixed identically, and in scope because it's a surface that links into the mix page. Both fixed queries were re-run against the hosted project and now return rows. Three pieces of hardening went in alongside: (1) **both queries capture `error`**, log it, and render a retryable error state (reusing the existing `sj.common.loadError` + `sj.common.retry` keys, driven by a `reloadKey` state) — dropping `error` is precisely what let a 300 masquerade as an empty result; (2) the fetch is now **gated on `useSession().ready`**, a genuine second bug — every mix but an explicitly public one is owner-only under RLS, so a fetch that raced session restore read as "not found" and, with deps of `[mixId]` only, never retried (home/search/taste already use this gate); (3) a `console.warn` when `mix_items` returns rows but every `release_groups` embed is null, since that state is otherwise pixel-identical to an empty mix. The bare `…` loader became a **#12 skeleton** (title line + meta line + `SkeletonRows`) shaped like the real page. `ProfileView`'s Mixes tab still has its own `…` — left for #12's rollout.
- **#15 artist discography, grouped.** The Albums tab rendered one flat list straight from `get_artist_release_groups` (the prompt's "backed by `/api/artist-albums`" was wrong — that route exists but this page doesn't use it), with a type label built by hand-capitalising the raw `release_group_type`, which meant it was never translated. Replaced with a `<Discography>` component: sections in a fixed order — **Albums · EPs · Singles · Compilations · Soundtracks · Other** — each with a release count, empty sections omitted. Those six come from checking the catalogue rather than guessing: `select release_group_type, count(*) from release_groups` returns exactly single (195,647) / album (139,670) / compilation (82,118) / ep (39,116) / soundtrack (18,389), so **Other** exists only as a catch-all for future or stray values instead of the code minting a section per unknown string. Two `Segmented` pill controls (plain `<button>`s with `aria-pressed`, so keyboard traversal needs no extra handling): group **By type** vs **All** (a single chronological list), and sort **Newest / Oldest / A–Z**. Both are a pure `useMemo` over the `releases` array the tab already holds — the controls never trigger a refetch, and the other tabs keep reading the same unsorted source. One judgement call in the comparator: **releases with no `first_release_date` sort last in both directions** rather than being treated as year 0, because "oldest first" opening with a block of undated rows reads as a broken page. Row markup was extracted verbatim into `ReleaseRow` (AlbumPeek hover bezel, hover bookmark, rate gauge, and score chip all preserved). `typeLabelKey` in `lib/sj/display.ts` gained `compilation` and `soundtrack` cases with matching `sj.type.*` keys in en+ko, so rows now go through i18n — that also fixes the label on the mix page and anywhere else `typeLabelKey` is used. New i18n group `sj.artist.{groupAlbums,groupEps,groupSingles,groupCompilations,groupSoundtracks,groupOther,groupByType,groupAll,sortNewest,sortOldest,sortTitle,oneRelease,nReleases}` in both locales. **⚠ Left alone:** the RPC still caps at `lim: 60`, so a prolific artist's discography is truncated before grouping ever sees it — grouping makes that ceiling more obvious than a flat list did.
- **Verified (pt 2):** `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint`, and `next build` all clean; #10's two corrected queries additionally verified live against the hosted Supabase project. #15 is not browser-verified.
- **#4 Profile > Stats rebuilt (`components/sj/ProfileStats.tsx`, new).** The tab moved out of `ProfileView.tsx` (which shed ~140 lines and now just renders `<ProfileStats items instinctCount />`); `Empty` and `StatCell` stayed behind because the Rated/Mixes tabs and the header still use them. `RatingHistogram.tsx` was **not** touched — despite the name it belongs to the *album* page's community distribution, a different component with a different data shape, so "polish the profile histogram" doesn't mean it. The audit found more than cosmetics. **Three different card treatments in one tab** (`rounded-xl bg-ink/[0.05]` strip → bare `<section>`s → `rounded-[10px] bg-accent/[0.08]` tiles) collapsed into one `StatCard` primitive plus a `KpiTile`; a stray **`max-w-lg`** pinned the dashboard to a narrow column while every sibling tab used the page's `max-w-3xl`. The substantive bug was **two undisclosed denominators**: the headline average ran over `items.map(i => i.score)` — manual scores only — while the histogram directly beneath it also included elo scores once `INSTINCT_REVEAL_THRESHOLD` was met, so the number didn't describe the chart. There is now a single `scoreOf()` applying the reveal rule once, feeding the average, the histogram *and* the new per-artist averages, with the count stated in the card header (`fromNScored`) so the denominator is visible rather than implied. Chart changes follow the `dataviz` skill: bar heights are percentages of the plot box (they were raw px against a fixed `h-24`, so the chart didn't respond to its own container), bars are coloured by #2's **`spectrumRing(bucketScore)`** — chosen over `spectrumColor` at a hand-picked lightness because L .63 is the one variant that holds on both the light and the dark surface without a second value, and because colour here is *redundant* with x-position, so a CVD reader loses nothing; counts became **selective labels** (tallest bucket always, every other on hover, in a fixed-height row so bars don't shift) instead of the anti-pattern of a number on every bar; and a dashed average reference line was added, positioned by `scoreToPct(s) = ((s*2 - 0.5) / 10) * 100` — bucket **centres**, not edges, which is the easy thing to get wrong here. Top artists: the bar track was `bg-transparent` so the bars floated with no reference, and the count column was `w-6` (clipping 3 digits) — now a real `bg-divider/60` track, `w-8` + `formatCount`, top 8 instead of 5, each row also showing that artist's average in the ramp colour, ties broken on average rather than insertion order. The rating-mode tiles became one legended `SplitBar` (2px segment gap per the mark spec, `bg-accent` + `bg-ink/40` so it's accent-plus-neutral and needs no palette validation), and its instinct count is now **elo-only** (`score == null && eloScore != null`) — the old one counted every row with an `elo_score`, including rows that also had a manual score, so the two "segments" overlapped. New low-data states: zero scored ratings renders a sentence instead of ten empty bars, and under 10 adds a `lowData` hint. New i18n `sj.profile.{avgShort,statArtists,fromNScored,noScores,lowData}` en+ko.
- **#9 @username over display name.** Audited every user-row surface before changing anything, and **most of the app was already correct** — `LikersModal`, `TrackLikersModal`, `CommentsModal` and `TrackCommentsModal` all render `@{profileHandle(...)}`, and `notifications.tsx` builds `@${actor.username ?? actor.display_name}`. The prompt's guess that search shows user results is wrong; `search/page.tsx` has no profile rows at all. Exactly two places were inverted, both in `ProfileView.tsx`: the **header**, which rendered `{displayName || \`@${handle}\`}` with the handle demoted to a trailing muted span — i.e. it treated the handle as the *fallback* — and **`FollowListModal`**'s rows, same shape. Both now lead with `@username` (16px / 13.5px semibold) and put the display name on a secondary muted line, omitted entirely when unset. In the modal the secondary line is also suppressed when `username` is missing, since in that case the handle slot is already showing the display name and repeating it would read as a bug. Presentation only — no query, column, or iOS payload touched.
- **Verified (pt 3):** `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint`, and `next build` all clean. Neither #4 nor #9 is browser-verified; #4's histogram colours, the average marker's placement, and the card grid at mobile width are the open visual questions.

**2026-07-16 (Mac) — Liquid Glass pass on Home tab + app icon, rated-state redesign (3 rounds), rating-UX polish, web parity + fixes. All pushed: `806b687` (web parity), `bc5ada8` (iOS batch), `74c729c` (Hangul fix). Session-close open items live in README START HERE + WEB_PARITY.md's new top section.**

- User: "the explore and following buttons at the top need a liquid glass bubble behind them." `feedTabButton` in `HomeView.swift` previously had zero background — active vs. inactive was shown purely by font weight/color (bold+ink vs. regular+muted), no visual chip at all. Added `.glassEffect(.regular, in: Capsule())` (the iOS 26 Liquid Glass API — already used once in the codebase, `ScoreBadge.swift`'s score circle; app's deployment target is iOS 26.0 so no availability check needed) behind whichever tab is active, plus `.matchedGeometryEffect(id: "activeTabBubble", in: tabBubbleNamespace)` on both buttons sharing one id so the capsule visually slides between them on tab switch instead of just cross-fading. Tightened the tab `HStack` spacing 28→4 since each button now carries its own 14pt horizontal capsule padding — the old spacing was tuned for bare text and would've left the bubbles floating too far apart. Verified on-device (simulator, iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5): screenshotted Explore active, then temporarily flipped `activeTab`'s default to `.following` to force-screenshot the other state (same technique as the 2026-07-15 quest-timeline verification below), confirmed the bubble renders correctly under both labels, then reverted the temporary default before considering the change done. **Scope note:** `RankingsView.swift`'s Albums/Songs toggle carries an explicit comment ("same style as Home Explore/Following") but was left untouched per the user's scope instructions (only Home was asked for) — now visually inconsistent with Home until/unless the user asks for parity there too.
- **Follow-up, same session:** user asked for the same glass treatment on the bell/notifications button (added, same `.glassEffect(.regular, in: Circle())` pattern as `ScoreBadge`), plus flagged "a cutoff at the top of the screen" — the status bar zone (time/wifi/battery) was flat opaque `Color.sjCream` with a hard edge, not the translucent/blur-through look Liquid Glass calls for. Root cause: `floatingHeader` had no background at all, and `feedContent`'s `ScrollView` fully respected the safe area, so nothing ever scrolled up far enough to be visible behind the status bar even in principle. **First attempt was wrong and caught before shipping:** tried `.safeAreaInset(edge: .top) { floatingHeader }` assuming it would let scrolled content flow underneath the header like Apple's own bars — it doesn't; it only reserves layout space, and an on-device screenshot showed the previous card had simply vanished off-screen rather than peeking through blurred. Correct fix: `feedContent.ignoresSafeArea(edges: .top)` (so the `ScrollView`'s own bounds extend to the physical screen top), `floatingHeader.background(.ultraThinMaterial, ignoresSafeAreaEdges: .top)` (extends the glass up through the status bar), and a `topSafeAreaInset` `@State` captured once via a `GeometryReader` placed in `.background` *outside* the ignoring chain (so it still sees the real device inset) — used to pad both the header's top and the feed's `contentMargins` so the resting layout is pixel-identical to before on any device, no hardcoded constant. Verified with a temporary `proxy.scrollTo(posts[1].id)` forced on `.onAppear` (reverted immediately after screenshotting): cropped into the status-bar strip and confirmed the scrolled-away card's like/comment row is now visible, blurred, through the glass — not just a static tinted rectangle. Iterated through 3 build+install+screenshot rounds on the same simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5) to catch the `safeAreaInset` dead end before landing on the working version.
- **Second follow-up, same session:** user pushed back that the blur "is not gradual and the blurring region is too wide... too strong as well," and asked if Apple has an official way to do this. Researched it properly (WebSearch + WebFetch on Apple docs/dev-blog coverage): yes — iOS 26's `scrollEdgeEffectStyle(_:for:)` gives `ScrollView`/`List`/`Form` an automatic graduated blur/dim (`.automatic`/`.soft`/`.hard`) for exactly this scenario. Tried it (`.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.soft, for: .top)` on the feed's `ScrollView`, removed the manual `ultraThinMaterial` block) and verified on-device: **zero effect** — a card scrolled behind the header rendered fully sharp, no dim at all. Concluded (and told the user) that the automatic effect only engages behind real native system chrome (toolbar/tab bar), not a hand-built overlay header like this one — so there's no one-line official fix available here. Fell back to the standard manual technique: `.ultraThinMaterial` masked by a top-to-bottom `LinearGradient` (opaque at 0%, half-opacity at 35%, fully clear by 75%) instead of a flat block, so it tapers. Verified via the same temporary forced-scroll-then-screenshot technique, cropped and zoomed into the status-bar strip to confirm the taper. Left it open whether the exact fade distance/opacity needs further tuning — genuinely subjective, asked the user to react to the result rather than guessing further.
- **Third follow-up, same session — "can we change our app logo to be compatible with liquid glass?" — went wrong, fully reverted, lesson recorded:** while scoping Icon Composer (Apple's official GUI tool for the layered `.icon` Liquid Glass format, confirmed installed at `/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Applications/Icon Composer.app`), misdiagnosed the brand logo as a *corrupted* asset: `AppIcon.png`/`AppIcon-dark.png`, all 7 `AlternateIcons/*.png`, and `logo-flower.svg` (the splash/auth flower, used via `Image("logo-flower")` in `AuthView`/`MainTabView`/`ShareCardView`/`ProfileView`) all contain a CMYK-halftone-dotted flower raster, which read as color-separation damage — especially next to `icon-flower.imageset/icon-flower.svg`, a clean single-path vector of a similar flower. Asked the user, got approval for a rebuild (but the approval was based on my "it's corrupted" framing), regenerated everything as a flat `sjBlue` flower via a Python/PIL pipeline, verified on-device... and the user immediately corrected: **the halftone dotted texture IS the intentional logo design, not corruption.** Reverted every asset via `git checkout` (verified `git status` — only `HomeView.swift`/`SearchView.swift` remain modified), deleted the `LiquidGlassIconLayers/` prep folder built on the wrong premise. **Then re-prepped the handoff correctly:** the base64 PNG embedded in `logo-flower.svg` turned out to be the original flower artwork *with real alpha* (729×754 RGBA, 80% transparent background, flower opaque) — extracted it byte-for-byte (no reprocessing) into `apps/ios/LiquidGlassIconLayers/foreground-flower-original.png` + a README with the Icon Composer steps (native background picker `#F5F0E8`/`#1A1A1A`, halftone flower as foreground layer at ~46% canvas, glass tuning by eye, save `AppIcon.icon` → drag into Xcode). Also saved a persistent memory (`sillajuku-halftone-logo-intentional`) so no future session repeats the misdiagnosis.
- **Fourth follow-up — Liquid Glass icon actually shipped:** user asked which Icon Composer to download from Apple's More Downloads page — answer: none; Xcode 26.6 already bundles Icon Composer 1.6 (checked its Info.plist: `CFBundleShortVersionString = 1.6`), which is the current stable, and the "Icon Composer 2 beta" track pairs with Xcode 27 betas (its `.icon` output may not parse in stable Xcode). User ran the GUI session and saved `LiquidGlassIconLayers/appicon.icon` (inspected: white `extended-gray` fill, flower layer with `glass: true`, `darken` blend for dark appearance, 0.9 opacity, neutral shadow, translucency 0.5). Wiring it in was one `cp -R` to `apps/ios/sillajuku/AppIcon.icon`: the capital name matches `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME = AppIcon`, the file lands inside the project's `PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup` (objectVersion 77) so no pbxproj edit, and Xcode 26 prefers a same-named `.icon` over the `.appiconset` (which stays as fallback). Verified three ways: build clean; `xcrun assetutil --info` on the built `Assets.car` shows `IconImageStack`/`IconGroup`/the `foreground-flower-original` layer (i.e. the layered icon compiled in, not the old flat one); springboard screenshots in light **and** dark (`xcrun simctl ui <udid> appearance dark` — first dark screenshot came back all black, mid-transition; retake after `sleep 4` worked). Observed + flagged, not changed: the new tile is white (not the old cream `#F5F0E8`) and stays white in dark mode since the user set no dark fill override — their design; and the 7 alternate icons remain flat PNGs (would need per-variant Icon Composer sessions to glass them). Goes out with the next App Store build.
- **Fifth follow-up — "did you test all 7 icons?" → full alternate-icon runtime test.** First answered honestly (no — static checks only: all 14 bundle PNGs pixel-compared to source after `pngcrush -revert-iphone-optimizations`, since Xcode's CopyPNGFile makes byte-compares useless; all 7 `CFBundleAlternateIcons` entries verified in the built Info.plist) and suggested the user tap through Settings — which failed because **the icon picker is invite-gated**: `SettingsView.swift:84` only renders it at `verifiedInviteCount >= 5` (from `referrals` where `verified_at` is set), documented in a comment I'd read but failed to connect. Then tested it properly without any GUI: temporary `onAppear` hook in `sillajukuApp.swift` reading a `SJ_TEST_ICON` env var → `setAlternateIconName` after 2s; driven per-icon from the terminal via `SIMCTL_CHILD_SJ_TEST_ICON=<name> xcrun simctl launch` (the `SIMCTL_CHILD_` prefix is how env vars reach a simulator app), launch → sleep 5 → terminate → springboard screenshot, for all 7 alternates + `default`. One build for the hook, 8 launch cycles, one build to revert it. **Result: all pass** — Sand/Blush/PowderBlue/Lavender/Mint/Terracotta/Black each show the correct tile color with the halftone flower, and switching back to default correctly restores the `.icon`-based Liquid Glass primary (the one genuinely new code path, since "default" no longer means the flat appiconset). **2026-07-15 (Mac) — quest timeline connector-line bug (2 iterations) + Vercel Fluid CPU root-cause:**

- **Quest timeline connector line.** User: a completed quest's circle correctly turns blue with a checkmark, but the connecting line below it was also turning blue "regardless of the completion of nearby items" — should only be blue if unbroken back to the first item. First attempt (`9ec41fd`) computed `chainDone[i] = items[0...i] all done` and colored the line below item i by `chainDone[i]` — looked right in isolation, but the user sent a real on-device screenshot showing it was still wrong: Set Profile Picture through Connect Phone Number (6 items) all done, Invite a Friend not done, and the line leading into Invite a Friend was blue anyway. Root cause: that line connects item i to item i+1, so it needs the chain unbroken *through i+1*, not just through i — an off-by-one, not a wrong concept. Fixed (`ef76615`) by indexing `chainDone[index + 1]` for the line below each item. Verified both the bug and the fix visually, not just by re-reading code: temporarily forced `MainTabView`'s default tab and `ProfileView`'s `showQuestChecklist` to launch straight into the exact same quest sheet, built + installed via `xcrun simctl`, screenshotted, confirmed the line color, then reverted both overrides before committing (plus reverted an unrelated `Localizable.xcstrings` whitespace-only reformat that a custom `-derivedDataPath` build triggered as a side effect).
- **Vercel Fluid Active CPU at 75%.** User pasted the Vercel usage-alert email, asked where the CPU was going and whether it's one-time or ongoing. No Vercel API/CLI access from this machine, so investigated at the code level instead of guessing: `/api/recommendations` and `/api/taste/profile` do real in-Node CPU work (cosine similarity, clustering — a deliberate CPU-for-DB-load tradeoff from the 2026-07-12 taste-vector rebuild, since Supabase is on a Micro instance), both routes have server-side caches (120s / 60s), and a 449KB `genre-embeddings.json` gets re-parsed on every cold start of either route. Checked client call sites for cache-defeating patterns and found one concrete bug: the Taste page called `/api/taste/profile?refresh=1` unconditionally, on every single page load — `refresh=1` skips the route's own `cacheGet`, so the cache never once helped, unlike the sibling `/api/discovery`/`/api/recommendations` calls (built the same day, 2026-07-12) which correctly omit it. `git blame` traced it to the original v2 rebuild commit with nothing explaining it as deliberate. Answered the user's actual question honestly: this is ongoing, not a blip — the taste-vector system is 3 days old and permanent, not a backfill, so cost scales with usage. Fixed the concrete bug (`76bab2b`, removed `?refresh=1`) with the user's go-ahead, but was explicit that this reduces the trajectory rather than eliminates the cost, and that Vercel dashboard confirmation is still needed (no access from here) before deciding if a TTL widen or Pro upgrade is also warranted.
- **iOS Add tab — "Compilation" type badge wrapping to two lines.** User reported the small blue type-chip on Discovery album cards (`DiscoveryAlbumCard` in `SearchView.swift`) broke onto two lines for longer type names. Root cause: the chip's `Text(release.typeLabel)` had no `lineLimit`, and its containing `HStack` sits in a fixed 128pt-wide column alongside the artist name — under width pressure the chip text wrapped instead of truncating. Directly relevant now that the 2026-07-14 `search_release_groups` migration (this session's ide selection) stopped filtering out compilations/soundtracks, so "Compilation" shows up in Add-tab results far more than before. Fixed by adding `.lineLimit(1)` to the chip `Text` — one line, ellipsis-truncates only in extreme cases, no change to `typeLabel` itself (still used unabbreviated elsewhere, e.g. `AlbumDetailView`).

**2026-07-16 (Windows) — iTunes discography backfill lane + closing the KR artist-discovery gap (11,750 queued):**

Two related catalog-completeness problems, both traced to root cause before building. User's governing constraint throughout (as with the recency lane): multi-source ingest must be duplicate-safe and accuracy-first, "extra careful."

- **Root-caused the P-Type gap (7 releases here vs 33 on YouTube Music).** Confirmed it's a genuine **MusicBrainz coverage gap**, not a pipeline bug: MB has only 8 release-groups for P-Type (7 own + 1 guest feature, which `shouldIngestRG` correctly drops); our DB matched exactly. iTunes has ~35, incl. real albums MB lacks (Soulfire 2006, Hardboiled Café 2022, THIS IS NOT AN ALBUM 2022). The recency lane can't reach these — it's recency-scoped; nothing backfilled *old* MB-missing releases from streaming.
- **Built the backfill lane** (`discover-itunes-backfill.ts`, `discover:backfill[:ingest]`, `test:backfill`) — sibling of the recency lane (same iTunes writers + `source='itunes'`/`mb_release_group_id` NULL provenance, so `reconcile:itunes` still guards MB-later dups) but NOT recency-scoped. Reaches back over the whole iTunes discography with **six layered guards** on top of the recency gate, each "missing > wrong": (1) **artist-identity confirmation** — a whole-catalog sweep is catastrophically exposed to resolving the *wrong* same-named artist (there are two "P-Type"s on iTunes), so it requires ≥2 of our existing titles to appear in the resolved discography or it aborts and ingests nothing; (2) primary-artist-only + feat-of-us title heuristic; (3) stronger dedup key (`backfillKey` also strips iTunes release-TYPE suffixes "… - Single"/"… - The 3rd Mini Album" so cross-source titles match); (4) within-iTunes dedup ("Soulfire" vs "Soulfire - Single" → keep the fuller/cleaner/earlier); (5) near-date-but-different-title → SUSPECT, held for review, never auto-ingested (the romanized-vs-Hangul same-release trap); (6) albums/EPs only by default (`--include-singles` to widen). Report-only default; `--ingest` writes; `--ingest-suspects` on top.
- **Extensive dry-run validation** (`test-itunes-backfill.ts`) across a 24-KR-artist sample surfaced real issues, all fixed before any live write: a **tie-break bug** (within-iTunes dedup kept the mislabeled "- Single" over the clean title); a **policy gap** (backfill ingested live albums/remix EPs the MB filter excludes → added `isNonCore` live/remix detection); and a **noise leak found at scale** during the live sweep (Ja Mezz's "Only God Can Stop Me [Sped Up Pack]" — the iTunes noise filter only drops sped-up/karaoke at ≤3 tracks → added `NOISE_RE` for sped-up/slowed/karaoke/off-vocal/MR/inst, high-precision so "Mr. Brightside"/legit instrumental beat albums aren't caught; 15 unit cases pass). Cleaned up the one noise row already written.
- **Recall fix (user: "we absolutely need 2NE1 and equivalently popular artists").** ~40% of the sample was "unresolved" — root cause: `searchAlbum` used `name_native ?? name` in the term, so Latin-branded acts with a Hangul `name_native` (2NE1→"투애니원", nafla→"나플라") never matched. Added `searchArtist` (entity=musicArtist) as the primary candidate source + try both name forms; still gated by the unchanged overlap check. Same 24-sample: confirmed resolution 11→14, unresolved 10→4; 2NE1/nafla/Yankie now resolve; **safety preserved** — the two wrong-artist canaries (XXX 1/3, 강영현 0/6) still abort.
- **Resumable, self-throttling sweep.** User asked why batch — answer: only iTunes IP-limits, not correctness. Made the CLI sweep the whole `country` set from one command via a persisted per-artist cursor (`backfill-sweep-state.json`), backing off 20m on `ItunesBlockedError` and resuming rather than dying. (Fixed an empty-cursor `.gt('id','')` invalid-uuid bug — same latent issue exists in the recency lane's cursor.) **P-Type live-ingest verified end-to-end:** 7→10 RGs, the 3 correct releases, `source='itunes'`/mbid NULL, no dup groups, tracks+canonical correct, `reconcile:itunes` reports them "no MB match yet" (makes no changes). Full KR sweep (866 artists) is running in the user's terminal.

Reversible, logged, no catalog-data surface. **Takes effect on next pipeline restart.** Startup `resetStale` unchanged (clean-shutdown recovery ≠ a hang, no penalty). **2026-07-13 (Windows) — web infinite-loading root cause: auth-lock deadlock in `SessionContext` (NOT a cache problem):**

User report: web content "takes infinite time to load; on hard refresh it sometimes works but breaks again next load." Diagnosed as a Supabase auth-lock **deadlock**, not caching.

- **Mechanism.** The whole app gates on `useSession().ready`; the home feed's `load()` only runs `if (ready)` and `loading` starts `true`, so "infinite skeleton" ⟺ `ready` never flips true. `ready` was being set *inside* the `onAuthStateChange` callback, **after** `await loadProfile(uid)` (a `supabase.from('profiles')` query). Confirmed `@supabase/auth-js` **2.103.2** uses `navigatorLock` (`navigator.locks`) by default: the callback fires while auth-js holds the session-token lock, and the awaited query tries to re-acquire the same lock → it queues behind the callback that's awaiting it → deadlock → the `await` never resolves → `setReady(true)` never runs → app stuck on the loading skeleton. This is the documented "don't await Supabase calls inside `onAuthStateChange`" footgun.
- **Why it was intermittent.** Two paths raced on load — `getSession().then()` and `onAuthStateChange`'s `INITIAL_SESSION` — both fetching the profile and setting `ready`. Whether the callback's inner query deadlocked depended on lock-acquisition timing between them, so it was nondeterministic (a sticky cache bug would be consistent — the tell that it wasn't caching). The server-side caching layer (`/api/feed`, Redis/CDN) never applied here: the hang is in the client auth bootstrap, *before* `load()` (and any cached route) is ever called.
- **Fix** (`components/sj/SessionContext.tsx`, no migration, web-only): the `onAuthStateChange` callback is now synchronous and only does `setUserId(session?.user?.id ?? null)` — no awaited Supabase call inside the lock. A **separate** effect keyed on `userId` fetches the profile off the lock and flips `ready` once it settles (signed-out → immediate). This also removes the redundant `getSession()` + `onAuthStateChange` double-fetch (`INITIAL_SESSION` delivers the initial session on subscribe). `ready` still waits for the profile before the onboarding-redirect effect can act, so no signed-in user is bounced to `/onboarding` against a not-yet-loaded profile. `tsc` clean (source-side; the only `tsc` errors are pre-existing stale `.next/types` route stubs).
- **Shipped:** pushed to `main` (auto-deploys via Vercel). The same deadlock shape does not exist elsewhere (grep: `onAuthStateChange` is only registered here).

Diagnosed by comparing against why the *album* RPC never had this problem: `recordings` (3.16M rows) has an index on `primary_artist_id` but **none on `artist_display`**, so `WHERE r.artist_display = ANY(p_artist_names)` forced a full sequential scan of the entire table before the 3-way join and `DISTINCT ON` sort could even start. `release_groups` (the album table) has an equivalent trigram index (`idx_release_groups_display_trgm`) and is ~10× smaller — that's why the album-side RPC was fine without one. Fixed with a single `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_recordings_artist_display` (migration `20260712000011`, applied as its own SQL-editor statement since `CONCURRENTLY` can't run inside a transaction block). Verified live: 0.67s → 0.33s on repeat calls (previously 57014 every time), and confirmed already-rated tracks (checked against the test account's real `track_ratings` rows for E SENS) are correctly excluded.

1. **"Star icons are inconsistent with the rest of the app — maybe make them the flower icon trace."** Checked first: `HalfStarRow`'s SF Symbol `"star"` turned out to be the *only* star-based control anywhere in the app — `ScoreBadge` and `ManualRatingSheet` both use the `icon-flower` mark (a slider for the latter, no stars at all). Swapped to the same `icon-flower` asset, template-rendered and outlined in `sjBorder`, same half-tap gesture logic.
2. **"Albums: there are too few/narrow suggestions — only 2 artists and 15 albums."** Checked the real data before assuming it was a code bug: the test account's `profiles.spotify_artists`/`spotify_recently_played` already had **7** distinct artists (Fred again.., Simon Dominic, dress, The Black Skirts, YANGHONGWON, Masta Wu, Skepta) — not 2 — so the report pointed at something else. Found a real bug: `QuickAddViewModel.init`'s own doc comment claimed the seed list included "the user's own highly-rated artist history," but `DiscoveryViewModel` never actually exposed that data anywhere — only the Spotify/Apple Music arrays were wired in, so the comment was aspirational, not accurate. Added `DiscoveryViewModel.ratedArtists` (score ≥3.5, populated in the existing `loadPersonalized()` pass, no new query) and wired it into `QuickAddViewModel`'s seed list. Confirmed against the live `ratings` table before calling it fixed: the account has real ≥3.5-equivalent (post-Elo-conversion) ratings for NewJeans, ATEEZ, E SENS, and Lauryn Hill — none of them in the Spotify set — exactly the artists the fix now surfaces.
3. **"Songs: the suggestion algorithm is clearly not sophisticated enough — they just list entire tracklists of albums."** Confirmed by reading the RPC: no per-album cap existed, so a page was literally one artist's entire unrated discography in album-prestige order (the live test earlier in the session had already shown this — 4 tracks from one album, then querying wider showed a single album could fill the entire page). Capped at 4 tracks/album via `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY release_group_id ORDER BY position)` (migration `20260713000000`), mirroring the exact cap-per-artist pattern `loadPersonalized()`/`loadTasteAlbums()` already use on the album side for the same flooding problem. No per-song popularity signal exists in the schema, so "first 4 tracks in tracklist order" is the available proxy, not a claim of picking an artist's most popular songs — documented as such in the migration. Verified live: the same 4-artist query that previously returned 20 tracks all from one Fred again.. album now spans 17 different releases, max 4 tracks from any one album, still fast (0.51s).

**Profile-page subtab swipe fixed (own profile) + added (other people's profile) — both silently broken/missing, found by direct comparison against the one screen that already worked.** User reported swiping felt insensitive and sometimes opened whatever row was under the finger instead of switching tabs, on **both** "my profile" and "someone else's profile." Comparing `ArtistPageView` (works fine, plain `TabView(.page)`) against `ProfileView` (doesn't) found the real cause: `ProfileView`'s hero scrolls away with the content in one shared vertical `ScrollView`, so it can't use native horizontal paging at all (nesting a `TabView.page` inside a `ScrollView` fights it for the gesture) — it had a hand-rolled `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 15)` instead, with a distance-only completion rule (33% of screen width, no velocity factored in at all). A real flick swipe often travels well under either threshold — real intent, small total finger movement — so the gesture frequently never recognized, and the touch fell straight through to whatever `NavigationLink` (album cover, mix row) sat underneath: one root cause explaining both complaints at once. Separately, `UserProfileView` (other people's profile) turned out to have **no swipe gesture whatsoever** — tab switching there was tap-only on the icon row; "not working well" there actually meant "doesn't exist."

Extracted the fix into a new shared `Components/SwipeableTabPager.swift` (generic over any `Hashable & CaseIterable` tab enum) rather than fixing it once and duplicating the same bug surface a second time: `minimumDistance` lowered 15→10 so a real swipe claims the gesture sooner; `onEnded` now honors a fast flick via `value.velocity` even when the total drag distance falls short of the (also lowered, 25%) page-turn threshold, matching how native paging already feels forgiving of short fast flicks; and the page content gets `.allowsHitTesting(false)` for the duration of an active drag as defense-in-depth alongside `.highPriorityGesture`, since `NavigationLink`'s own tap recognizer has a known history of not reliably yielding to a sibling gesture. Wired into `ProfileView` (replacing its inline ~90-line copy) and `UserProfileView` (net new — required adding the same hero-height/min-height-floor plumbing `ProfileView` already had, since the pager didn't exist there at all before). One Swift-specific snag: a `PreferenceKey` nested inside the generic `SwipeableTabPager` struct failed to compile ("static stored properties not supported in generic types") — moved it to a top-level private type instead. Build succeeds; interactive on-device re-verification is left to the user (see the aside directly below for why).

**Aside — a GUI-automation near-miss, self-corrected mid-session.** Attempting to drive the Simulator via coordinate-click AppleScript (to verify the song RPC fix visually, then again to test the swipe fix) ran into repeated window-state ambiguity (multiple booted devices, Simulator's `-SessionOnLaunch NO` flag meaning no window opens automatically, windows silently closing after menu actions). Chasing the exact window position at one point fell back to `screencapture -x` for a full-desktop screenshot — which captured unrelated live windows already open on the user's Mac, including what looked like a real-money poker session. Recognized this immediately as a privacy problem (capturing content that has nothing to do with the task and wasn't offered), deleted the screenshot, and abandoned desktop-level GUI automation for the rest of the session in favor of backend-only (REST/RPC) verification, asking the user to do the remaining interactive spot-checks (rating a song, confirming the swipe feel) themselves. Later in the session, the user confirmed a *legitimate* pre-existing Simulator window was already open and just needed the right `File → Open Simulator → <device>` menu path rather than a new boot — worth knowing before assuming a window doesn't exist next time.

**Disk-usage question answered — investigation only, no code change, at the user's explicit request.** User asked whether to stop the ingestion pipeline given Supabase was at 6GB/8GB (75%) disk. Investigated with real numbers instead of guessing: the existing `apps/web/scripts/measure-storage.ts` estimator is stale against the post-June-renovation schema (still checks `releases.embedding`/`releases.tracklist`, which moved to `release_groups`/`release_tracks` — it reported 0 for both, which is simply wrong) and was set aside in favor of asking the user to run real `pg_total_relation_size`/`pg_stat_user_indexes`/`pg_stat_user_tables` queries in the SQL editor (read-only, same round-trip pattern already established for migrations this session). Findings: **`release_groups` alone is 3.59GB, of which only 125MB is actual table data** — 1.89GB is `idx_release_groups_embedding_hnsw` (the vector-search index) and 1.29GB is TOAST (the raw 1024-dim embedding vectors themselves, ~4KB/row). So **roughly half the entire database's disk usage is the semantic-search embeddings feature**, not ingestion volume — genuinely pipeline-driven tables (`recordings` 1.2GB + `release_tracks` 0.88GB + `releases` 0.3GB) total only ~2.4GB combined. Dead-tuple/autovacuum stats ruled out reclaimable bloat as the explanation (release_groups ~6% dead, recordings ~0.07%, release_tracks 0%, all with recent autovacuum runs). **Recommendation given (not acted on — the user's call to make):** don't stop the pipeline outright — Supabase Pro typically autoscales disk past the included 8GB rather than going read-only the way Free tier does (flagged as worth confirming is actually enabled on this project, not asserted as fact), and the `ingest` lane was nearly drained anyway. Did suggest pausing the `discover` lane specifically, since it still had ~22k candidate artists queued and is the one lever still actively committing to *new* growth, while `ingest`/`freshness`/`gapfill` finish what's already queued.

**2026-07-11/12 (Windows) — MusicBrainz-gap recovery (we can't rely 100% on MB), multi-source duplicate safety, demand-signal hardening, and the Korean Hangul-name backfill:**

Triggered by "why don't we have System Seoul?" — a real artist on Deezer (25 fans, 2 albums) but not in MusicBrainz, so the MB-only pipeline could never collect it.

- **MB-gap strategy, 3 tiers (Deezer as the non-MB source).** (1) **On-demand:** `scripts/seed-deezer-artist.ts` (`npm run seed:deezer-artist -- --name "X" --write`) — added System Seoul. (2) **Demand-driven:** the pipeline's `tryMisses` now recovers an artist from Deezer when a user search finds nothing in MB (`MISS_DEEZER_FALLBACK`, default on). (3) **Backlog drain** was investigated via dry-run and **declined** — the skipped backlog is mostly generic names + VA/classical artists already in MB (Mozart 432 albums), so a blind drain would pollute; added a ≤100-album cap so no Deezer path can clog on VA-tier.
- **Multi-source duplicate safety (the critical prerequisite the user flagged).** The Deezer path was a one-shot and had TWO duplicate bugs once wired into repeated calls: (a) **cross-source** — it only checked for an existing Deezer link, never MusicBrainz, so an MB artist whose name-resolve failed got a second row (5 already live: Stromae, Damso, Hamza, Atif Aslam, Stereo MC's); (b) **within-source** — Deezer release_groups insert with random UUIDs and no dedup key, so re-ingest duplicated every album. Fixed: `existingCatalogArtist()` (search_artists exact name/native/alias check → skip, return -1) + seed the release-group seen-set with the artist's existing albums. Cleaned the 5 live dupes (252 RGs, 0 ratings → FK-safe atomic delete). Verified: re-seeding Stromae skips, re-seeding System Seoul adds 0. Confirmed 0 cross-source dupes after the catalog grew to 48k artists.
- **Q1 — demand-signal hardening (real gap vs wrong/typo search).** iOS now logs a `search_miss` when a query returns nothing (was web-only → the primary surface was blind; added the missing `search_misses` INSERT policy `20260711000000`). The Deezer miss-fallback fires only on a genuine repeated gap: `db_count=0` (catalog truly returned nothing, not a variant we have) AND `>= MISS_MIN_DEMAND` (2) occurrences AND an exact Deezer name match.
- **Q2 — source-agnostic popularity.** `discover-popularity.ts` no longer drops charting artists MB lacks — it recovers them from Deezer, famous-first (`--deezer-limit`, `--no-deezer`). Collection priority is now popularity, not source (per user: anti-commercial taste ≠ missing artists people actually search). Safe because of the dedup/cap/idempotency guards above.
- **Korean Hangul-name backfill (FOR WINDOWS #5).** KR artists with no Hangul anywhere are unfindable by Korean search. True gap: **56** (not the 352 name_native-null headline). `scripts/backfill-korean-native-names.ts` (`npm run backfill:korean-names`). **Source pivot MB→Wikipedia** (MB had no Hangul aliases for these — verified SHINHWA/EVERGLOW/CRAVITY); Korean Wikipedia `ko`-langlink via `opensearch` (case-tolerant — full-text search returned noise + missed stylized ALL-CAPS). 3 guards (title-exact · Korean-musician category · Hangul). **Written to `name_phonetic_ko` not `name_native`** (name_native drives display — would wrongly show 에버글로우 for Everglow; phonetic_ko is search-only, still matched by search_artists). Filled 6 (SHINHWA→신화, EVERGLOW→에버글로우, Seori→서리, MYNAME, SUPER JUNIOR-K.R.Y., Asian Glow), verified live. The other 50 correctly stay null (brand/stylized names or Deezer-only like System Seoul, genuinely absent from Wikipedia).
- **⚑ Operational:** the pipeline changes (cross-source guard, tier-2 miss fallback, Q1 gates) take effect on the **next pipeline restart**; `discover-popularity` should run during a pipeline pause (its MB-resolve step contends with the ingest worker); the iOS miss-logging + the earlier romanization/edition matching need a **Mac build**.
